# Submit product suggestions in Ideas Portal

> **Section:** Reltio > What’s in the box? > What's in the box at a glance > Technical assistance at a glance > Technical assistance operations


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/reltio/whats-in-the-box/whats-in-the-box-at-a-glance/technical-assistance-at-a-glance/technical-assistance-operations/submit-product-suggestions-in-ideas-portal?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs

**Keywords:** Reltio Ideas Portal, Ideas Portl, Submit an idea, suggest improvements, suggest enhancements, share an idea, request an enhancement, enhancement request, new feature request


Learn about the Reltio Ideas Portal, where you can share ideas with Reltio and other Reltio users

Have a great idea to improve the Reltio Context Intelligence Platform ? We'd love to hear it!

## Be a Reltio roadmap influencer

Influence the Reltio product roadmap by providing input on new features or enhancements you would like to see in the Reltio Context Intelligence Platform. Share your product improvement suggestions directly with the Reltio product team as well as other users in the **Reltio Ideas Portal**. Comment and vote on other users' ideas. Track the progress of submitted ideas.

*Image: ideasportal-process.png*

Reltio looks at these ideas for future product features, so they are not considered time critical. To report a product bug or critical issue, raise a ticket with Reltio Support (for more information, see topic [Get help in Support Portal](https://docs.reltio.com/en/reltio/whats-in-the-box/whats-in-the-box-at-a-glance/technical-assistance-at-a-glance/technical-assistance-operations/get-help-in-support-portal?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs)).

OK, so you've got a hot idea and want to know what's your best shot for getting it prioritized? Here are some top tips and some cold drips to consider when submitting or supporting a product improvement idea.

| Most likely to succeed | Least likely to succeed |
| --- | --- |
| -     Solve for a broad use case reported by many customers -     Have a large business impact on a broad range of customers -     Align with the core competency of the product -     Create a competitive advantage for an industry or customer segment | -     Have a narrow focus for a solution to a problem -     Are specific to a niche market -     Create a one-off solution or solve a problem that is not seen often -     Are nice-to-have but have no business value -     Conflict with the core competency of the product |

If an idea garners votes from five or more companies, Reltio product managers will dig deeper into the idea and determine the best way to address the request. Reltio product managers archive ideas that have been in either of the following statuses for more than one year: Open with fewer than five votes or Future Consideration. In the event the roadmap scope changes to cover an archived idea, Reltio will update the idea's status. In fact, any time we update the status of an idea, we add a comment to help you keep track of its progress.

We encourage you to use the Community to engage with fellow Reltio customers to get support (votes!) for your idea. For more information, see topic [Collaborate and engage in Community](https://docs.reltio.com/en/reltio/whats-in-the-box/whats-in-the-box-at-a-glance/technical-assistance-at-a-glance/technical-assistance-operations/collaborate-and-engage-in-community?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).

# Support Portal designated contacts

> **Section:** Reltio > What’s in the box? > What's in the box at a glance > Technical assistance at a glance > Technical assistance operations > Get help in Support Portal


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/reltio/whats-in-the-box/whats-in-the-box-at-a-glance/technical-assistance-at-a-glance/technical-assistance-operations/get-help-in-support-portal/support-portal-designated-contacts?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs


Learn about designated contacts on the Support portal.

The Reltio Support portal accepts ticket submissions only from Designated Contacts within your organization. The Reltio support plan you licensed entitles you to a maximum number of named Designated Contacts, shown below. Review your license agreement to determine the number of Designated Contacts to which you're entitled. For details on our offerings, see [Support Level Agreement and Support Policy](https://www.reltio.com/sla-and-support-policy/).

| Support Plan | Number of Named, Designated Contacts per production tenant |
| --- | --- |
| Standard | 4 |
| Premier | 8 |
| Concierge | 12 |

In order to successfully submit a support ticket, a Designated Contact **must also be set up as a tenant user**, which you should plan to do via the [User Management](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/console/security-applications/user-management-at-a-glance/managing-user-accounts/creating-a-new-user-account?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs) function within the Reltio Console.

As mentioned in the [Quick Start Guide](https://docs.reltio.com/en/objectives/administer-system/system-administration-at-a-glance/system-administration-operation/quick-start-guide?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs), the person set up as the initial Customer Admin for your account is also set up as the first Designated Contact Administrator in our support site.

This means they have the ability to submit tickets immediately. Typically, as the Designated Contact Administrator, you determine other users who should additionally be named as contacts within your organization and then [Configure designated contacts in the Support Portal](https://docs.reltio.com/en/reltio/whats-in-the-box/whats-in-the-box-at-a-glance/technical-assistance-at-a-glance/technical-assistance-operations/get-help-in-support-portal/support-portal-designated-contacts/configure-designated-contacts-in-the-support-portal?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs). There's no need to configure the full set of 4, 8, or 12 Designated Contacts per your entitlement on day one but do plan and use the **Designated Contact Application** to manage those contacts. Anyone on your team who’s signed into the Support portal can use the application to view the list of all current Designated Contacts within your organization. However, only Designated Contact Administrators can edit the list of Designated Contacts.

It's generally a good idea to have one or two other Designated Contacts from the development and configuration team who can file tickets. Lastly, if you're working with an SI partner that is doing Reltio configuration or integration work for you, you may want to have persons from the partner organization named as Designated Contacts.

> **Important:** All persons named as Designated Contacts should use your organization's email domain within their email address, even if they work for a partner organization, for proper association with your account and your tenants.

Designated Contacts automatically receive notifications for all updates related to their submitted tickets. As a Designated Contact Admin, you may give them the privilege to view tickets opened by others in your organization.

Lastly, you can CC others on a ticket. Anyone CC'd will receive all updates via email in a read-only format. If a CC'd person is also a Designated Contact, they can add updates to the ticket by selecting the ticket link and accessing it through the Support Portal.

Learn how to get technical assistance in Reltio Support Portal.

You can use the Reltio Support Portal to explore support resources, interact with Sage (our AI Assistant), and submit a request for help or information.

## Support Portal Roles and Actions

The Support Portal customizes the available actions based on your assigned role. The following table lists the actions available to each role in the Support Portal.

| Actions | Regular User | Designated Contact | Designated Contact Admin |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Submit a Support Request | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ (Only if the admin is also a Designated contact) |
| Manage Designated Contacts list | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
| Access the Chatbot | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |

> **Note:** To know how to configure designated contacts in the Support portal, see [Configure designated contacts in the Support Portal](https://docs.reltio.com/en/reltio/whats-in-the-box/whats-in-the-box-at-a-glance/technical-assistance-at-a-glance/technical-assistance-operations/get-help-in-support-portal/support-portal-designated-contacts/configure-designated-contacts-in-the-support-portal?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).

## Explore our support resources

The following resources are available in the Support Portal for troubleshooting and guidance:

- [Knowledge Base](https://support.reltio.com/hc/en-us/categories/360001751992): Technical articles and how-to guides from the Reltio Support team. Useful for resolving common issues or learning feature workflows.
- [Reltio Community](https://community.reltio.com): Peer discussions, shared use cases, and best practices from other Reltio users and experts.

## Interact with Sage

**Sage***Image: sage_icon.svg*

[support portal](https://support.reltio.com/hc/en-us)*Image: p-support-portal-chatbot-icon.png*

The following support options are available to you:

- Ask product questions
- Request information about designated contacts
- Check the status of enhancement requests
- Submit a support request

For more information, see [Sage - Reltio's support AI assistant](https://docs.reltio.com/en/reltio/whats-in-the-box/whats-in-the-box-at-a-glance/technical-assistance-at-a-glance/technical-assistance-operations/get-help-in-support-portal/sage---reltios-support-ai-assistant?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs)

## Submit a support request

You can [submit a support request](https://support.reltio.com/hc/en-us/requests/new) on the Reltio Support Portal. A Reltio Support Engineer will follow up to help with any product questions, enhancement requests, tasks, or technical issues.

> **Note:** Only designated contacts in your organization can create tickets. If you're not a designated contact, reach out to your organization's **Designated Contact Administrator** or **Customer Success Manager**. For more information, see [Support Portal designated contacts](https://docs.reltio.com/en/reltio/whats-in-the-box/whats-in-the-box-at-a-glance/technical-assistance-at-a-glance/technical-assistance-operations/get-help-in-support-portal/support-portal-designated-contacts?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).

Support requests are of three types: Break-Fix Problems, Tasks, and Product Questions. 

**Report a Break-Fix Problem**

Use this request type to report bugs, errors, or unexpected behavior in the platform. To help Reltio Support respond effectively, include the following details: 

- **Describe the Issue**: Explain what is happening versus what you expected. Be as specific as possible.
- **Steps to Reproduce**: Provide a step-by-step guide on how to replicate the problem. This helps us diagnose the issue quickly.
- **Impact Assessment**: Describe how the issue is affecting your operations. Understanding the severity and scope helps us prioritize our response. See **Severity Definitions** in the [Support Policy](https://www.reltio.com/sla-and-support-policy).
- **Error Messages and Logs**: Include any error messages, codes, or logs that are related to the issue. These often contain key insights for troubleshooting.
- **Visual Proof**: Screenshots or screen recordings of the issue in action are helpful in understanding the exact nature of the problem.

**Request a Task**

Use this request type when you need help performing a technical action or want to suggest a product improvement. Tasks are of two types:

- **Technical tasks**: For requesting help with specific actions in your tenant, such as cloning, snapshots, or configuration changes.
- **Enhancement requests**: For suggesting improvements to existing features or proposing new capabilities.





To help Reltio Support respond effectively, include the following information: 

- **Define the Objective**: Clearly describe the outcome you're trying to achieve.This helps us understand the context and purpose of the request.
- **Detail the Requirements**: Describe the conditions or inputs needed to complete the task. If you're unsure, share what you've already tried or considered.
- **Provide a Timeline**: Share a timeline so we can prioritize accordingly.

**Ask a Product Question**

Use this request type to ask about Reltio features, clarify documentation, or get guidance on usage best practices. To help Reltio Support respond effectively, include the following details: 

- **Be Specific**: Clearly describe what you're trying to achieve, including any relevant use case details or expected outcomes.
- **Include Context**: Briefly explain what led to your question. Understanding your workflow helps us tailor our response.
- **Reference Materials**: Mention any documentation or resources you've already consulted. This helps avoid repeating known guidance.
- **Provide Visuals**: Whenever possible, include screenshots or recordings to visually illustrate your question.

# RDM Autopilot

> **Section:** Applications > RDM > RDM at a glance > RDM operation


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/rdm/rdm-at-a-glance/rdm-operation/rdm-autopilot?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs

**Keywords:** RDM Autopilot, Reltio Autopilot, Autopilot API, Autopilot configuration, automatic mapping RDM, suggested mapping RDM, misspelling detection RDM, lookup creation RDM, unmapped values RDM, transcode failures RDM, semantic matching RDM, fuzzy matching RDM, AI-based mapping RDM, frequency-based mapping, Autopilot preview mode, Autopilot active mode, data mapping automation, DCR mapping workflow, Autopilot dashboard, mapping statistics RDM


Learn how to configure RDM Autopilot for automated and assisted reference data mapping.

RDM Autopilot (Intelligent Mapping) is an optional automation capability in Reltio Reference Data Management (RDM) that helps organizations automatically resolve unmapped source values during transcode operations. When a source value does not have a mapping to a canonical lookup value, Autopilot analyzes the value using semantic similarity, fuzzy matching, AI reasoning, and frequency thresholds. Based on this evaluation, Autopilot automatically maps values, generates suggestions for steward review, detect misspellings, or recommends creating new lookup entries.

> **Note:** - Autopilot is disabled by default. Because it uses AI-based evaluation, you must explicitly enable the Autopilot feature in the configuration settings before you can use it.
> - To enable RDM Autopilot, you must have Create, Read, Update, and Delete access to the **RDM Configuration** resource. Users assigned the `ROLE_ADMIN_TENANT` role have this access by default. You can also grant resource-level access on **RDM Configuration** to specific users, allowing them to enable RDM Autopilot without the full `ROLE_ADMIN_TENANT` role.

You maintain full control over whether the feature is used. If the feature is not turned on, the system continues to behave as usual, and unmapped values must be handled manually..

> **Note:** Autopilot does not work for MDM tenants configured with the "All in memory" RDM cache. In such tenants, Autopilot will not act on transcode errors originating from MDM. However, Autopilot can still be used independently on the RDM tenant through the Transcode API.

Once enabled, Autopilot monitors transcode failures and evaluates unmapped values in the background. The processing is asynchronous, which means it does not impact transcode API performance or latency. This allows organizations to introduce automation safely while maintaining governance through configurable thresholds, workflow approvals, and monitoring tools.

Based on its configuration, Autopilot supports the following capabilities:

| Capability | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Automatic Mapping | Automatically creates mappings when confidence thresholds are met |
| Suggested Mapping | Generates a Data Change Request (DCR) for human review |
| Misspelling Detection | Identifies likely misspellings and caches the resolution |
| Lookup Creation | Automatically creates new lookup entries |
| Suggested lookup | Recommends creating a new lookup entry and generates a Data Change Request (DCR) for steward review when the value belongs to the lookup type but does not match an existing entry. |

## Why would I use RDM Autopilot

Organizations often receive reference data from multiple source systems. These systems may send values with typos, abbreviations, naming variations, or new entries that do not yet exist in the lookup table. When this happens, the transcode operation fails and data stewards must manually review and map the value.

As data volume increases, these unmapped values can accumulate quickly and create delays in data processing. Manual resolution also increases the risk of inconsistent mappings.

RDM Autopilot helps reduce this effort by automatically analyzing unmapped values, identifying likely matches, and either creating mappings or generating suggestions for steward review.

| Common Issue | Example |
| --- | --- |
| Typos | Untied States → United States |
| Naming Variations | U.S.A → United States |
| Different Conventions | UK → United Kingdom |
| New Values from Source Systems | New region, currency, or product code |

## Autopilot Capabilities

Autopilot combines multiple technologies to intelligently resolve mappings.

| Capability | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Semantic Matching | Uses semantic score to understand meaning and find similar canonical values |
| Fuzzy Matching | Calculates textual similarity between source values and lookup values |
| AI Decision Support | Uses AI models to evaluate ambiguous matches and provide reasoning |
| Frequency Validation | Requires a value to meet the configured frequency threshold before automation occurs, including cases where the threshold is set to 1 |
| Workflow Integration | Generates DCR tasks for steward review when needed |

## Autopilot Modes

RDM Autopilot supports two operating modes that control how the system handles unmapped values. These modes allow you to evaluate the feature safely before enabling full automation. Youcan choose the appropriate mode based on their governance requirements and confidence in the configured thresholds.

**Preview Mode**

In Preview mode, Autopilot analyzes unmapped values and identifies potential matches but does not automatically create mappings. The system records similarity scores and tracks how frequently values appear. This mode allows you to observe how Autopilot performs and refine configuration settings before enabling automation.

**Active Mode**

In Active mode, Autopilot automatically creates mappings when the configured similarity score and frequency thresholds are met. If a value does not meet the automation threshold but still qualifies as a potential match, Autopilot generates a suggestion for steward review through a Data Change Request (DCR) workflow. This mode allows you to automate routine mapping decisions while maintaining governance for cases that require manual validation.

> **Note:** - Switching between Preview and Active modes does not delete Autopilot's learning or existing stats. Use mode switching to pause or resume Autopilot processing without losing learned behavior or tracked data.
> - Before you switch from Preview to Active mode, review the Insights (statistics) tab. If the AI reasoning looks incorrect, adjust the thresholds, lookup type descriptions, or blocked values first. Active mode starts acting on data immediately.

## How Autopilot Evaluates and Resolves Unmapped Values

When a transcode operation fails because a source value does not have a mapping, RDM Autopilot evaluates the value to determine the appropriate action. The system analyzes the value using similarity scoring, and frequency tracking. Based on this evaluation, Autopilot decides whether to automatically create a mapping, suggest a mapping for review, detect a misspelling, or recommend creating a new lookup entry.

This evaluation process ensures that automation occurs only when sufficient confidence and usage frequency are observed.

> **Note:** Autopilot tracks unmapped values separately for each source. The same value from different sources is evaluated independently. Autopilot also calculates the required frequency per source within a rolling time window.

**Evaluation Factors**

Autopilot evaluates unmapped values using several factors.

| Evaluation Factor | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Similarity Score | Measures how closely the source value matches existing lookup values using semantic and fuzzy similarity |
| Frequency Threshold | Ensures that value appears within a defined time window before automation occurs |
| AI Evaluation | Uses AI models to validate ambiguous matches, detect misspellings, or recommend creating new lookup values |

**Possible Outcomes**

After evaluating a value, Autopilot assigns one of the following outcomes.

| Outcome | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Automatic Mapping | Creates a mapping between the source value and the canonical lookup value when confidence and frequency thresholds are met |
| Suggested Mapping | Generates a suggestion and creates a Data Change Request (DCR) for steward review |
| Misspelling Detection | Identifies a spelling error and caches the corrected mapping for future occurrences |
| Lookup Creation | Creates a new lookup entry automatically when the value belongs to the lookup type and the configured threshold is met. |
| Suggested lookup creation | Recommends creating a new lookup entry and creates a Data Change Request (DCR) for steward review when the value belongs to the lookup type but does not match an existing entry. |
| No Match | No suitable candidate is found, so the value remains unresolved |

> **Note:** DCR_PENDING rows are not terminal but remain paused. Autopilot does not process them until the DCR is completed in the workflow. If a DCR is stuck or no longer needed, close or reject it, then delete the stat to allow a new evaluation.

## Autopilot Dashboard

The RDM Autopilot Dashboard allows users to monitor Autopilot activity.

| Metrics | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Automapped | Number of values automatically mapped by Autopilot based on thresholds. |
| Mappings suggested | Number of mappings generated as suggestions pending steward review. |
| Lookup Created | Number of new lookup values created automatically, which appear under the Lookup Suggested tab. |
| Lookup suggested | Number of suggestions to create new lookup values when no match is found. |
| Misspelled | Number of values identified as potential misspellings. |
| Ignored | Number of values excluded from processing due to configuration or rules. |

> **Note:** Ensure that the tenant is registered in the Workflow Service and has the required permissions to access and use workflow features for Autopilot in the UI.

# Create and share a product idea

> **Section:** Reltio > What’s in the box? > What's in the box at a glance > Technical assistance at a glance > Technical assistance operations > Submit product suggestions in Ideas Portal


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/reltio/whats-in-the-box/whats-in-the-box-at-a-glance/technical-assistance-at-a-glance/technical-assistance-operations/submit-product-suggestions-in-ideas-portal/create-and-share-a-product-idea?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs

**Keywords:** Reltio Ideas Portal, Ideas Portl, Submit an idea, suggest improvements, suggest enhancements, share an idea, request an enhancement, enhancement request, new feature request


Learn how to submit an idea to the Reltio Ideas Portal.

The Reltio Ideas Portal requires separate credentials from your Reltio Context Intelligence Platform account. Contact the Product Management to get access.account. Contact the Product Management to get access.

When you have your access credentials, share your ideas on how to improve the Reltio Context Intelligence Platform with Reltio Product Managers and other users! with Reltio Product Managers and other users! > **Note:** Great minds think alike! Before you submit your idea, see if someone else has already shared something similar (for mor information, see topic [View existing product ideas](https://docs.reltio.com/en/reltio/whats-in-the-box/whats-in-the-box-at-a-glance/technical-assistance-at-a-glance/technical-assistance-operations/submit-product-suggestions-in-ideas-portal/view-existing-product-ideas?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs)). If so, add your own comment on business impact and vote on an existing idea to increase its influence on the product (for more information, see topic [Vote and comment on product ideas](https://docs.reltio.com/en/reltio/whats-in-the-box/whats-in-the-box-at-a-glance/technical-assistance-at-a-glance/technical-assistance-operations/submit-product-suggestions-in-ideas-portal/vote-and-comment-on-product-ideas?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs)). If no similar idea exists, get yours out there for others to vote on.


To create and share a product idea:

1. Sign into the **Reltio Ideas Portal** (for more information, see topic [Get started with the Reltio Ideas Portal](https://docs.reltio.com/en/reltio/whats-in-the-box/whats-in-the-box-at-a-glance/technical-assistance-at-a-glance/technical-assistance-operations/submit-product-suggestions-in-ideas-portal/get-started-with-the-reltio-ideas-portal?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs)).
2. In the left panel on the **Welcome to the Ideas Portal** site, select **Add a new idea**.
3. In the displayed **Add idea** page, fill in the following fields:
   - **Your idea**: Enter a one-sentence summary of your idea. This is the title displayed on the **All ideas** page, so make it clear and simple.

> **Tip:** Look in the tip field, which displays any similar items that have already been submitted. Pretty close to your idea? Add your voice to that one by adding a comment to it and voting for it. Yours is completely different? Carry on creating yours.
   - **Choose a category for this idea**: Click in this field and select the component or area for your idea, for example:

- 

  API
- 

  Cleanse
- 

  Connectors

  - 

    D&B Connector
  - 

    Reltio GBQ Connector
  - 

    Reltio Snowflake Connector
- 

  Data Quality
- 

  Match
- 

  Workflow
   - **Describe the problem this idea is meant to solve**: Explain how your idea solves a pain point you're experiencing. This is the summary displayed under your idea title on the **All ideas** page, so make your point clearly in the first sentence and then elaborate as needed. The Reltio Product Management team evaluates the applicability of this information to other issues shared by other customers.
   - **Detailed use case**: Describe the user navigation and data flow for your proposed solution to help visualize the idea in action. Enter any known requirements for the idea, specifically focusing on the must-haves. The Reltio Product Management team uses this information for determining the possibility of implementing the idea.
   - **Business impact**: Describe how this idea would benefit your company. The Reltio Product Management team uses this information for rating this idea against others. Remember, the more companies that vote for an idea that would have an impact on their business, the higher the chances of the idea being considered for implementation. For more information, see topic [Vote and comment on product ideas](https://docs.reltio.com/en/reltio/whats-in-the-box/whats-in-the-box-at-a-glance/technical-assistance-at-a-glance/technical-assistance-operations/submit-product-suggestions-in-ideas-portal/vote-and-comment-on-product-ideas?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).
   - **Industry**:Click in this field and select the industry or market segment your idea is applicable to, for example:

- 

  B2B
- 

  B2C
- 

  Financial Services
- 

  Healthcare
- 

  Insurance
- 

  Life Sciences
   - **User type**: Click in this field and select the user role that would benefit from your idea, for example:

- 

  Admin/Configurator
- 

  Business User
- 

  Data Steward
- 

  Solution Architect



For more information on user roles, see topic[About roles](https://docs.reltio.com/en/roles/about-roles?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).
   - **Customer ID**: Enter an anonymous company identifier you can use to track ideas your team submits.

> **Caution:** Idea Portal suggestions are visible to all customers, so don't enter personal or company-sensitive information.
4. Check your entries for completeness. Providing this information upfront ensures the Product Manager has a complete understanding of the request, reduces the back and forth requests for clarification, and streamlines the process.
5. Select **Add idea** to submit your suggestion,
   OR
   At the top of the page, select **Back to all ideas** to return to the **All ideas** page without submitting your idea.
6. Back on the **All ideas** page, view your submitted idea.

Track your idea's progress in the **Reltio Ideas Portal** search result page, where you can see if other users added comments to or voted for your idea. When a Reltio Product Manager updates the status or adds a comment to your submitted idea, you and anyone else who voted on it will receive an email with the updates. If the Product Manager's email asks you for more details, such as specific use cases, add a comment to your idea in the search result page, where you can see if other users added comments to or voted for your idea. When a Reltio Product Manager updates the status or adds a comment to your submitted idea, you and anyone else who voted on it will receive an email with the updates. If the Product Manager's email asks you for more details, such as specific use cases, add a comment to your idea in the **Ideas Portal**. For more information, see topic . For more information, see topic [Vote and comment on product ideas](https://docs.reltio.com/en/reltio/whats-in-the-box/whats-in-the-box-at-a-glance/technical-assistance-at-a-glance/technical-assistance-operations/submit-product-suggestions-in-ideas-portal/vote-and-comment-on-product-ideas?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs)..

Learn how to search, sort, and filter product improvement suggestions in the Reltio Ideas Portal.

The **Reltio Ideas Portal** requires separate sign-in credentials from your requires separate sign-in credentials from your Reltio Context Intelligence Platform account. For more information, see topic account. For more information, see topic [Get started with the Reltio Ideas Portal](https://docs.reltio.com/en/reltio/whats-in-the-box/whats-in-the-box-at-a-glance/technical-assistance-at-a-glance/technical-assistance-operations/submit-product-suggestions-in-ideas-portal/get-started-with-the-reltio-ideas-portal?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs)..

The **Reltio Ideas Portal** is brimming with bright ideas from our engaged users! Intriguing as it would be to investigate the full inventory of ideas, you probably don't have enough hours in your busy day. Search, sort, or filter product improvement suggestions in the is brimming with bright ideas from our engaged users! Intriguing as it would be to investigate the full inventory of ideas, you probably don't have enough hours in your busy day. Search, sort, or filter product improvement suggestions in the **All ideas** page to take a quick peek around or find a specific idea among the total number shown on the top right.page to take a quick peek around or find a specific idea among the total number shown on the top right.


To view previously submitted ideas in the All ideas page:

1. Sign into the **Reltio Ideas Portal** (for more information, see topic [Get started with the Reltio Ideas Portal](https://docs.reltio.com/en/reltio/whats-in-the-box/whats-in-the-box-at-a-glance/technical-assistance-at-a-glance/technical-assistance-operations/submit-product-suggestions-in-ideas-portal/get-started-with-the-reltio-ideas-portal?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs)).
2. For each idea, view the following details:
   **Vote count and button**

The number of votes for the requested feature. For more information, see topic [Vote and comment on product ideas](https://docs.reltio.com/en/reltio/whats-in-the-box/whats-in-the-box-at-a-glance/technical-assistance-at-a-glance/technical-assistance-operations/submit-product-suggestions-in-ideas-portal/vote-and-comment-on-product-ideas?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).

**Idea summary**

A one-sentence summary of the idea for a new feature.

**Problem description**

A brief explanation of the problem the enhancement feature would resolve.

**Details link**

A link to the enhancement request raised for this idea. 

- 

  **Creation date**: The date this idea was submitted.
- 

  **Category**: The category this idea was submitted under.
- 

  **Comments**: The number of and link to any comments added to the submitted idea in the enhancement request.
- 

  **Status**: The color-coded status of this submitted idea.
   *Image: ideasportal-view-details.png*
3. In the **Search all ideas** field on the top left of the page, enter text for a specific idea you're looking for and then press **Enter**.
4. In the left panel, select a facet to filter the displayed ideas (the number of ideas is shown for each facet):
   - **My ideas**: Any ideas you have submitted. For more information, see topic [Create and share a product idea](https://docs.reltio.com/en/reltio/whats-in-the-box/whats-in-the-box-at-a-glance/technical-assistance-at-a-glance/technical-assistance-operations/submit-product-suggestions-in-ideas-portal/create-and-share-a-product-idea?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).
   - **My votes**: Any ideas from other users you have voted on.
   - **Filter by Category**: A specific category or sub category, for example:

- 

  API
- 

  Cleanse
- 

  Connectors
- 

  Data Quality
- 

  Match
- 

  Workflow

The currently applied facet is displayed at the top of the page. The **Filter by Category** facet shows results only within **My ideas** or **My votes** if you first selected one of these facets.

Click the **x** on a selected facet to clear it.
5. From the **Sort by** menu on the top right of the page, select the way you'd like to sort the entries displayed in the page:
   - **Recent**: Order by newest.
   - **Trending**: Order by date of votes{what?} This is the default.
   - **Popular**: Order by the number of votes {and comments?}.
6. From the **Filter by status** menu on the top right of the page, select the status of the entries you'd like to view in the page (the number of ideas is displayed for each status):
   - **Open**: The requested feature has not yet been reviewed; awaiting more customer votes to support the idea before making a decision.
   - **Already exists**: The requested feature already is available in the product.
   - **Planned**: The requested feature is planned for the next release
   - **Review in progress**: The idea is being researched to determine the best way to address the requested feature. Depending on the complexity, it may remain this status for some time before being moved to another status.
   - **Future consideration**: The requested feature will not be implemented immediately but will be considered for inclusion in one of the next 3 release cycles. This status is hidden by default.
   - **Shipped**: The requested feature has been released. This status is hidden by default.
   - **Archived**: The requested feature is not in the product roadmap for the foreseeable future. In the event the roadmap scope changes and the idea is covered, the status will be updated at that time.
7. In the displayed Search results page, scroll down through the list of ideas that match any applied facets or filters. For a large volume of results, use the navigation buttons at the bottom of the page to go to the **First**, **Prev**, **Next**, **Last**, or a specific results page.
8. Select an idea to view the full enhancement request.
   *Image: ideasportal-view-er.png*

See an idea you can get on board with? You can further influence its chances! For more information, see topic [Vote and comment on product ideas](https://docs.reltio.com/en/reltio/whats-in-the-box/whats-in-the-box-at-a-glance/technical-assistance-at-a-glance/technical-assistance-operations/submit-product-suggestions-in-ideas-portal/vote-and-comment-on-product-ideas?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs)..

Learn how to add your support to a previously submitted product idea.

The **Reltio Ideas Portal** requires separate sign-in credentials from your requires separate sign-in credentials from your Reltio Context Intelligence Platform account. For more information, see topic account. For more information, see topic [Submit product suggestions in Ideas Portal](https://docs.reltio.com/en/reltio/whats-in-the-box/whats-in-the-box-at-a-glance/technical-assistance-at-a-glance/technical-assistance-operations/submit-product-suggestions-in-ideas-portal?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs)

Great minds think alike! If you see an idea from another user that would work for you, add comments to provide further context for your use case and vote on it to further influence its chances of getting implemented. When an idea at Open status receives votes from five or more companies, the Reltio product team reviews it to determine the next step. For more information on idea statuses, see topic [View existing product ideas](https://docs.reltio.com/en/reltio/whats-in-the-box/whats-in-the-box-at-a-glance/technical-assistance-at-a-glance/technical-assistance-operations/submit-product-suggestions-in-ideas-portal/view-existing-product-ideas?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs). .


To vote and comment on existing product ideas.

1. Sign into the **Reltio Ideas Portal** (for more information, see topic [Get started with the Reltio Ideas Portal](https://docs.reltio.com/en/reltio/whats-in-the-box/whats-in-the-box-at-a-glance/technical-assistance-at-a-glance/technical-assistance-operations/submit-product-suggestions-in-ideas-portal/get-started-with-the-reltio-ideas-portal?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs)).
2. Locate an idea you want to contribute to (for more information, see topic [View existing product ideas](https://docs.reltio.com/en/reltio/whats-in-the-box/whats-in-the-box-at-a-glance/technical-assistance-at-a-glance/technical-assistance-operations/submit-product-suggestions-in-ideas-portal/view-existing-product-ideas?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs)).
3. Select **Vote** on its left to add your support. Select it again if you want to remove your support.
4. Add your thoughts to the idea:
   - Select the comment icon below the idea description.
   - In the **Comments** section at the bottom of the displayed enhancement request, select **Add a comment**.
   - In the displayed text editor, type in your input and then select **Post comment**.
5. View your added comment in the enhancement request.
6. Select a location on the breadcrumb trail at the top left of the page to return to your previous search result page.

Track an idea's progress in the **Reltio Ideas Portal** search result page, where you can see if other users added comments to or voted for an idea. When a Reltio Product Manager updates the status or adds a comment to a submitted idea, the user who raised it and anyone else who voted on it will receive an email with the updates.search result page, where you can see if other users added comments to or voted for an idea. When a Reltio Product Manager updates the status or adds a comment to a submitted idea, the user who raised it and anyone else who voted on it will receive an email with the updates.

# Get started with Reltio Certifications

> **Section:** Reltio > What’s in the box? > What's in the box at a glance > Technical assistance at a glance > Technical assistance operations > Develop skills in Learn & Partner Portal


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/reltio/whats-in-the-box/whats-in-the-box-at-a-glance/technical-assistance-at-a-glance/technical-assistance-operations/develop-skills-in-learn--partner-portal/get-started-with-reltio-certifications?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs


Learn how to enroll in and complete Reltio Certifications.

Reltio Certifications provide industry-recognized credentials to validate your expertise. Complete exams with advanced proctoring for secure, high-integrity assessments.

An account on **Reltio Learn** is required for certification enrollment, see [Get started with Reltio Learn](https://docs.reltio.com/en/reltio/whats-in-the-box/whats-in-the-box-at-a-glance/technical-assistance-at-a-glance/technical-assistance-operations/develop-skills-in-learn--partner-portal/get-started-with-reltio-learn?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).

Follow these steps to enroll in and complete Reltio Certifications through **Reltio Learn**..


To enroll in a Reltio Certification:

1. In your web browser, log in to [Reltio Learn](https://learn.reltio.com/). For more information, see [Get started with Reltio Learn](https://docs.reltio.com/en/reltio/whats-in-the-box/whats-in-the-box-at-a-glance/technical-assistance-at-a-glance/technical-assistance-operations/develop-skills-in-learn--partner-portal/get-started-with-reltio-learn?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).
   *Image: learn-access.png*
2. On the **Welcome** page, scroll down to **Certifications**.
   *Image: learn-loggedin.png*
3. Select and Enroll in the Certification.
4. First time certification attempt? Complete any noted prerequisites and the Reltio Certification Exam Guide in the Syllabus of the selected Certification.
5. Complete the exam.
6. Results will be sent via email.
7. If you pass, you will receive an email from **Credly** with instructions to claim your credential.
8. Login to **Credly** via the link provided in your email.
   - If you do not have a Credly account, create one.
   - If you already have an account, go to your profile page to view your awarded credential.
9. Learn how to share your credential [here](https://vimeo.com/315901382).
10. Share feedback to [training@reltio.com](mailto:training@reltio.com).

After earning your certification, explore additional learning paths and resources in [Reltio Learn](https://learn.reltio.com/).

# Develop skills in Learn & Partner Portal

> **Section:** Reltio > What’s in the box? > What's in the box at a glance > Technical assistance at a glance > Technical assistance operations

Learn about Reltio's complimentary learning paths and content to start your MDM journey.

Turn Data into Action, Value, Insights, Growth!

If you're a Reltio user or partner, we're here to get you started on your learning journey.

# Configure designated contacts in the Support Portal

> **Section:** Reltio > What’s in the box? > What's in the box at a glance > Technical assistance at a glance > Technical assistance operations > Get help in Support Portal > Support Portal designated contacts


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/reltio/whats-in-the-box/whats-in-the-box-at-a-glance/technical-assistance-at-a-glance/technical-assistance-operations/get-help-in-support-portal/support-portal-designated-contacts/configure-designated-contacts-in-the-support-portal?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs

**Keywords:** Designated Contacts, Support Portal, Contact Management


Learn how to add, modify, or remove support contacts using the Designated Contact App.

Ensure you have Designated Contact Administrator permissions in the Reltio Support Portal.

Use the **Designated Contact App** to manage your organization's support contacts. Only these designated contacts may request support, for more details see to manage your organization's support contacts. Only these designated contacts may request support, for more details see [Support Portal designated contacts](https://docs.reltio.com/en/reltio/whats-in-the-box/whats-in-the-box-at-a-glance/technical-assistance-at-a-glance/technical-assistance-operations/get-help-in-support-portal/support-portal-designated-contacts?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs). .

1. Log in to the [Reltio Support Portal](https://support.reltio.com/).
2. In the navigation bar at the top of the page, select the **Designated Contact** tab.
3. Review the list of current Designated Contacts under the **Manage Contacts** tab.
4. To add a contact, select the right arrow **>**.
5. To remove a contact, select the desired contact and then select the left arrow **<**.
6. Save your changes and notify the team as needed.

The updated list of Designated Contacts is saved, and the selected contacts can now access support resources.

# Tenant cloning, backups, and snapshots

> **Section:** Reltio > What’s in the box? > What's in the box at a glance > Tenants at a glance > Tenant architecture


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/reltio/whats-in-the-box/whats-in-the-box-at-a-glance/tenants-at-a-glance/tenant-architecture/tenant-cloning-backups-and-snapshots?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs


Learn about tenant cloning, backups, and snapshots for restoring data on your tenant.

Reltio provides the following services to help you recover or clone your tenant environment:

- **Tenant cloning**: Creates a full copy of a source tenant, including both data and configuration. Your subscription includes one clone per month. You can purchase additional clones if needed.
- **Daily backups:** Backups are created automatically each day (for AWS only) and include tenant data only, configuration is not included. This service is included in your Reltio subscription.
- **Point-in-time recovery (PITR):** You can use retained backups to restore tenant data to a previous state; for example, after an unexpected result from a data load.
- **On-demand snapshots**: An on-demand backup that you can request through a Support ticket, often before making high-impact changes. The tenant snapshots service saves a copy of your tenant data to file storage. A standard subscription includes a tenant snapshot once a month; you can purchase additional snapshots if needed.

  > **Note:** By default, snapshots include tenant data only, but you can ask Support to include configuration, logs, or other components. Snapshots are retained for 30 days and can be restored once during that period.

## Tenant cloning and snapshots entitlements

The following table displays what is included with your Reltio subscription. You'll be invoiced for any additional requests beyond the default limits.

| Service details | Service details | Amounts |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tenant Cloning | Default entitlement | One per month |
| Tenant Cloning | Pricing* | USD $5,000 per clone |
| Tenant Snapshot & Restore | Default entitlement | One per month |
| Tenant Snapshot & Restore | Pricing* | USD $5,000 per snapshot & restore |
| Tenant Snapshot & Restore | Retention | Default: 30 Days  If required, up to 90 days on AWS and Azure (not available for GCP). |

## Tenant cloning and backup operation

The following guidelines and requirements apply when initiating and scheduling tenant cloning and backup operations:

- Clones or backups can be scheduled to start at any hour from Sunday 9:00 p.m. EST to Thursday 9:00 a.m. EST.
- **Weekend requests:** If you need a clone or backup to start on a weekend, you must submit your ticket at least 5 business days in advance of the desired initiation date.
- **Weekday requests:** For requests submitted on business days, Reltio typically initiates the task within 24 hours after all required information has been received.
- A complete restore or clone of MDM typically takes 3 to 5 business days, excluding holidays, depending on the size of the data.

For additional answers, see the [Tenant cloning, backups, and snapshots FAQ](https://docs.reltio.com/en/reltio/whats-in-the-box/whats-in-the-box-at-a-glance/tenants-at-a-glance/tenant-operation/tenant-cloning-backups-and-snapshots-faq?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).

## Configuration rollback and version history

Reltio doesn't maintain historical versions of your configuration items such as the L3 data model, UI configuration, or RDM. Any update you make replaces the current configuration and cannot be undone automatically. To manage risk, you should maintain your own configuration backups outside of Reltio; for example, by exporting JSON files and storing them in version control systems like Git.

**Best practices:**

- Export and archive your configuration files before any changes — especially the L3 model, RDM configuration, and UI files.
- Store exported configuration in a source control system with branch or folder structures for each tenant (Dev, Test, Prod).
- Use scripts or CI/CD automation to export current configuration regularly and commit it to your repository.
- If needed, re-import a prior version manually to recover from misconfigurations — this is faster and safer than a full tenant rollback.

For critical environments, coordinate with Support to take a snapshot before making changes.

## Daily automated backups

Reltio retains full tenant data backups as part of its business continuity safeguards. Backups apply only to tenant data. They do not include configuration, logs, match rules, or system metadata. These recovery options are not intended for configuration-level restores and should be used only when necessary.

**Daily backups** are system-managed snapshots of your tenant’s core data storage.

| Cloud provider | Availability | Retention |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **AWS** | Enabled | 2 days |
| **Azure** | Not available | — |
| **GCP** | Not available | — |

## Point-in-time recovery (PITR)

PITR enables you to restore tenant data to a specific point within the retention window in **production environments**. PITR applies only to tenant data. It does not include configuration, logs, match rules, or system metadata. These recovery options are not intended for configuration-level restores and should be used only when necessary.

| Cloud provider | Availability | Retention |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **AWS** | Enabled | 35 days |
| **Azure** | Enabled | 30 days |
| **GCP** | Enabled | 30 days |

## On-demand Snapshots

To reduce recovery time and support safer changes, you can request an on-demand snapshot by submitting a Support ticket. These are often used before high-risk configuration updates. 

> **Note:** Snapshots are retained for 30 days by default.

Snapshots include tenant data only, unless you explicitly ask the support team to include configuration, logs, or other metadata. Restoring a snapshot reverts the entire tenant to its earlier state. Snapshots are not automatically deleted after restore and remain available until the end of the retention period.

# Tenants at a glance

> **Section:** Reltio > What’s in the box? > What's in the box at a glance


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/reltio/whats-in-the-box/whats-in-the-box-at-a-glance/tenants-at-a-glance?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs


Get a high-level view of Tenants.

Take it from the top with Tenants. Get the overview here, then see the sub topics in this section to drill down to the details.

## What are Tenants?

Multi-tenancy is a software architecture model that allows multiple users, known as tenants, to share common infrastructure or applications while maintaining logical isolation from one another. Each tenant operates as if it has a dedicated instance of the software or service, even though they all share the underlying resources. In software architecture, tenants share common physical infrastructure or applications while maintaining logical isolation from one another.

A Reltio Context Intelligence Platform license base package provides three tenants: Development, Test, and Production. Your organization can purchase additional tenants to suit its needs.

## Who are Tenants for?

This content is curated for these Reltio user roles defined in topic [About roles](https://docs.reltio.com/en/roles/about-roles?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs):

Data Product OwnerSolution ArchitectDeveloperReltio ConfiguratorSystem AdministratorData StewardBusiness User

## Why would I use Tenants?

You unify and manage your organization data your DEV, TEST, and PROD tenants, which come with:

**Velocity pack**

A preconfigured that most closely supports the business objectives.

**Queues**

An allocated and linked AWS SQS queue to receive events from the tenant. This conveniently enables message-queue style of integrations with other systems in your enterprise.

**Reference Data Management (RDM)**

A logically linked RDM tenant preconfigured with reference data applicable to the preconfigured velocity pack.

**File space**

An AWS S3 bucket to store data files and perform file manipulations. The bucket serves as a convenient folder in the Reltio Context Intelligence Platform where applications can retrieve and place files for data loading and extraction. Sometimes, you may want to place extracts from on-premises systems into this folder for easy access by integration tools.

**Data as a Service (DaaS)**

If your Reltio Context Intelligence Platform license includes the use of Reltio DaaS integration to a Reltio Data Tenant, your DEV, TEST, AND PROD tenants are pre-integrated using Reltio DTSS (Data Tenant Subscription Service).

If your Reltio Context Intelligence Platform license includes the use of Reltio DaaS integration to an enrichment dataset for which you have an account, your DEV, TEST, AND PROD tenants are pre-integrated to the appropriate Reltio data enrichment integration.

## When would I use Tenants?

Use your Reltio tenants typically in this sequence: 

**Development (DEV)**

Develop and modify new configurations. This is the place to perform your configuration research and development, try out new ideas, and experiment and brainstorm with business users. This tenant is provisioned with a small set of sample data designed to illustrate the use of the out-of-the-box application.

A maximum of 200,000 entities is allowed in this tenant.

**Testing (TEST)**

Apply selected elements of the configuration you have created in your Development tenant, and then try them out with a volume of data and various add-ons (for example, integrations) that mimic your production tenant. This tenant is typically integrated with the test environments of your other systems. 

The maximum number of entities allowed in this tenant is the same as your production tenant.

**Production (PROD)**

Actively manage your live production data on this tenant. This tenant provisions the data to downstream analytics and operational systems. It is typically integrated with your organization's other production systems.

The number of entities allowed in this tenant is specified in your organization's license.

## Where do I find Tenants?

Reltio emails an Asset Sheet to the person listed as the Technical Contact on the Reltio Context Intelligence Platform Order Form. That Technical Contact is set up as the organization's Reltio System Administrator, with access to all tenants and assets listed in the Asset Sheet.

The Asset Sheet lists the MDM Tenant UI URLs for the DEV, TEST, and PROD tenants. Any additional components that your organization licensed and enabled are also listed in this sheet.

# Consistency service

> **Section:** Reltio > What’s in the box? > What's in the box at a glance > Tenants at a glance > Tenant operation


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/reltio/whats-in-the-box/whats-in-the-box-at-a-glance/tenants-at-a-glance/tenant-operation/consistency-service?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs

**Keywords:** Consistency service, Data Integrity, Tenant Data Synchronization


Learn about the service for ensuring consistency among storage layers.

The Consistency service is a critical background process in Reltio's platform that automatically identifies and resolves data inconsistencies between different storage layers, ensuring data integrity across the system. The Consistency service plays a vital role in maintaining synchronization between primary and secondary storage systems while operating seamlessly to avoid disrupting your daily operations.

The Consistency service is designed to detect and correct inconsistencies that may arise due to discrepancies between the primary data store (typically used for real-time access) and secondary systems (used for backup, replication, or data recovery). These discrepancies can occur due to network interruptions, temporary system outages, or other unexpected events.

## How the Consistency service works

When an inconsistency is detected, the Consistency service works in real-time to repair the data and synchronize storage layers. Here are the key steps:

1. **Detection:**
   - The Consistency service continuously monitors event logs and data replication queues to detect any potential mismatch between the primary and secondary storage.
   - Internal systems like Reltio Event Bus and Data Replication service generate alerts when a transaction in primary storage doesn’t propagate as expected.
2. **Identification:**
   - The Consistency service cross-references data snapshots in both the primary and secondary layers to isolate discrepancies.
   - It also checks transactional logs and write-ahead logs (WALs) to verify whether all intended transactions were successfully recorded in both storage systems.
3. **Repair:**
   - The repair process leverages data replication protocols that ensure real-time consistency. The Consistency service uses the Data Repair Engine to initiate corrective actions.
   - For significant inconsistencies, version control mechanisms track changes between different data states, and the most recent valid state is restored.
   - Consistency service also invokes schema validation routines to verify that the data structure remains intact during repair.
4. **Storage Synchronization:**
   - After the inconsistency is repaired, the Consistency service initiates synchronization jobs to ensure the data in secondary storage is updated to match the primary store
   - The Data Consistency Validator performs a final verification to confirm that the repair was successful.

Any job or task created by the `irs-admin-user` is associated with the Consistency service.

## Impact on Platform and Data

Here are the key points to note regarding impact:

- **No data loss:** The Consistency service does not delete or modify your data beyond resolving inconsistencies. It is focused on restoring synchronization between storage layers.
- **Minimal performance impact:** The Consistency service typically completes its work without any noticeable impact on system performance. In rare cases, there may be a temporary delay when accessing recently modified records as the system synchronizes data across storage layers.
- **Background execution:** These repairs run as background processes, ensuring that regular operations remain unaffected.

## Why Do These Events Happen?

Data inconsistencies can occur due to a variety of reasons:

- **Temporary network disruptions:** Short-term connectivity issues may cause some transactions to fail to propagate to secondary storage.
- **System failovers:** In the event of a failover, the Consistency service is responsible for ensuring that the secondary storage matches the primary system post-recovery.
- **Latency in storage replication:** The primary and secondary storage systems may occasionally experience a delay in data synchronization, which the Consistency service rectifies.

Reltio uses multi-zone replication and distributed storage systems to minimize the chances of data inconsistencies. The Consistency service ensures that these occasional issues do not affect long-term data accuracy.

## Other Internal Processes That Support Consistency service

The Consistency service works in tandem with several other internal system processes to ensure the platform remains reliable and consistent:

- **Transactional Logging service (TLS):** This service keeps a record of all transactional events across the system and provides a reference point for the Consistency service to validate if any transaction has been missed or duplicated during storage replication.
- **Reltio Event Bus:** The Event Bus is responsible for propagating changes across the system in real-time. When the Consistency service is triggered, it ensures that the changes made by the Consistency service are distributed across the platform, preventing further inconsistencies.
- **Real-time Indexing service:** As the Consistency service modifies or corrects data, the Real-time Indexing service ensures that all updates are reflected in Reltio's search index, allowing users to access the most up-to-date information quickly.
- **Replication Consistency Checker:** This service runs scheduled checks to ensure that all copies of data in the system (both primary and secondary) are fully consistent, reducing the likelihood of discrepancies. If it detects a mismatch, it informs the Consistency service.
- **High Availability (HA) Mechanisms:** The Consistency service is closely integrated with Reltio's HA architecture, which ensures that even during system failovers or data migrations, the platform remains consistent. HA mechanisms work in conjunction with the Consistency service to handle repairs when needed.

## Action Required?

No direct action is required from your side during Consistency service operations. In rare cases where a Consistency service activity might cause a temporary delay or a slight disruption, our Support team will proactively notify you.

If you experience an issue and are informed that the Consistency service resolved it, this means that our system detected and repaired an inconsistency, ensuring your data remains accurate and synchronized.

# Internet Content Provider (ICP) compliance

> **Section:** Reltio > What’s in the box? > What's in the box at a glance > Tenants at a glance > Tenant architecture


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/reltio/whats-in-the-box/whats-in-the-box-at-a-glance/tenants-at-a-glance/tenant-architecture/internet-content-provider-icp-compliance?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs

**Keywords:** China UI Updates, UI updates - China, ICP license, google maps, location profile, China UI updates


Learn more about the ICP regulations in China.

Reltio hosts its Software as a Service (SaaS) platform in China also. In accordance with government rules and regulations, we may not make available in China the features and functionality we provide in other parts of the world.

Any business operating in China needs an Internet Content Provider (ICP) license issued by the Chinese Ministry of Industry and Information Technology. The Internet Content Provider (ICP) License is a permit issued by the Chinese Ministry of Industry and Information Technology to permit China-based websites to operate legally in China. Any commercial website that offers services to customers must obtain the ICP License.

As per the Chinese regulations, the ICP license number must be visible to users in the UI. To comply with this rule, we display our Reltio ICP license on the following pages on our platform.

- **Login page**: When you sign in to Reltio, you can see the license number at the footer of the page. For more information, see topic [Sign in to Reltio Data Cloud](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/platform/platform-at-a-glance/platform-navigation/sign-in-to-reltio-data-cloud?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).

  *Image: ui_chinaupdateicplogin.png*
- In the **Profile Settings**, in the **Hub**:

  *Image: ui_chinaupdateicpprofile.png*

This license number is also a link, which when clicked takes you to [https://beian.miit.gov.cn/](https://beian.miit.gov.cn/), where you can validate the license against public records.

**Reference Data Management**

In compliance with the local rules related to data sovereignty, we introduced the **Reference Data Management** in our Reltio platform in China. You can now define and maintain reference data for your MDM tenants and your enterprise in general.

# Tenant cloning, backups, and snapshots FAQ

> **Section:** Reltio > What’s in the box? > What's in the box at a glance > Tenants at a glance > Tenant operation


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/reltio/whats-in-the-box/whats-in-the-box-at-a-glance/tenants-at-a-glance/tenant-operation/tenant-cloning-backups-and-snapshots-faq?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs

**Keywords:** Tenant Cloning FAQ, Snapshot and Restore FAQ, snapshot and restore, tenant cloning, snapshots, entitlements


Find the answers to some of the Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) about Tenant Cloning, Backups, and Snapshots, including Restore.

## General

1. **Will my monthly entitlements carry forward if I don't request these operations for a given month?**

   No, these default entitlements don't roll over to the next month.
2. **At the beginning of the year, do I start with 12 entitlements or one entitlement?**

   At the beginning of every month, you start with one entitlement each for a clone, and a snapshot and restore. This entitlement doesn’t change for the first month of the year.
3. **What is the process of requesting clones or snapshots or restores? Do I contact my Customer Success Manager (CSM)?**

   To request one of these operations, you must raise a [support](https://support.reltio.com/hc/en-us) ticket. You don't have to contact your CSM.
4. **If I exceed my base entitlement for either operation for a particular calendar month, when will the invoice get generated?**

   An invoice would be generated at the end of the month based on the number of additional cloning or snapshot operations requested by you, above your default entitlement.
5. **Are the default entitlements per subscription or per tenant?**

   The entitlements are per base package subscription. For example, if you have three base package subscriptions, you get one clone and one snapshot for free per each of those base package subscriptions. These entitlements apply only to their respective base package subscription and may not be used across subscriptions.
6. **If I buy an additional test package, do I get a clone for that package?**

   No. These entitlements are for full base package subscriptions.
7. **What are the implications for those who have already paid for clones or snapshots in the past and never used it?**

   You now have higher entitlements
8. **Does the clone or snapshot include my Reference Data Management (RDM) tenant?**

   Yes. Every Reltio tenant is connected to its own RDM tenant. When you request a clone or snapshot of your Reltio tenant, the RDM tenant is included only if **explicitly** requested.
9. **Does the backup retention period vary for different cloud providers?**

   Yes. Backup retention period differs based on your cloud provider:

   | Cloud provider | Availability | Retention |
   | --- | --- | --- |
   | **AWS** | Enabled | 2 days |
   | **Azure** | Not available | — |
   | **GCP** | Not available | — |
10. **What is the Point-in-time Recovery (PITR) retention period for different cloud providers?**

   Point-in-time recovery (PITR) availability and retention differs based on your cloud providers:

   | Cloud provider | Availability | Retention Period |
   | --- | --- | --- |
   | **AWS** | Enabled | 35 days |
   | **Azure** | Enabled | 30 days |
   | **GCP** | Enabled | 30 days |
11. **Does PITR comply with data protection regulations?**

   Yes. PITR is designed to comply with GDPR, CCPA, HIPAA, and other major regulations. All recovery operations are audited, and backups are encrypted in transit and at rest.

## Tenant snapshot and restore

1. **Will snapshots be taken once a month without me asking for it, just like backups?**

   No, snapshots will be taken only on request.
2. **What is the difference between a snapshot and the regular backups that Reltio provides?**

   Daily backups and snapshots serve different recovery purposes in Reltio. The following table highlights the differences.

   | Attribute | Daily Backups | Snapshots |
   | --- | --- | --- |
   | **Description** | Automatically created once per day for production tenants in AWS environments. Not suitable for restoring data to an exact point in time. | On-demand backups initiated via Support ticket, typically before major configuration changes. Not suitable for restoring data to an exact point in time. |
   | **Type of Data** | Tenant data only | Tenant data only by default; configuration, logs, and other elements available on request |
   | **Cloud Provider** | AWS only | AWS and Azure (not available for GCP) |
   | **Retention period** | 2 days | 30 days |
   | **Included in Entitlement** | Yes | Yes. Additional charges apply if usage exceeds licensed entitlements. |
3. **Will all snapshots be retained for up to 30 days?**

   If you request a restore, then the snapshot will be deleted after the restore is completed. If you don't request a restore from a particular snapshot, then the snapshot will be kept for 30 days from its date of creation after which it will be automatically deleted.
4. **If I request a snapshot on the 15th of the month and a restore of it on the 10th of the next month, does the monthly default entitlements limit apply to me for the restore?**

   The default entitlement is for a snapshot per calendar month plus an associated restore operation. So, if you request a snapshot, you can request a restore of it anytime within the next 30 days starting from the date the snapshot was taken (not from the date of request), regardless of whether the restore falls into the subsequent calendar month.
5. **Consider this scenario: I request a restore on the 10th of September of a snapshot taken in August. But I also want to request another snapshot later during the month of September. Will I be invoiced for the September snapshot operation?**

   No, the September restore is coupled with the August snapshot, so you will still have your free snapshot entitlement remaining for the month of September.
6. **Can I request multiple restores of the same snapshot?**

   No, after a restore is performed on an existing snapshot, the snapshot would be deleted.
7. **What is included in the snapshot?**

   The snapshot includes tenant data and configurations. It does not include activity logs or history.

   When provisioning a snapshot, Reltio may ask whether you'd like to include the configuration layer. If requested, this is backed up and restored with the snapshot.
8. **What date is counted for calculating the free limit? The request date or the operation complete date?**

   The request date is considered for calculating the free limit.
9. **Is there any data size cap for snapshots?**

   Yes. The supported data size for snapshots for free of cost operation would be up to 50 TB. You may request custom pricing for exceeding this limit.
10. **Can I use a snapshot or backup to recover from an unwanted configuration change?**

   Yes, but use caution. Reltio snapshots and backups include both configuration and data. Restoring either will revert the entire tenant to an earlier point in time, including any data changes made after that point. This action can’t selectively roll back only the configuration. If the issue is isolated to configuration changes, it’s faster and safer to manually re-import a previously saved version of your configuration file. Reltio doesn't support configuration-only restores via the UI or API.

## Tenant cloning

1. **What are the guidelines and requirements for initiating and scheduling tenant cloning and backup operations?**

   There are mainly timing requirements, see [Tenant cloning, backups, and snapshots](https://docs.reltio.com/en/reltio/whats-in-the-box/whats-in-the-box-at-a-glance/tenants-at-a-glance/tenant-architecture/tenant-cloning-backups-and-snapshots?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).
2. **Can I request partial clones?**

   No, partial clones won't be supported. If you are looking to bring production or test data to your dev environment, then there are other means to accomplish that, such as [exporting data](https://docs.reltio.com/en/objectives/load-and-export-data/data-exporting-at-a-glance/data-exporting-operation/export-data-using-reltio-export-service?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).
3. **Is cloning of history supported?**

   Cloning of history isn't encouraged as it inflates the size of the cloned tenant, and will be done only if specifically requested.
4. **Will the target tenant be accessible during the cloning process?**

   No, the target tenant isn't available during the cloning process. Any activity on the tenant can interfere with cloning and may lead to an incomplete or unsuccessful outcome. To ensure a successful cloning process, don't use the target tenant until cloning is complete.

   > **Tip:** Track the progress of the cloning ticket you submitted with Reltio Support. This ensures you know exactly when it's safe to access the target system again without disrupting the cloning process.

# GDPR compliance in the Reltio Platform

> **Section:** Reltio > What’s in the box? > What's in the box at a glance > Tenants at a glance > Tenant architecture


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/reltio/whats-in-the-box/whats-in-the-box-at-a-glance/tenants-at-a-glance/tenant-architecture/gdpr-compliance-in-the-reltio-platform?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs

**Keywords:** EU GDPR Law, Directive 95/46/EC, consumer data compliance, GDPR compliance, GDPR law and compliance requirements, GDPR compliance in Reltio Platform, how Reltio supports GDPR compliance, Right to be Forgotten in Reltio, GDPR data deletion concepts


Learn about how the Reltio Platform supports compliance with EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) requirements.

## About GDPR

The European Union (EU) General Data Protection Regulations (GDPR) is a law designed to enhance data protection for EU residents and provide a consolidated framework to guide business usage of personal data across the EU. According to the written regulation published by [gdpr.eu](https://gdpr.eu/tag/gdpr/), it: 

- protects the personal data of individuals residing in the EU, as well as non-EU residents visiting the EU.
- applies to monitoring individual behavior, processing personal data through automation, and processing data by any method with the intention of filing that data.
- applies to any entity that processes or controls data in the EU, offers goods or services to people who are in the EU, or monitors behaviors of people physically in or related to the EU.
- extends due diligence obligations and potential liability to data controllers and data processor.



The broad scope and definitions of the GDPR means it applies to almost every website or app that tracks data, and any business - whether located in the EU or not - that does work in or for the EU.

> **Note:** The breadth and scope of the GDPR typically outweighs the regulations of local laws, such as the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) in the US. Local laws may or may not have different regulations that apply to you.

## GDPR compliance requirements

According to the GDPR Compliance requirements, the following data is affected: 

- All profile entity or entities
- All historical data
- All losing entity or entities (for more information, see [Merging Two Entities](https://docs.reltio.com/en/developer-resources/entity-management-apis/entity-management-apis-at-a-glance/merge-and-unmerge-entities-api/merging-two-entities?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs))
- All records from the [Activity Log](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/hub/profiles-at-a-glance/profile-perspectives-tabs/profile-perspectives-navigation/activity-log-perspective?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs) except records about creating and deleting

Your consumer data in Reltio must be compliant within 30 days of the request, unless: 

- The customer has a pending transaction.
- The customer has completed a transaction with the past 30 days.

> **Important:** We recommend that you keep a record of the person or organization requesting each GDPR delete, preferably in a rights management system, as the Reltio platform doesn't store the identity of the requester.

## How the Reltio Platform supports GDPR compliance

The Reltio Platform supports compliance with the EU GDPR by providing mechanisms to remove personal data when a data subject exercises their **Right to be forgotten**.

When consumer data is deleted for GDPR purposes, the platform removes personal attribute values and related historical information associated with the entity. This ensures that personal data is no longer accessible or processed within the platform.

The platform also sanitizes audit and activity information to ensure that sensitive data is no longer visible, while retaining minimal system events related to entity creation and deletion for compliance and traceability.

GDPR deletion requests are typically initiated outside of the Reltio Platform through a rights management or compliance system. The Reltio Platform does not store the identity of the individual or organization requesting the deletion.

For more information about how GDPR deletion is implemented in Reltio, see [Delete Entities by GDPR](https://docs.reltio.com/en/developer-resources/entity-management-apis/entity-management-apis-at-a-glance/entities-api/delete-entity/delete-entities-by-gdpr?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).
