# Create an Analyze match strategy job

> **Section:** Applications > Console > Tenant management applications > Tenant Management at a glance > Jobs at a glance


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/console/tenant-management-applications/tenant-management-at-a-glance/jobs-at-a-glance/create-an-analyze-match-strategy-job?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs

**Keywords:** learn how to create analyze match strategy job, create analyze match strategy in console, analyze match rules job setup, measure match precision score, analyze match configuration performance, run analyze match strategy job, entity types in analyze match strategy, job parameters for analyze match strategy, analyze match rules, precision, configuration, job


Learn how to create an Analyze Match Strategy job to review match rules, measure precision, and analyze configuration performance.

This job analyzes the match strategy using sample match pairs from your tenant. The analysis generates key statistics and actionable recommendations to improve match accuracy and effectiveness.

**Prerequisites**

To calculate match precision, tenants must have labeled data. For details on labeling data, see [Match precision labeling APIs](https://docs.reltio.com/en/developer-resources/entity-management-apis/entity-management-apis-at-a-glance/potential-matches-api/match-precision-labeling-apis?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs)..


Follow these steps to create an Analyze match strategy job:

1. In **Console**, select the **Tenant Management** application.
2. Select **+ SELECT A JOB**.
   The **Create new job** screen displays all the jobs that you can run, as shown below.
   *Image: em_analyze_1.png*
3. Select the **Analyze match strategy** job.
   This job's parameters appear as follows:
   *Image: em_analyze_2.png*
   You can select multiple entity types as shown in the following image:
   *Image: em_analyze_3.png*
   > **Note:** Entity types without configured match rules do not appear in the list.
4. Enable at least one option:
   - **Calculate match precision score** — measures the accuracy of match rules based on reviewed matches.
   - **Analyze match configuration** — provides statistics on how efficiently match rules generate potential matches. To use this option, enter the number of entities to analyze (up to 100000).
5. Select **RUN JOB**.
   A notification appears indicating that an email will be sent once the job is completed.
6. When the job is under the **Pending** tab, you can pause (⏸) or stop (◼) the job by selecting the respective button as shown below.
   *Image: em_analyze_4.png*
7. Select on a job under the **Completed** tab to view job details as follows:
   *Image: em_analyze_5.png*

# Delete tenant data

> **Section:** Applications > Console > Tenant management applications > Tenant Management at a glance > Jobs at a glance


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/console/tenant-management-applications/tenant-management-at-a-glance/jobs-at-a-glance/delete-tenant-data?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs

**Keywords:** delete tenant data, delete tenant data job, ROLE_ADMIN_TENANT, ROLE_ADMIN_CUSTOMER, tenant management job


Learn about the Delete tenant data job.

As a tenant administrator, have you ever secretly wished to have greater control over how quickly your organization’s tenant data is deleted? Sure, your data delete request is taken care of without any delay and it's all going fine, but sometimes you’re just left wanting more.

If you’ve ever wanted to delete your data, so you can load brand new data or reload the data to test your configurations any time you want, you’ve come to the right place!

Exercise your right to get rid of old data in a development or test tenant and replace it with new data using the **Delete tenant data** job in the **Console Tenant Management** application. You can delete from your tenant just its data or both its data and activity log.

The **Delete tenant data** job runs only on development or testing tenants. If you want to delete data from a Production tenants, contact Reltio Customer Engineering for assistance (for further information, see topic [Get help in Support Portal](https://docs.reltio.com/en/reltio/whats-in-the-box/whats-in-the-box-at-a-glance/technical-assistance-at-a-glance/technical-assistance-operations/get-help-in-support-portal?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).

Ensure no other jobs are running before you start a **Delete tenant data** job. Once you start this job, all other tenant management jobs are locked, so you cannot run them until this job is complete. You can run only one **Delete tenant data** job at a time. If you try to run another **Delete tenant data** job before the current job is completed, you receive a notification to either wait for the job to complete or stop that job to run a new **Delete tenant data** job.

*Image: tenant-delete-job.png**Image: [unresolved]*

## Permissions to delete tenant data

You don't want just anyone to be able to delete data from your organization's tenants. The Reltio security model keeps you in control of who can access and manage your tenant data by defining roles and specifying their permissions:

**System roles**

Reltio provides these default roles for managing your organization's tenants:

- 

  ROLE_ADMIN_TENANT: This Tenant Administrator role is associated with a tenant. It provides permissions to access and manage tenant services and data.This role is automatically assigned to each tenant in your organization's Reltio Context Intelligence Platform. For more information, see topic [ROLE_ADMIN_CUSTOMER Access permissions](https://docs.reltio.com/en/objectives/administer-system/system-administration-at-a-glance/access-management-at-a-glance/access-management-reference/authorization/system-roles/critical-high-privilege-roles/role_admin_customer-access-permissions?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).
- 

  ROLE_ADMIN_CUSTOMER: This Customer Administrator role is associated with a user. It provides permissions to manage tenants and their users. This role is automatically assigned to users identified as your organization's tenant administrators.

**Custom roles**

As a Customer Administrator with the ROLE_ADMIN_CUSTOMER role assigned, you can create custom roles to meet your organization's needs instead of depending on various Reltio system roles. associate permissions, and assign them to users

To enable other users to delete data from a tenant, in the **Console User Management** application, create a new role or update and existing one. Select the appropriate access privileges for this service and the tenant. Then assign this role to a user with access to the tenant. For more information, see topics [Custom roles](https://docs.reltio.com/en/objectives/administer-system/system-administration-at-a-glance/access-management-at-a-glance/access-management-reference/authorization/custom-roles?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs) and [Managing Role Definitions](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/console/security-applications/user-management-at-a-glance/managing-role-definitions?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).

# Creating a Consistency Check Job

> **Section:** Applications > Console > Tenant management applications > Tenant Management at a glance > Jobs at a glance


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/console/tenant-management-applications/tenant-management-at-a-glance/jobs-at-a-glance/creating-a-consistency-check-job?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs

**Keywords:** Consistency Check Job, consistency check job, resolve inconsistencies job, consistency job, primary storage, secondary storage


This job resolves inconsistencies between primary and secondary storages.

This job performs background comparison of primary and secondary storages to find inconsistencies. If any entities are found in the primary storage that are not present in the secondary storage, this job will try to re-index such entities. If any entities are missing from the primary storage but present in the secondary storage, this job will remove such entities from the secondary storage.To run the **Consistency Check** job, perform the following steps:

1. In Console, click on the **Tenant Management** application.
2. Click **NEW JOB**.
   The **Create new job** screen displays all the jobs that the user can run as shown below:
   *Image: em_selectnewjob.png*
3. Click on **Consistency check** job.
   The job parameters appear as follows:
   *Image: em_consistcheckparam.png*
   > **Note:** If the **Compare Versions** and **Fix Version Conflicts** parameters are not enabled, then this job checks/fixes only those cases where objects are available in one of the storages. The job does not fix those cases where objects with different content are available in both the storages. These parameters are very useful during investigations.
4. Specify values for the job parameters based on your requirement.
5. Click **RUN JOB**.

# Creating a Rebuild Match Tables Job

> **Section:** Applications > Console > Tenant management applications > Tenant Management at a glance > Jobs at a glance


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/console/tenant-management-applications/tenant-management-at-a-glance/jobs-at-a-glance/creating-a-rebuild-match-tables-job?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs

**Keywords:** create rebuild match table job tenant management, rebuild match tables job reltio, include fern vectorization toggle, fern vector rebuild before match table, runFernReindexBeforeRebuild parameter, tenant management rebuild match table console


Learn how to create a Rebuild Match Tables job in Tenant Management, including the optional FERN vectorization step.

The **Rebuild Match Tables** job recalculates potential matches for a tenant based on the current match rules. Run this job when you need potential matches to reflect recent changes; for example, after loading data or updating match rules.

If your tenant uses FERN for AI-powered matching, the Rebuild Match Tables job includes vectorization by default to update vector data before the rebuild starts. You can turn off vectorization if vectors are already up to date.

**Prerequisites**

Before you create a Rebuild Match Tables job, make sure you have the following permissions and access:

- 

  Permission to update the L3 tenant configuration using the Configuration API
- 

  `ROLE_ADMIN_TENANT` role to run the Rebuild Match Table task from Console
- 

  Access to the **Tenant Management** application in **Console**


To create a Rebuild Match Tables job:

1. In the **Console**, select the **Tenant Management** application.
2. Click **NEW JOB**.
   The **Create new job** page displays all the jobs that you can run.
   *Image: em_selectnewjob.png*
3. Select the **Rebuild match table** job to view to view the **Rebuild match table** page.
   *Image: em_rebuild_job.png*
4. Specify values for the job parameters based on your requirement.
   | Parameter | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Entity type** | Select the entity type, or select **All types** to process every entity type. | All types |
| **Skip entities count** | Number of entities to skip before the job starts processing. | 0 |
| **Entities limit** | Number of entities to process. Leave blank to process all entities. | All |
| **AI-powered vectorization** | Turn on to run FERN vectorization before the rebuild. The **AI-powered vectorization** parameter appears only if your tenant uses [FERN](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/console/configuration-applications/ai-powered-flexible-entity-resolution-network-fern-model-based-matching-at-a-glance?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs). This parameter is on by default. When on, the job runs vectorization to update your records for AI-powered matching. The rebuild starts only after vectorization completes successfully. When off, the job rebuilds the match table without running vectorization. | On |
| **Delete Old Column Families** | Turn on to delete existing column families as part of this run. | Off |
| **Distributed** | Turn on to split work across multiple parallel jobs on different API nodes. | Off |
| **Job parts count** | Number of parallel jobs for distributed mode. Available only when **Distributed** is on. Reltio recommends setting this to the number of API nodes available to run the job. | 2 |
5. Click **RUN JOB**.

**Result**The job rebuilds the match table for the selected entities based on the current match rules, so that new or changed data is considered during matching. The result depends on the parameters you selected:

- 

  **AI-powered vectorization on**: The job checks whether vectorization is needed. If needed, the job runs vectorization first and starts the rebuild only after vectorization completes successfully. If not needed, the job proceeds directly to the rebuild.
- 

  **AI-powered vectorization off**: The job rebuilds the match table without running vectorization.
- 

  **Delete Old Column Families on**: The job deletes existing column families before rebuilding. Distributed on: The job splits work across the number of parts set in Job parts count.

**Verification steps**

- 

  Check the job status in **Tenant Management** to confirm the job completed successfully.
- 

  If AI-powered vectorization was on and vectorization ran, check the Completed tab for these jobs in execution order:
  1. AI vectorization task
  2. AI vectorization worker task
  3. Rebuild match table
- 

  Review potential matches in **Hub** to confirm they reflect the current match rules and, if applicable, current vector data.

For API parameter names and additional options not available in Console, see [Rebuild Match Table Task](https://docs.reltio.com/en/developer-resources/system-administration-apis/system-administration-apis-at-a-glance/tasks-api/rebuild-match-table-task?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).

# External Match at a glance

> **Section:** Objectives > Resolve potential matches > Potential matching at a glance > Potential matching operation


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/objectives/resolve-potential-matches/potential-matching-at-a-glance/potential-matching-operation/external-match-at-a-glance?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs

**Keywords:** External Matching, Rule-Based External Match, External Match, external match, external matching, external match application, rule-based external matching, rule-based matching


Learn about the Console External Match application to match records stored externally in a file with entities within the Reltio platform.

Reltio Entity ResolutionReltio Multidomain MDMReltio Intelligent 360

Use the Console External Match application to match records stored in an external file with entities in the Reltio platform.

To perform this matching, you need to upload the file with entities, map the file columns to an entity's attributes in Reltio tenant, and choose an appropriate match rule to run the match. It is also possible to do cleansing as an option before matching.

> **Note:** Be aware of these source file considerations:
>
> - You can only upload CSV files to the Console External March application. The maximum size of the CSV file that you can upload from a local file system is 50 MB.
> - The `External Match API` provides additional capabilities not available in this Console External Match application, such as the ability to resolve lookups in the source data file. For more information, see topic [External match API](https://docs.reltio.com/en/developer-resources/entity-management-apis/entity-management-apis-at-a-glance/potential-matches-api/external-match-api?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).
> - You can upload JSON files and CSV files using the `External Match API`. The maximum size of the JSON file that you can upload is 50 MB, whether it's from the local file system or remote storage.

The following sections provide information about how to use rule-based matching:

- [External Match Workflow](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/console/tenant-management-applications/external-match-at-a-glance/external-match-workflow?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs)
- [Permissions for the External Match Service](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/console/tenant-management-applications/external-match-at-a-glance/permissions-for-the-external-match-service?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs)
- [Selecting External Entities for Matching](https://docs.reltio.com/en/objectives/resolve-potential-matches/potential-matching-at-a-glance/potential-matching-operation/external-match-at-a-glance/selecting-external-entities-for-matching?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs)
- [Mapping File Columns to Attributes](https://docs.reltio.com/en/objectives/resolve-potential-matches/potential-matching-at-a-glance/potential-matching-operation/external-match-at-a-glance/mapping-file-columns-to-attributes?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs)
- [Mapping Multiple Nested Attributes](https://docs.reltio.com/en/objectives/resolve-potential-matches/potential-matching-at-a-glance/potential-matching-operation/external-match-at-a-glance/mapping-multiple-nested-attributes?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs)

# External Match Workflow

> **Section:** Applications > Console > Tenant management applications > External Match at a glance


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/console/tenant-management-applications/external-match-at-a-glance/external-match-workflow?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs

**Keywords:** External Match Workflow, Rule-Based External Matching Workflow, external match workflow, external matching workflow, match workflow, rule based external matching workflow


The workflow is a sequence of steps for matching the entities from a file with the data in the tenant.

The workflow of how entities from a file are matched is as follows:

1. Create a new job or duplicate an existing job definition.
2. Select the input file from the required source system.
3. Define new mappings or use an existing mapping to map file columns to the entity attributes (part of the entity model). The user can map multiple attributes to one column, if required.
4. Add crosswalks, if required.
5. Review and start Matching.

# Match Analysis at a glance

> **Section:** Applications > Console > Tenant management applications > Tenant Management at a glance


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/console/tenant-management-applications/tenant-management-at-a-glance/match-analysis-at-a-glance?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs

**Keywords:** learn about match analysis, analyze match rules in tenant management, how to view match token phrases, analyze match rules performance, check precision score in match analysis, analyze entity types with match analysis, use filters for match analysis results, match token phrases analysis, match rules analysis, match precision score, tokenization, accuracy


Learn about analyzing match rules, token phrases, and precision scores to improve entity matching accuracy and optimize tenant performance.

The number of match token phrases generated for match groups is very important for the matching process. The number of match token phrases generated has a direct impact on the performance of a match rule. The `Analyze Match Rules` job analyzes the generation of match token phrases and the performance of the match rules configured in your tenant.

For the generation of match token phrases, the `Analyze Match Rules` job checks for the following: 

- If too many tokens are generated by a subset of the processed entities than the specified threshold for the specified match groups.
- If too few tokens are generated by a subset of the processed entities than the specified threshold for the specified match groups.

To analyze the performance of match rules, this job checks the number of match pairs generated for the specified set of entities.

You can use this information to improve your tokenization scheme or tune your match rules to ensure that matching in your tenant produces the desired results.

## View Summary of Match Analysis

1. In **Console**, select the **Tenant Management** application.
2. Select **Match Analysis** on the left navigation bar.

The summary shows the latest results for:

- **Match token phrases analysis** - reviews the distribution of token phrases generated.
- **Match rules analysis** - reviews the number of match pairs generated.
- **Match precision score** - measures the accuracy of match rules based on reviewed matches.

*Image: tm_summary.png*

The image above shows the **HCP** entity type summary when you click the corresponding down arrow on the right.

To view detailed information, select **VIEW DETAILS** in the **Match token phrases analysis**, **Match rules analysis**, or **Match precision score** section.

Alternatively, select a tab at the top:

- **MATCH TOKEN PHRASES******
- **MATCH RULES******
- **MATCH PRECISION**

The **RUN ANALYSIS** button is available in the upper-right corner of the **Match Analysis** page, regardless of the tab you select. The date displayed next to this button shows when the job was last run.

Select **RUN ANALYSIS** to launch a new job if the current results are from an earlier run. This provides a quick way to initiate a new **Analyze Match Strategy** job and refresh the results.*Image: i-tm-matchanalysis-runanalysis.gif* For more information, see [Create an Analyze match strategy job](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/console/tenant-management-applications/tenant-management-at-a-glance/jobs-at-a-glance/create-an-analyze-match-strategy-job?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).

## View Match token phrases analysis

When you select to view the **Match token phrases analysis**, the following page appears:

*Image: tm_matchtoken.png*

This page provides information about the distribution of token phrases generated between the too few and too many ranges.

You can use the **Entity Type** and **Match Rule** filters to view the results of different entity types and match rule combinations.

Select the downward facing arrow under the **What the results mean** section to view a detailed explanation for each item. This section is not displayed if enough data is not available from the analysis.*Image: tm_matchtoken_2.png*

Select the **VIEW PROFILE DETAILS** button above the results section to view profiling information as shown below.

*Image: tm_profiledetails.png*

> **Tip:** You can also **VIEW PROFILING DETAILS** for **MATCH RULES**.

Scroll down to view the list of match token phrases that contain the most entities.

*Image: tm_tokenreview.png*

The image above shows five sample entities for each token phrase. To view all entities, select **VIEW MORE**. A dialog appears, similar to this:

*Image: tm_entitieslist.png*

Select **Download entity IDs** to download a list of entities in a text file.*Image: tm_entitieslist_download.png*

## View Match rules analysis

When you select to view **Match rules analysis**, the following page appears:

*Image: tm_matchrules.png*

This page provides information about the number of match pairs corresponding to the number of entities. Hover your mouse over the graph to view the exact number at that point.

You can change the entity type by using the **Entity Type** filter on the top right-hand corner.

Click the down arrow under the **What the results mean** section to view a detailed explanation about the results.

Scroll to view the list of least frequently used match rules.

*Image: tm_leastrules.png*

When you scroll down further, the information about the overlap of match results by rule pairs is also available at the bottom as shown below.

*Image: tm_ruleoverlap.png*

If you are viewing Match analysis for an individual entity type and if it's [FERN-enabled](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/console/configuration-applications/ai-powered-flexible-entity-resolution-network-fern-model-based-matching-at-a-glance/fern-based-matching/use-a-pretrained-fern-model/enable-a-pretrained-fern-model?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs), the page appears as follows:

*Image: match-rules-fern.png*

## View Match precision score

> **Important:** To calculate match precision, tenants must have labeled data. For details on labeling data, see [Match precision labeling APIs](https://docs.reltio.com/en/developer-resources/entity-management-apis/entity-management-apis-at-a-glance/potential-matches-api/match-precision-labeling-apis?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).



When you select to view**Match precision score**, the following page appears:

*Image: i-tm-matchprecision.png*

This page provides information about how accurately the system identifies true matches versus false matches when comparing entity records. Hover over the graph to view precision values at each point.

You can change the entity type by using the **Entity Type** filter on the top right-hand corner.

Scroll to the **Precision Score Breakdown** table to see precision scores by **Match Strategy**, including the number of true positives, false positives, and false negatives. You can also type a match strategy in the search box to filter the results.*Image: i-tm-matchprecision-matchstrategy.gif*

# Create a revalidate job

> **Section:** Applications > Console > Tenant management applications > Tenant Management at a glance > Jobs at a glance


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/console/tenant-management-applications/tenant-management-at-a-glance/jobs-at-a-glance/create-a-revalidate-job?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs

**Keywords:** Revalidate Job, Creating Revalidate Job, revalidate job, revalidate rules, create revalidate job


Learn how to create a job that analyzes and validates entities or relationships against a set of data validation functions.

Before you create a revalidate job, you must create data validation functions for the job to analyze. For more information, see topic [Create DVFs in the Data Modeler](https://docs.reltio.com/en/objectives/cleanse-and-verify-data/data-cleansing-at-a-glance/data-cleansing-operation/define-data-validation-functions/create-dvfs-in-the-data-modeler?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs)..

After you create or edit Data Validation Functions, use the **Tenant Management** to run a revalidate job for existing data in your tenant. This job runs the DVFs for all entities and relationships of the specified type.to run a revalidate job for existing data in your tenant. This job runs the DVFs for all entities and relationships of the specified type.


To create and run a revalidate job:

1. In Console, select the **Tenant Management** application.
2. In the **Tenant Management** navigation panel, select **Jobs**.
3. Select **Select a job**.
4. In the **Create new job** page, select **Revalidate** job.
   *Image: i-jobs-revalidate.png*
5. In the **Revalidate** menu, specify one or more of the following fields:
   - **Entity type:**: From this drop-down menu, select an entity type to run all the Data Validation Functions for all entities of this type.
   - **Entity URI list:**: Enter the URI list of only selected entities that you want to run all Data Validation Functions for.

> **Note:** If you specify both **Entity type** and **Entity URI list** fields, then Data Validation Functions run only on the URI list and ignore other Entity types in the request.
   - **Relationship type:** From this drop-down menu, select a relationship type to run all the Data Validation Functions for all relationships of this type.
   - **Relationship URI list:** Enter the URI list of only selected relationships that you want to run all data validation functions for.

> **Note:** If you select both **Relationship type** and **Relationship URI list** fields, Data Validation Functions run only on the URI list and ignore other Relationship types in the request.
   *Image: i-jobs-create_new.png*
   If you run the revalidate job on entities and relationships at the same time, the **Jobs** page displays two separated job entries.
6. Select **Run Job**. A notification appears indicating that an email will be sent once the job is completed.
7. While the job is processing, it appears in the **Pending** tab. To pause or stop the revalidate job, at the top of the **Revalidate** panel on the right, select the **pause** or **stop** icon.
   *Image: i-jobs-processing.png*
8. Select the **Completed** tab to view the details of the completed revalidate jobs.
   *Image: i-jobs-completed.png*

# Run a Delete tenant data job

> **Section:** Applications > Console > Tenant management applications > Tenant Management at a glance > Jobs at a glance > Delete tenant data


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/console/tenant-management-applications/tenant-management-at-a-glance/jobs-at-a-glance/delete-tenant-data/run-a-delete-tenant-data-job?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs

**Keywords:** delete tenant data, delete tenant data job, ROLE_ADMIN_TENANT, ROLE_ADMIN_CUSTOMER, tenant management job


Learn how to run the Delete tenant data job.

You must have a role with access to the tenant and the appropriate permissions to delete data. For details, see [Delete tenant data](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/console/tenant-management-applications/tenant-management-at-a-glance/jobs-at-a-glance/delete-tenant-data?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs). . The **Delete tenant data** job runs only on development or test tenants. If you want to delete data from a production tenant, [request Support](https://docs.reltio.com/en/reltio/whats-in-the-box/whats-in-the-box-at-a-glance/technical-assistance-at-a-glance/technical-assistance-operations/get-help-in-support-portal?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).

If you want to delete data in a development or testing tenant and replace it with new data, run the **Delete tenant data** job in the **Console Tenant Management** application.

Ensure no other jobs are running before you start a **Delete tenant data** job. Once you start this job, all other tenant management jobs are locked, so you cannot run them until this job is complete. You can run only one **Delete tenant data** job at a time. If you try to run another **Delete tenant data** job before the current job is completed, you receive a notification to either wait for the job to complete or stop that job to run a new **Delete tenant** data job.

*Image: tenant-delete-job.png*


To run a delete tenant data job:

1. From the **Applications** menu, select **Console** application. For more information, see [Console](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/console/console-at-a-glance?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).
2. From the **Tenant Management** section, select the **Tenant Management** application.
3. At the top of the page, from the **Select tenant** drop-down menu, select the tenant you want to work with. For more information, see [Selecting a tenant](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/platform/platform-at-a-glance/platform-navigation/select-a-tenant?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).
4. On the left navigation bar, select **Jobs**.
5. In the right pane, select **SELECT A JOB**.
   *Image: tenant-delete-job-select.png*
6. In the **Create new job** page, select the **Delete Tenant data** job.
7. In the displayed **Delete Tenant data** pane:
   *Image: tenant-delete-job-select-job.png*
   - Select one or both of the following options:
     - **Tenant data**:Delete all data (entities, attributes, relationships, interactions, graphs) currently in use in your tenant.
     - **Activity Log**: Delete all historical data from your tenant. For compliance reasons, you must delete the data before you can delete the Activity Log from the tenant, so this option is enabled only if you select the **Tenant data** option.
   - Select **DELETE DATA**, which is enabled only after you select the **Tenant data** option.
8. In the displayed confirmation window:
   *Image: tenant-delete-job-select-job-delete.png*
   - In the entry field type `DELETE`.
   - Select the confirmation check box.
   - Select **CONTINUE TO DELETE**.
9. In the **PENDING** tab in the **+ SELECT A JOB** page, select your user name to view the status of your job:
   - **Not started**: The job hasn't started yet.
   - **Processing**: The job has stared.
10. In the **COMPLETED** tab, select your user name to view the status of your completed job:
   - **Completed**: The job completed successfully.
   - **Failed**: The job was not able to complete. If you see a job failed notification, contact Reltio Customer Engineering for assistance (for more information, see [Get help in Support Portal](https://docs.reltio.com/en/reltio/whats-in-the-box/whats-in-the-box-at-a-glance/technical-assistance-at-a-glance/technical-assistance-operations/get-help-in-support-portal?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs)).

*Image: tenant-delete-job-select-job-failed.png*

Let's cover Console tenant management applications. Get the overview here, then see the subtopics in this section to get to the details.

## What are Tenant Management applications?

Tenant Management applications are a suite of tools in the Reltio Console for overseeing, monitoring, and optimizing your Reltio tenant's operations. These applications enable you to manage performance, monitor usage, and handle data sharing, exports, and imports, and leverage external data matching tools.

## Who are Tenant Management applications for?

This content is curated for these Reltio user roles:

Data Product OwnerData StewardReltio ConfiguratorSystem Administrator

## Why would I use Tenant Management applications?

Use Tenant Management applications to maintain and optimize your Reltio tenant. These tools provide administrators and data stewards with capabilities to monitor tenant health, analyze resource usage, execute bulk data operations, and share trusted data securely with external cloud data warehouses.

## When would I use Tenant Management applications?

You would use Tenant Management applications in scenarios like these:

- Monitoring tenant performance and identifying potential bottlenecks.
- Tracking resource usage with detailed usage reports.
- Sharing AI-ready and trusted data in near-real-time with cloud data warehouses.
- Exporting tenant data for external analysis or archiving.
- Loading bulk data into your tenant.
- Performing external matching to resolve duplicate records against third-party data sources.

## Where do I find Tenant Management applications?

Reltio Entity ResolutionReltio Multidomain MDMReltio Intelligent 360

Tenant Management applications are accessible from the Reltio Console, for details see [Tenant Management applications navigation](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/console/tenant-management-applications/tenant-management-applications-at-a-glance/tenant-management-applications-navigation?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).

# Get started with performance monitoring

> **Section:** Applications > Console > Tenant management applications > Usage Reporting at a glance > API usage


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/console/tenant-management-applications/usage-reporting-at-a-glance/api-usage/get-started-with-performance-monitoring?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs

**Keywords:** get started with performance monitoring, api performance dashboard, access the Performance Monitoring application, API Performance Dashboard, Get Started with Performance Monitoring, Access the Performance Monitoring Application


Learn how to monitor API performance with the **Performance Monitoring** application using data displayed in the different dashboards of the application.

Let’s take a look at the data you can obtain from the **Performance Monitoring** dashboards:

- **API performance summary** dashboard: the total number of API requests that are sent over a specific date range, average and median API latency, percentage of successful API requests, and failed API request details.
- **API usage** dashboard: the number of times a specific HTTP request method is used.
- **API latency** dashboard: the APIs that created peaks or troughs on a specific date range and their usage.
- **Authentication API usage** dashboard: the performance of the authentication API.

We’ll provide more details on these dashboards in topic [API perfomance monitoring dashboards](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/console/tenant-management-applications/usage-reporting-at-a-glance/api-usage/api-perfomance-monitoring-dashboards?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs). But first let’s find out how to get to them.

**To access the Performance Monitoring application:**

1. In the **App Selector** icon, select **Console**.
2. In the **Console** home page, under the **Tenant Management** section, select **Performance Monitoring**. For more information, see topic [Console](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/console/console-at-a-glance?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).

   *Image: pm_banner.png*
3. At the top of the page, from the **Select tenant** dropdown menu, select the tenant you want to work with. For more information, see topic [Selecting a tenant](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/platform/platform-at-a-glance/platform-navigation/select-a-tenant?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).

You use these key sections of the **API performance dashboards** to determine the data to display and analyze displayed data.

*Image: pm.png*

***Image: pm_selectentity.png***Select tenant:****

A dropdown menu at the top of the **Console** page. This provides a list of available tenants. For more information, see topic [Select a tenant](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/platform/platform-at-a-glance/platform-navigation/select-a-tenant?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).

***Image: pm_titlebar.png***Navigation Pane:****

For more information, see topic [Specify a date range](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/console/tenant-management-applications/usage-reporting-at-a-glance/api-usage/specify-a-date-range?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).

# API latency dashboard

> **Section:** Applications > Console > Tenant management applications > Usage Reporting at a glance > API usage


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/console/tenant-management-applications/usage-reporting-at-a-glance/api-usage/api-latency-dashboard?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs

**Keywords:** api latency, http method, gear, percentile, HTTP Method, API Latency, Gear, Percentile


Learn about the data in the **API latency** dashboard in the **Performance Monitoring** application.

The **Performance Monitoring** application enables you to monitor the APIs in your Reltio tenant. After specifying a date range and selecting the HTTP methods and APIs you want to monitor, you can determine if the API that created a peak on a specific date is regularly used or not.

By default, this dashboard displays the average latency value and the median API latency value of all API requests sent during the specified date range. You can also view the number of API requests that are in the 90th, 95th, and 99th percentiles by clicking the **Gear** icon and selecting the relevant check box. It also contains the HTTP method and API endpoint filter components.

*Image: pm_latency.png*

## Data definition

This dashboard provides the following metrics:

| Data label | Data definition |
| --- | --- |
| API latency trend | A line graph that shows the average latency value and median API latency value of all API requests sent during the specified date range. You can also view the number of API requests that are in the 90th, 95th, and 99th percentiles by clicking the **Gear** icon and selecting the relevant check box. |

## Data analysis scenarios

So, armed with these amazing metrics, what can you deduce about your data?

## Find the slowest API

You can use the HTTP method and API filters to determine the exact API that created the peak. The latency value of this API will be the largest.

## Determine how often the slowest API is used

You can use the percentiles to know if the API that created the peak is regularly used or not.

# API performance summary dashboard

> **Section:** Applications > Console > Tenant management applications > Usage Reporting at a glance > API usage


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/console/tenant-management-applications/usage-reporting-at-a-glance/api-usage/api-performance-summary-dashboard?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs

**Keywords:** api performance summary, success rate, failed request, latency, api request, anamolies, API Performance Summary, Success Rate, Failed Request, Latency, API Request, Anamolies


Learn about the data in the **API performance summary** dashboard in the **Performance Monitoring** application.

You monitor APIs in your Reltio tenant in the **Performance Monitoring** application in the **Console**. After specifying a date range, you can analyze the API request status, API latency, API success rate, and the number of failed API requests date range.

*Image: pm_apiperformance.png*

## Data definition

This dashboard provides the following metrics:

| Data label | Data definition |
| --- | --- |
| **Usage** | A summary chart of API usage for the date range specified in the a Data Picker (for more information, see topic [Specify a date range](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/console/tenant-management-applications/usage-reporting-at-a-glance/api-usage/specify-a-date-range?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs):  - **Usage:** The chart title, which links directly to the [API usage dashboard](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/console/tenant-management-applications/usage-reporting-at-a-glance/api-usage/api-usage-dashboard?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs). - **Total requests:** The total number of API requests that have been sent and a percentage increase (*Image: pm_uparrow.png*) or decrease (*Image: pm_downarrow.png*) over the past 90 days. - **Success rate:** The percentage of successful requests out of the total number sent. - **Failed requests:** The number of sent requests that failed. - **Trend line:** A color-coded graph indicating the status of the API request: Green = pass or Red=fail.      Click **Usage** to drill down to the [API usage dashboard](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/console/tenant-management-applications/usage-reporting-at-a-glance/api-usage/api-usage-dashboard?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs). |
| **Latency** | Two trend lines show the average and median API latency values respectively, for a specified time range. The latency value of an API is the time needed for an API to provide a response.Click **Latency** to drill down to the [API latency dashboard](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/console/tenant-management-applications/usage-reporting-at-a-glance/api-usage/api-latency-dashboard?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs). **Note:** The number of API requests are measured differently for average and median latency values. Average latency is latency for 50% of API requests and median latency is 50% of the latency value. |
| **Daily success rate** | A bar graph that shows the success rate trend for API calls over a specified time range. The threshold value is identified using a horizontal orange line that goes across the bar graph. The threshold value is dynamic and changes depending on the tenant that is used.**Tip:** Hover your mouse pointer over the vertical blue bars to display a tooltip with the success rate and threshold value for a specific day. |
| **Failed requests** | A table that shows number of times an API request failed and the corresponding error code. |

## Data analysis scenarios

So, armed with these amazing metrics, what can you deduce about your data?

## API usage

You can find out the number of API requests sent over a period of time and how much the usage has dropped from a previous period of the same amount of time.*Image: pm_apiperformance_usage.png*

The arrow indicates that the number of requests sent for the last 90 days is lesser compared to the previous period of the same duration.

## View all failed requests

You can view at a glance the number of times a request failed.

## Look out for high-level anomalies

You can look for an unexpected rise or drop in the API latency value and API usage.

## See the total number of requests

You can view information about failed requests and the API success rate. For example, [this sample image](#r_apiperfmon_chart_summary/apiperformancesummary) tells you that the total number of requests sent for the last 90 days is 923,000, the number of failed requests is 8, and the success rate is 100% (rounded off value).

# API usage dashboard

> **Section:** Applications > Console > Tenant management applications > Usage Reporting at a glance > API usage


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/console/tenant-management-applications/usage-reporting-at-a-glance/api-usage/api-usage-dashboard?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs

**Keywords:** http method, peak, trough, resource consumption, api usage, HTTP Method, Peak, Trough, API Usage, Resource Consumption


Learn about the data in the API Usage dashboard in the Performance Monitoring application.

The **Performance Monitoring** application enables you to monitor the APIs in your Reltio tenant. After you specify a date range, HTTP methods, and APIs, the **Performance Monitoring** retrieves data from third-party data-monitoring tools and displays in the **API Usage** dashboard information such as which APIs showed a peak or trough in number of requests during a specific specified time period, which are used the most and by whom, and the capacity needed.

*Image: pm_apiusage.png*

## Data definition

This table lists and describes the metrics available in the **API Usage** dashboard.

| Data label | Data definition |
| --- | --- |
| API usage trend | A line graph that shows the number of times an API request is sent over the selected date range. |
| Most used APIs | A table that shows the latency value of the most frequently used APIs. |
| API usage by compute capacity | A table that shows the amount of resources taken by a specific API when the request is sent. |
| Most time-consuming APIs | A table that shows the APIs that take the most time to execute in descending order, along with the type of method and execution date. |

## Data analysis scenarios

So, armed with these amazing metrics, what can you deduce about your data?

## Manage Resource consumption

You can check the number of units consumed by an API and use this information to find the impact on data load times.

## Identify the most frequently used API and its consumption

You can get to know the most frequently used API and how much resources the API consumes when you send a request. APIs that consume a lot of resources are associated with peaks.

## Look out for high-level anomalies

You can look for anomalies like an unexpected API request that was sent. For example, your team was not expected to send any requests over the weekend, but a look at the API usage dashboard tells you that someone sent a request.

# Specify a date range

> **Section:** Applications > Console > Tenant management applications > Usage Reporting at a glance > API usage


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/console/tenant-management-applications/usage-reporting-at-a-glance/api-usage/specify-a-date-range?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs

**Keywords:** pick date and time, date picker, reset filters, select a date range, Date Picker, Pick Date and Time, Reset Filters, Select a Date Range


Learn how to select a specific date range for API performance data using the **Date Picker**.

By default, the **Performance Monitoring** application shows data for the previous week. You can change this to the date range you want to analyze in the **Date Picker**.

*Image: pm_datepicker_drilldown.png*

**To specify a date range for data to display:**

1. In the upper-right corner of the **Title bar**, select the **Date Picker** dropdown menu.*Image: pm_datepicker_drilldown2.png*
2. In the **Date Picker**, specify the date range in either of the following ways:
   1. In the left navigation pane, select a predefined date range:

- **This week:** the current week, Sunday through Saturday.
- **Last week:** the previous week, seven days before the previous Sunday. For example, if the current date is April 19 , then data from April 17th to April 10th is displayed.
- **Last 7 days:** the last 7 days, seven days before the current date. For example, if the current date is April 19th, then data from April 19th to April 12th is displayed.
- **Last 30 days:** the previous month, 30 days before and including the current date.
- **Last 90 days:** the previous three months, 90 days before and including the current date.
- **Last 12 months:** the previous year, 360 days before and including the current date.
- **This year (Jan - Today):** the current year, starting from January 1st until the current date.
   2. In the **Pick date and time** section, in the **From** and **To** fields, select the start and end dates.
3. Click **UPDATE**.
   The specific date range displays at the top right, and the selected dates are highlighted in the calendars in the **Pick date and time** section as shown in this example where all dates between March 1st st and April 19th are highlighted in light blue.
   *Image: pm_datepicker.png*
   > **Note:** You can specify a date range through the previous year. If there is no data available for a specified date range, you will see one or both of the following messages:
   > - *No data for this period for selected filter* in the chart that does not have data.
   > - *No data found for the selected period and filter values. Select a different time period or filter value* above the [filter chips](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/console/tenant-management-applications/usage-reporting-at-a-glance/api-usage/select-filters?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs). You can either click **RESET FILTERS** or the close icon to go back to the default setting and change the date range in the **Date Picker**.

# Select filters

> **Section:** Applications > Console > Tenant management applications > Usage Reporting at a glance > API usage


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/console/tenant-management-applications/usage-reporting-at-a-glance/api-usage/select-filters?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs

**Keywords:** filter by, reset filters, api usage, http method, latency, no data, Reset Filters, Fiter By, API Usage, HTTP Method, Latency, No Data


Learn about the filters you can use to filter API data in **Performance Monitoring** dashboard charts.

Use the **HTTP method** and **API endpoint** filters in the **API Usage** and **API Latency** dashboards to filter and select data based on the type of HTTP request method and API. You can view data for:

- All methods
- GET method
- POST method
- DELETE method
- PUT method
- One or more selected APIs

**To select the filters:**

1. In the **API Usage** or **API Latency** dashboard area, click a filter chip.
   *Image: pm_filterchips.png*
2. In the **Filter by** pane, select one or all HTTP methods and one or all APIs and click **APPLY**.
   *Image: pm_filterbypane.png*
   You use the filters to view data for the selected methods and APIs. By default, all HTTP methods are selected, and you can view all methods in the **Filter by** pane. If you deselect one of the methods, a **RESET FILTERS** button is enabled. Click this button to go back to the default setting.
   When you click the **HTTP method** filter, all available HTTP methods are displayed in the **Filter by** pane along with a counter that displays the number of times a request has been sent for each method.
   When you click the **HTTP method** filter, all available HTTP methods are displayed in the **Filter by** pane along with a counter that displays the number of times a request has been sent for each method.
   > **Note:** You must select at least one method.
   When you click the **API endpoint** filter, a **Search** bar is displayed. All available APIs are displayed in the **Filter by** pane along with a counter that displays the number of times a request has been sent for each method.
   When you click the **API endpoint** filter, a **Search** bar is displayed. All available APIs are displayed in the **Filter by** pane along with a counter that displays the number of times a request has been sent for each method.
   > **Note:** You must select at least one method.
   When you click the **API endpoint** filter, a **Search** bar is displayed. All available APIs are displayed in the **Filter by** pane along with a counter that displays the number of times a request has been sent for each API. Use the **Search** bar to search for a specific API.
   If you do not see any results for a specific date range, it means that no requests have been sent for the selected HTTP method and API. For example, if no requests have been sent during the previous week for the **GET** method and the **/entities** API, you will not see any results for the previous week.

# Console at a glance

> **Section:** Applications > Console


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/console/console-at-a-glance?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs


Learn how to configure Console application data, manage tenants, and secure user access within Reltio.

Take it from the top with Console. Get the overview here, then see the sub topics in this section to drill down to the details.

## What is Console?

Console is a self-service tool for configuring data models, setting up integrations, and managing user roles and permissions, empowering organizations to tailor the platform to their specific business needs.

## Who is Console for?

This content is curated for these Reltio user roles defined in topic [About roles](https://docs.reltio.com/en/roles/about-roles?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs):

Data Product OwnerData StewardDeveloperReltio ConfiguratorSolution ArchitectSystem Administrator

## Why would I use Console?

Console is perfect for users who prefer working through an intuitive interface rather than relying on technical expertise. It offers a streamlined, user-friendly platform that simplifies complex tasks, enabling self-service capabilities for configuration, workflow setup, and permission management.

Console is ideal for those who prefer to work in a User Interface.

Use Console for:

- 

  Configuring the data model: Manage entity types, attributes, relationship types, match rules, survivorship rules, data validation functions, and more, ensuring your data structure aligns with your business needs.
- 

  Setting up data integrations: Leverage the Reltio Integration Hub and Data Pipeline to establish integrations with source systems seamlessly.
- 

  Overseeing tenant management: Monitor performance and usage metrics to optimize your tenant's efficiency.
- Managing security settings: Handle user management, configure SSO, and manage client credentials to ensure secure and streamlined access.

- Centralized view of data assets: The console provides a single, centralized view of all of your data assets, making it easy to find and access the data you need.
- Simplified data discovery: The console's intuitive interface makes it easy to discover new data assets and learn about their contents.
- Powerful querying capabilities: The console provides powerful querying capabilities that allow you to quickly and easily extract the data you need.
- Seamless integration with other Reltio tools: The console seamlessly integrates with other Reltio tools, such as the data quality tool and the data governance tool, making it easy to manage and govern your data.

To configure, manage, and secure your data using APIs, see section [About developer resources](https://docs.reltio.com/en/developer-resources/about-developer-resources?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).

## When would I use Console?

Use Console to ensure that your data is accurate, consistent, and secure when you're:

- 

  preparing data for unification, including data cleansing, data transformation, and data enrichment.
- 

  unifying data, including data matching, data merging, and data deduplication.
- 

  governing data, including data quality rules, data lineage, and data security.

## Where do I find Console?

Console is available from the Applications menu in your Reltio tenant. For more information, see topic [Console navigation](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/console/console-at-a-glance/console-navigation?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).

# Bulk match review navigation

> **Section:** Applications > Hub > Bulk match review at a glance


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/hub/bulk-match-review-at-a-glance/bulk-match-review-navigation?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs


Learn how to find your way around with Bulk match review

> **Note:** This feature is available to limited users through the Reltio Early Access (EA) program. Interested in finding out more about this feature or participating in our EA program? Get details in topic Early Access (EA) features.

Reltio Multidomain MDMReltio Intelligent 360

Let's take you around the **Bulk match review** neighborhood.

## Bulk match review access

Access **Bulk match review** from here in the UI: **Applications > Hub > Bulk match**. For general information on using the left navigation drawer in the Hub, see topic [Hub navigation](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/hub/hub-at-a-glance/hub-navigation?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).

> **Note:** The **Bulk match** option appears in the left navigation pane only after [you enable](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/hub/bulk-match-review-at-a-glance/enable-bulk-match-in-a-tenant?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs) it in **UI Modeler**.

If `No results found` is displayed, use Search to select a specific profile whose potential matches you want to review. For more information, see section [Search at a glance](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/hub/search-at-a-glance?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).

## Bulk match review anatomy

The **Bulk match** page contains tabs for the entity types defined for the specified profile, for example, Location, Individual, Organization, and Household.

To review potential matches in bulk, select one or more check boxes from the **Profile** column. The **Match Review** bar then prompts you to choose between:

- **MERGE ALL**, or
- **NOT A MATCH**.

  > **Attention:** The maximum number of profile pairs you can apply **MERGE ALL** or **NOT A MATCH** to in a single request is 25.

*Image: ui_bulkmatchmain.png*

For instructions on how to perform your data unification and management tasks using this application, see [Review and resolve matches in bulk](https://docs.reltio.com/en/objectives/manage-profiles/profile-management-at-a-glance/profile-management-operation/review-and-resolve-matches-in-bulk?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).

## Filter Operational Values (OVs)

The **Show only OV** filter is enabled by default, so you'll see only the surviving values determined by your survivorship configuration.

To adjust this view, use the **Settings** icon in the top-right corner. If you clear the checkbox, the grid will display all attribute values from contributing crosswalks. This is useful if you want to investigate data variations or match contexts more deeply.*Image: i-apps-bulk-match-ovs-filter.png*

Enabling this setting again will refocus the view on only the OVs, simplifying the review process for **Bulk match review** decisions.

# Bulk match review at a glance

> **Section:** Applications > Hub


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/hub/bulk-match-review-at-a-glance?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs


Get a high-level view of Bulk match reviews and actions feature in the Hub.

> **Note:** This feature is available to limited users through the Reltio Early Access (EA) program. Interested in finding out more about this feature or participating in our EA program? Get details in topic Early Access (EA) features.

## What is it?

**Bulk match review** helps you resolve duplicate records efficiently. Instead of reviewing matches one at a time, review multiple potential matches in a single session and use pagination to move through additional pairs as needed.

Use filtering options to narrow down the list of potential matches and decide which records to merge or exclude. The feature ensures consistent data quality and speeds up match resolution tasks.

## Who is it for?

This content is curated for these Reltio user roles defined in topic [About roles](https://docs.reltio.com/en/roles/about-roles?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs):

Data Steward

## Why would I use it?

Duplicate records are common in organizations managing data across multiple systems. Often, the same entity appears in multiple records, with inconsistencies between them. In the **Hub**, when you open a profile, the **Potential Matches** tab lets you select and view a list of potential matches for the selected record. From there, you can either merge the records or mark them as not a match.

This, however, is a tedious process since you match records for an individual entity and its associated potential matches one by one. You have to navigate to each profile, view its potential matches, and then merge them. This takes time, especially if you are dealing with a large amount of data.

Wouldn't it be more efficient if you can view a list of existing entities and merge records which you think are the same, with just a click of a button?

That's exactly what the **Bulk match review** feature offers. For a selected entity type, you can merge or mark records as "Not a Match" in bulk, saving you time and effort.

The topics in this section provide a guided tour of the **Bulk match review** UI, describing where to access this application, what its key components are, and how to use its fields and controls. This, in a nutshell, is why you should use this feature:

**Save Time**

Process large groups of potential matches in one go.

**Enhance Data Quality**

Maintain accurate and reliable records.

**Simplify Workflows**

Use bulk actions to reduce repetitive tasks.

For instructions on how to perform your data unification and management tasks using **Bulk match review**, see [Review and resolve matches in bulk](https://docs.reltio.com/en/objectives/manage-profiles/profile-management-at-a-glance/profile-management-operation/review-and-resolve-matches-in-bulk?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).

## When would I use it?

Use **Bulk match review** when you want to:

- Resolve duplicate records after data ingestion or cleansing.
- Manage match resolution at scale to reduce backlogs.

## When can't I use it?

**Bulk match review** is not supported for matches originating from these sources:

- Reltio Integration for Salesforce or Reltio Enrichment with D&B with a third-party Data Tenant Subscription Service (DTSS)
- Reltio Enrichment with D&B (Data Blocks) or Reltio Enrichment with ZoomInfo

## Where do I find Bulk match review?

Reltio Multidomain MDMReltio Intelligent 360

Access it in the **Hub** application by selecting the **Bulk match** icon on the left sidebar. 

> **Note:** The **Bulk match** option appears in the left navigation pane only after you [enable](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/hub/bulk-match-review-at-a-glance/enable-bulk-match-in-a-tenant?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs) it in the UI configuration file.

# Enable Bulk match in a tenant

> **Section:** Applications > Hub > Bulk match review at a glance


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/hub/bulk-match-review-at-a-glance/enable-bulk-match-in-a-tenant?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs

**Keywords:** enable bulk match tenant, enable bulk match review, configure bulk match screen, add bulk match navigation, update ui configuration file, import and publish ui config, uimodeler, layout, navigation


Learn how to update the UI configuration file to add Bulk match to the left navigation so that users can open Bulk match review in Hub.

> **Note:** This feature is available to limited users through the Reltio Early Access (EA) program. Interested in finding out more about this feature or participating in our EA program? Get details in topic Early Access (EA) features.

[Bulk Match](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/hub/bulk-match-review-at-a-glance?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs) enables matching operations across large datasets directly from the Hub. To enable this feature for a specific tenant, update the UI configuration file through the UI Modeler.

**Prerequisites**- 

  You have access to the [Console](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/console/console-at-a-glance?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs) application in your tenant.
- 

  You have a backup copy of the current UI configuration file.


To enable the bulk match feature in your tenant

1. In the **Console**, select **UI Modeler**.
2. From the left navigation menu, select **Import/Export UI Config Files**. The **Import/export UI Config files** page is displayed.
   *Image: import-export-ui_new.png*
3. Select the `config.json` file by clicking on the checkbox next to it.
4. Click **Export**. The file is exported to your local file system.
   - Open the downloaded JSON file in a text editor.
   - In the `layout` section, locate the `items` array, and add the following code;
     ```
{
  "label": "Bulk match",
  "icon": "https://reltio-ui-files.s3.amazonaws.com/new-ui/BulkMatch.svg",
  "class": "BulkMatch"
}
```
   - Save the file.
5. In the **UI Modeler**, select the same configuration file, and then select **Import & Replace**. The **Select file** page is displayed.
   *Image: uimod_importfile.png*
   - In the **Browse File** field, select the updated configuration file that must be imported and replaced.
   - Click **Continue**. The **Review** page is displayed where you can review the changes.
   - Select **Replace**. This action will replace the current configuration with the Imported configuration file.
6. Select **Publish**.

The changes in the configuration file are published. The **Bulk Match** option appears in the left navigation pane in the option appears in the left navigation pane in the **Hub**. .

# Use quick filters in Bulk match review

> **Section:** Applications > Hub > Bulk match review at a glance


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/hub/bulk-match-review-at-a-glance/use-quick-filters-in-bulk-match-review?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs

Learn how to apply and manage filters in Bulk Match review using the quick filters panel

> **Note:** This feature is available to limited users through the Reltio Early Access (EA) program. Interested in finding out more about this feature or participating in our EA program? Get details in topic Early Access (EA) features.

**Prerequisites**

You must have access to **Bulk Match review** in the **Hub**.

The attributes used for filtering must be marked as `"faceted": true` in your tenant configuration. For more information, see [Using Quick Filters](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/search/search-at-a-glance/search-operation/using-quick-filters?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).

The quick filters panel allows you to filter match results by selecting attribute values. Filters are applied instantly and remain saved across sessions. For more information, see [Quick filters panel in Bulk match review](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/hub/bulk-match-review-at-a-glance/quick-filters-panel-in-bulk-match-review?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs)..


To apply filters:

1. Select the **Bulk Match** from the left-side panel in the **Hub**.*Image: i-apps-bulk-match-start.png*
2. In the left-side panel, select one or more values from **Entity types**. The results update automatically on the right-side panel.*Image: i-apps-bulk-match-quick-filters-1.png*
3. Select **ADVANCED SEARCH** to specify your filtering requirements.
   - In the **Advanced search** page, select or enter the filtering attributes as applicable. *Image: i-apps-bulk-match-quick-filters-2.png*
     *Image: UI_Bulkmatch_example.png*
   - Optional: Use the **Apply to both profiles** checkbox to control how the filter is applied.*Image: i-apps-bulk-match-quick-filters-5.png*
     - When checked (default), both profiles in the match pair must meet the attribute condition.
- When unchecked, only the leading profile must meet the condition.
   - Select **APPLY** to create the search filter.*Image: i-apps-bulk-match-quick-filters-3.png*
     *Image: i-apps-bulk-match-quick-filters-4.png*

**Result**

The match results are filtered based on the selected values. Your last filters are saved and applied automatically the next time you return to the page.

> **Tip:** After you're done using the quick filters to narrow your results, collapse the panel to expand your workspace and view more profile match details side by side.



To use quick filters in the**Bulk Match** page, see this video. *Image: i-apps-bulk-match-quick-filters-collapse.gif*

# Data Model at a glance

> **Section:** Applications > Hub


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/hub/data-model-at-a-glance?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs


Learn about the Data Model feature for Reltio Reltio Intelligent 360 in the Reltio Hub.

Reltio Intelligent 360

The Reltio Intelligent 360 hub provides an option for you to easily and quickly visualize the data model on your tenant.

Open the **Data Model** page to see a graphic representation of how your tenant's entities, relationships, and interactions relate to each other.

View the number of entities, relationships and interactions on the top left corner of the page, and zoom in/out with the button on the bottom right corner of the page. Additionally, on the top right side select the **Hide Interaction types** checkbox to show or hide the interaction types.

*Image: dp_dmg_overview.png*

## Entity types

Entity types are represented as round icons.

Select an entity, and click the **i** (info) button on the top right corner of the page, to open a side panel containing additional information about the selected entity. Additionally, the selected entity, its related entities and the connecting edges, remain highlighted while all other elements of the graph dim.

*Image: dp_dmg_entity_view.png*

**Entity name menu**

Displays the name of the selected entity and a dropdown menu for you to select other entities.

**Description**

Displays the description of the selected entity.

**Overview**

Displays information about the number of profiles, attributes, relationships and interactions associated with the selected entity.

**Contributing sources**

Displays the sources that contributed to the data associated with the selected entity.

Select the **attribute table view** button on the top right corner of the page to view other details about the selected entity in the information panel.

*Image: dp_dmg_entity_table.png*

**Attributes**

Displays the attributes and sub-attributes configured for the selected entity. It also displays a search bar for you to easily find the attribute you want.

**Data type**

Displays information about the data type of each attribute and sub-attribute configured for the selected entity.

**Description**

Displays the name and a small description of the each attribute and sub-attribute configured for the selected entity.

**Contributing sources**

Displays the sources that contributed to each attribute and sub-attribute configured for the selected entity.

## Relationship types

Relationship types are represented by the lines or edges that connect entity types.

An entity can have more than one relationship, which is denoted by a number on the line connecting the two entities. Select the number, and a dropdown list appears for you with the list of relationships.

Select the relationship you want to analyze and click the **i** (info) button on the top right corner of the page, to view more details in the side panel. Additionally, the relationship you selected and all related entities, remain highlighted while all other elements of the graph dim.

*Image: dp_dmg_relation_view.png*

**Relationship name menu**

Displays the name of the selected relationship and a dropdown menu for you to select other relationships.

**Description**

Displays the description of the selected relationship.

**Overview**

Displays information about the number of attributes associated with the selected relationship.

**Direction**

Displays the two entities that compose this relationship as well as the label of the relationship.

Select the **attribute table view** button on the top right corner of the page to view other details about the relationship.

*Image: dp_dmg_relation_table.png*

**Attributes**

Displays the attributes and sub-attributes configured for the selected relationship.

**Data type**

Displays information about the data type of each attribute and sub-attribute configured for the selected relationship.

## Interaction types

Interaction types are represented by round icons with dotted lines.

Select an interaction, and click the **i** (info) button on the top right corner of the page, to open a side panel that displays additional information.. Additionally, the interaction you selected and its related entities remain highlighted while all other elements of the graph dim.

*Image: dp_dmg_interaction_view.png*

**Interaction name menu**

Displays the name of the selected interaction and a dropdown menu for you to select other interactions.

**Description**

Displays the description of the selected interaction.

**Overview**

Displays information about the number of attributes associated with the selected interaction.

**Member type**

Displays the names of the entities that are members of the selected interaction.

Select the **attribute table view** button on the top right corner of the page to view more details about the interaction in the information panel.

*Image: dp_dmg_interaction_table.png*

**Attributes**

Displays the attributes and sub-attributes configured for the selected interaction.

**Data type**

Displays information about the data type of each attribute and sub-attribute configured for the selected interaction.

Reltio Multidomain MDMReltio Intelligent 360

The Data Quality dashboard in the Hub has over a dozen charts providing metrics on entities and attributes that give you a complete picture of your data in real time. Configure KPIs, metrics, and key data points in charts to display the data you want to monitor in the dashboard.

Use these key areas of the Data quality dashboard UI to determine the data to display in the DQ Dashboard.

**Entity type bar**
