# Append interactions using Groupkeys

> **Section:** Applications > Hub > Profiles at a glance > Profile perspectives tabs > Profile perspectives navigation > Interactions perspective > Interactions perspective navigation


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/hub/profiles-at-a-glance/profile-perspectives-tabs/profile-perspectives-navigation/interactions-perspective/interactions-perspective-navigation/append-interactions-using-groupkeys?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs

**Keywords:** groupkey-based interaction update, append interaction with groupkey, retain interaction history, configure groupkey for interactions, latest interaction record display, interaction audit log, profile interactions tab, data modeler interaction configuration, groupkey, interaction update, retention, hub


Learn about using group keys to version and manage evolving interactions while preserving history and audit compliance.

In many industries, such as hospitality, healthcare, and telecommunications, customers frequently modify existing interactions. A hotel guest might change the length of a stay, upgrade a room, or cancel a reservation, all under the same booking ID. Traditionally, each of these updates is sent to Reltio as a new interaction, which clutters the profile view and prevents users from easily identifying the current status of an interaction.

The **Append interactions** feature tracks updates to a transaction, like a hotel booking, without altering the original. It lets you define a specific attribute (such as a booking ID or appointment ID) as a `GroupKey`, allowing Reltio to treat a series of related interaction updates as part of a single logical thread. In the Hub UI, you will see only the latest version of the interaction for each `GroupKey`, while earlier updates remain accessible in an audit log. This approach preserves full history without overwhelming the interface or the user. Here's an example:

Mark books a hotel room. Over the next few days, he:

1. Extends his stay
2. Upgrades to a premium suite
3. He later downgrades to a standard room

Each of these updates is sent to Reltio as a new interaction, but all share the same booking ID as their `GroupKey`. In the **Hub**, the **Interactions** tab shows only the final (downgraded) version. The earlier updates are available in the log panel for full traceability. If you're a data steward, you can review these interactions and understand how they've changed over time.

To work with this feature, you must first enable a grouping attribute for an interaction type. For more information, see topic [Create an Interaction type](https://docs.reltio.com/en/objectives/model-data/data-modeling-at-a-glance/data-modeling-operation/configure-interaction-types/create-an-interaction-type?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).

Learn more about interaction grouping in the [Interaction](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/hub/profiles-at-a-glance/profile-perspectives-tabs/profile-perspectives-navigation/interactions-perspective/interactions-perspective-navigation/append-interactions-using-groupkeys/view-groupkey-based-interactions?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs) tab.

# Interactions perspective navigation

> **Section:** Applications > Hub > Profiles at a glance > Profile perspectives tabs > Profile perspectives navigation > Interactions perspective


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/hub/profiles-at-a-glance/profile-perspectives-tabs/profile-perspectives-navigation/interactions-perspective/interactions-perspective-navigation?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs


Learn how to find your way around with Interactions.

Reltio Intelligent 360

## Interactions access

Access Interactions from here in the UI: **Applications > Hub > Search > Profile > Interactions**.

## Interactions anatomy

From the **Interactions** tab of a selected profile, selecting a specific interaction type from the drop-down and focus on the interaction data that matters to you. Let us explore this view in detail.

The selected Interaction type and the number of interactions available for that interaction type are listed.

*Image: interaction-selected-type.png*

By default, the **All interaction types** option is selected, so all the interactions available for the entity is displayed. All the interactions are displayed in reverse chronological order by default. The most recent activity is listed first, followed by each activity that occurred before that.

Use the filter option to filter the interactions further. For details, see the topic [Apply filter options on attributes](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/hub/profiles-at-a-glance/profile-perspectives-tabs/profile-perspectives-navigation/interactions-perspective/interactions-perspective-navigation/interactions-table-in-profile-view/apply-filter-options-on-attributes?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).

> **Note:** You can select any of the members in the interaction and it opens the respective profiles.



If there are more than three attributes, select the**View more** link to view more details about the interaction.

Additionally, you can set the number of rows that you want to view by changing the **Rows per page** value at the bottom of the page. Set it to either 10, 15, 25, 50, or 100 rows per page. Use the left and right arrows to navigate to the previous and next pages.

*Image: interaction-main-page.png*

# View Groupkey based interactions

> **Section:** Applications > Hub > Profiles at a glance > Profile perspectives tabs > Profile perspectives navigation > Interactions perspective > Interactions perspective navigation > Append interactions using Groupkeys


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/hub/profiles-at-a-glance/profile-perspectives-tabs/profile-perspectives-navigation/interactions-perspective/interactions-perspective-navigation/append-interactions-using-groupkeys/view-groupkey-based-interactions?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs

**Keywords:** view grouped interactions in hub, how to filter interactions by groupkey, access interaction history in reltio, view latest interaction by groupkey, groupkey interaction version history, interaction tab filtering options, audit trail for grouped interactions, interaction version tracking, groupkey, audit, filtering, interactions


Learn how grouped interactions are displayed, how the latest version is highlighted, and how to access the full audit history.

When `GroupKey` based interaction updates are enabled for a classified interaction type, the **Interactions tab** on a profile displays a simplified list where each row represents the **most recent interaction** for a unique `GroupKey` value (for example, a Booking ID or Case ID). This reduces clutter and improves readability without losing historical visibility. For more information about grouped interactions, see topics [Append interactions using Groupkeys](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/hub/profiles-at-a-glance/profile-perspectives-tabs/profile-perspectives-navigation/interactions-perspective/interactions-perspective-navigation/append-interactions-using-groupkeys?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs) and [Create an Interaction type](https://docs.reltio.com/en/objectives/model-data/data-modeling-at-a-glance/data-modeling-operation/configure-interaction-types/create-an-interaction-type?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).

To view interactions based on group keys:

1. 

   In the **Hub**, search and select an entity whose interactions you want to view.
2. *Image: ui-appendinteractionshub.png*

   In the **Profile** view, select the **Interactions** tab.

   This tab lists all interactions for the selected profile. Since the interactions are based on a group key, the list displays only the latest interaction per `GroupKey`. Interactions are sorted by timestamp (most recent first). Each entry displays summary details like status, type, participants, and last updated time.
3. From the dropdown, select an interaction type to view related interactions.
4. Select the Filter icon to filter interactions for a specified period or a specified interaction type.
5. Select the Log icon available next to each interaction. *Image: ui-appendinteractionauditlog.png*

   View the full version history for the selected interaction. Earlier versions are listed with their timestamp along with the details of attribute values added, removed, or modified.

# Interactions table in Profile view

> **Section:** Applications > Hub > Profiles at a glance > Profile perspectives tabs > Profile perspectives navigation > Interactions perspective > Interactions perspective navigation


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/hub/profiles-at-a-glance/profile-perspectives-tabs/profile-perspectives-navigation/interactions-perspective/interactions-perspective-navigation/interactions-table-in-profile-view?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs


Learn about the Interactions table in the Profile view.

An interaction represents an event (or transaction) that occurs at a particular moment, such as, making a retail purchase, opening an email, opening a support case, or, visiting a website. Interactions can be associated with multiple entities (actors), have an interaction type, and have associated attributes. Effectively, interactions represent transactional data associated with an entity.

The Interactions table displays only the interaction types and attributes permitted for your role. For more information, see [Interaction permissions](https://docs.reltio.com/en/developer-resources/system-administration-apis/system-administration-apis-at-a-glance/configuration-api/role-based-security/metadata-security?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).

Configure your **Profile view** to include the **Interactions view table**. Update your UI configuration file to add the configuration for interactions, for example:

```
{
                     "id": "com.reltio.plugins.entity.InteractionsTable",
                     "component": "InteractionsTable",
                     "caption": "Interactions view table",
                     "interactionType": "configuration/interactionTypes/Meeting"
                  },
```

Specify an interaction type in the configuration to view only interactions of that type in the table. If you don't specify an interaction type, the table displays details for all types.

Here's a sample **Interaction view table** in the **Profile view**:

*Image: dp_profile_interactionstable.png*

In the interactions table, view the date and the actors involved in the interaction. The interactions are displayed in reverse chronological order by default. The most recent activity is listed first, followed by each activity that occurred before that.

Manage interactions by using the search and filter options. Show or hide attributes for interactions and focus on the value of the interaction data that matters to you.

## Search interactions

Select the Search icon to open the search bar and specify the criteria to search for interactions in the table.

*Image: dp_profile_interactionssearch.png* For example, you can search by the member label, that is the name of the actor. Select the Search icon and enter the name of the entity. The interactions list is updated to display only those interactions with the specified entity name.

## Filter interactions

Select the Filter icon to view the details of only the required interactions. When you click the Filter icon, the filter icon changes and the filter drop-down is displayed next to the column name in the table.

For example, let us view interactions that occurred on a specific date, say the 16th of July. Select the dropdown in the **Date** column. Select the arrow next to the **On** operator to see the list of operators based on the attribute or column you are filtering upon.

*Image: dp_profile_interactionsfilter.png*

Select the **On** operator and select the calendar to select the date, that is 16th July. Select **Enter** and the interaction table filters to display all interactions for the 16th of July.

## Show/hide columns

Select **Show/hide columns** to add or remove columns from the table. Selecting this option displays a list of available columns, as shown below:

*Image: dp_profile_interactionsshowhide.png* From this list, select the columns to be added or removed.

# Apply filter options on attributes

> **Section:** Applications > Hub > Profiles at a glance > Profile perspectives tabs > Profile perspectives navigation > Interactions perspective > Interactions perspective navigation > Interactions table in Profile view


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/hub/profiles-at-a-glance/profile-perspectives-tabs/profile-perspectives-navigation/interactions-perspective/interactions-perspective-navigation/interactions-table-in-profile-view/apply-filter-options-on-attributes?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs


Learn how to apply filter options on attributes.

The filter feature helps you view the details of only the required interactions.


To apply filter options:

1. In the **Hub**, select a profile, and select the **Interactions** tab.
2. Select the filter icon (*Image: interaction-filter-icon.png*) on the **Interactions** page.
   *Image: interaction-filter-options.png*
3. In the Filter options window, select the **Within the last** option to filter the available interactions within a specific time. Specify the number of **Minutes**, **Hours**, **Days**, **Weeks**, **Months**, or **Years** using this option. Enter the value and select any of these options.
   Alternatively, select the **Date range** option to filter the interactions available within a specific date range. For example, 05/18/2024 - 05/25/2024 as shown in the sample image.
4. Select the interaction type from the drop-down to filter the interactions based on attributes. For example, **Generic Interaction** as selected in the sample image.
5. Select the the attribute for the selected interaction type from the drop-down. For example, **Interaction ID** as selected in the sample image.
   > **Note:** All the attributes available for the selected interaction type are available in the **Select attribute** drop-down.
6. Select further filter options for the selected attribute. Select any of these options – **Equals**, **Not**, **Exists**, **Full text**, **Has all**, **Missing value**, **Starts with**, **Count equals**, **Count not equal**, **Count less**, **Count less or equal**, **Count greater**, **Count greater or equal**, **Count in range**, or **Contains**. For example, **Equals** as selected in the sample image.
   > **Note:** You can add more filter options, copy the existing filter options, or delete the filter options by selecting*Image: interaction-filter-options-add.png*, *Image: interaction-filter-options-copy.png*, or *Image: interaction-filter-options-delete.png* respectively.
7. Select **APPLY** to apply the filter and view the interactions based on your filter settings.
   *Image: interaction-filter-options-result.png*
   > **Note:** After you select the filter options, the filter icon changes (*Image: interaction-filter-highlight-icon.png*)You can clear the filter options by selecting the **CLEAR ALL** in the Filter options window.

# Hub navigation in Reltio Intelligent 360

> **Section:** Applications > Hub > Hub at a glance > Hub navigation


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/hub/hub-at-a-glance/hub-navigation/hub-navigation-in-reltio-intelligent-360?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs


Learn how to navigate Reltio Intelligent 360

When you log into the Reltio Intelligent 360 Hub, you see the Reltio Intelligent Assistant (RIA) - your virtual assistant that helps you find data and information with a simple conversation. Start here by asking RIA for help, or navigate to other sections of the Hub.

Let's see what's in the store for you in the Reltio Intelligent 360 Hub.

*Image: dp_hub_anatomy.png*

**Header/Banner**

The bar on the top of the screen that displays the Reltio logo, the tenant you are logged into, the Search bar and the global filter.

- 

  Navigate to other tenants (if you have access to more than one tenant) by selecting the drop-down menu next to the tenant name and selecting the one you want from the list.
- 

  Quickly locate a particular profile by typing the profile name in the Search bar and selecting the relevant one from the list.

**Left navigation drawer**

Hover your mouse pointer over the left navigation drawer and select one of these options from the slide-out menu:

- 

  **Reltio Intelligent Assistant**: Opens RIA. For more information, see topic [RIA for operation](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/ria/ria-reltio-intelligent-assistant-at-a-glance/ria-for-reltio-intelligent-360/ria-for-reltio-intelligent-360-operation?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).
- 

  **Profile Stats**: Displays the Profile Stats charts for the tenant. For more information, see topic [Profile Stats dashboard navigation](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/hub/profile-stats-dashboard-at-a-glance/profile-stats-dashboard-navigation?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).
- 

  **Data quality**: Displays the Data quality charts for the tenant. For more information, see topic [Data Quality dashboard a glance](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/hub/data-quality-dashboard-a-glance?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).
-

Learn how to navigate the Hub.

When you log into your Reltio Multidomain Data Management tenant using your credentials, you land in the Hub. If you are in any other application, such as the Console or Inbox, select the **Hub** option from the **Applications** menu.

When you log into the Hub, you see the **Dashboard** page with options to navigate to the **Data quality**, **Search**, and **Profiles** pages as well as to other applications.

Use these key sections in the **Hub** to manage your data in the Reltio platform:

*Image: ui_hubsections.png*

**Header/banner**

Displays the Reltio logo, the tenant you are currently logged into, and the Search bar. You can: 

- Banner color: Make it easier to identify your tenants by configuring a different header color for each tenant. For more information, see topic [Configuring Dashboards](https://docs.reltio.com/en/objectives/explore-data-insights/data-insights-at-a-glance/data-insights-reference/configuring-dashboards?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).

- Tenants: Navigate to other tenants by clicking the drop-down next to the tenant name and selecting the one you want from the list.
- Search bar: Quickly locate a particular profile by typing the profile name here and selecting the relevant one from the list.

**Left navigation drawer**

Hover your mouse pointer over the left navigation drawer and select one of these options from the slide-out menu:

- **Profile stats**: Displays charts and maps of tenant data. Three preconfigured charts and maps are displayed by default as well as any additional ones you configure. For more information, see topic .[Configure dashboard charts and maps](https://docs.reltio.com/en/objectives/explore-data-insights/data-insights-at-a-glance/data-insights-reference/configuring-dashboards/configure-dashboard-charts-and-maps?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).
- **Data quality**: Displays charts that provides insight about the quality of your data. For more information, see topic [Accessing Search](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/search/search-at-a-glance/search-navigation/accessing-search?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).
- **Create a new profile**: Displays a sub menu with options to create a new profile for the selected entity type. For more information, see topic [Adding a Profile](https://docs.reltio.com/en/objectives/manage-profiles/profile-management-at-a-glance/profile-management-operation/adding-a-profile?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).
- **Notifications**: Navigates to the **Notifications** page in the Console. For more information, see topic [Notification Management at a glance](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/console/configuration-applications/notification-management-at-a-glance?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).
- **Applications**: Displays a menu to navigate to other applications such as the Console, RDM, and Inbox.
- **Profile settings**: Displays a sub menu with options to view the the Reltio platform version number or sign out of the tenant.

# Reltio ID overview

> **Section:** Applications > Hub > Profiles at a glance > Profiles set up


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/hub/profiles-at-a-glance/profiles-set-up/reltio-id-overview?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs

**Keywords:** reltioid, durable, unique identifier, reltioid generation enablement, custom uid, ReltioID, Durable, Unique Identifier, Reltio ID Generation Enablement, Custom UID


Learn how to generate and maintain a unique and durable identifier to track data across all your applications inside and outside the Reltio platform.

Take a sneak peek at Reltio ID - your unique, durable identifier.

Are you a Data Steward or a Business User who is in charge of handling customer data across multiple disconnected analytical environments and distributed systems across your organization?

Does your management team often have discussions on implementing a costly and time-consuming in-house solution to build an identifier that can be used to identify an entity uniquely across all these different systems?

If this sounds like you, perhaps you could use a universal identifier generated in Reltio for every unique entity. This identifier can be used to connect and tie the entities' data spread across your distributed systems. It enables you to match and complete data across your applications, which ultimately leads to better data quality, accurate analytics reporting, and good business decisions.

## What is Reltio ID?

Reltio ID is a system-generated, UUID v6-based identifier that ensures every entity in your tenant has a durable, globally unique reference. It is automatically assigned to new entities created in your tenant

When Reltio ID generation is enabled, a new Reltio ID is assigned each time an entity is created — unless the entity merges on the fly with an existing entity that already has a Reltio ID.

> **Important:** The ReltioID attribute can only be generated for entities. It can’t be generated for relationships and interactions. Only one Reltio ID parameter can be selected for an entity type.

## Reltio ID generation for existing and cloned tenants

Reltio ID generation doesn’t apply retroactively to existing records when the feature is enabled. To assign Reltio IDs to existing entities, run the [Generate Reltio ID task](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/hub/profiles-at-a-glance/profiles-set-up/reltio-id-overview/generate-a-reltio-id-for-an-entity?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).

- **For new tenants or entity types:** Reltio IDs are created on-the-fly as new entities are added.
- **For existing tenants:** Run the task manually to generate IDs for existing records.
- **For cloned tenants or profiles:** Reltio IDs from the source tenant are cloned by default. Run the task with `regenerate=true` to assign new, unique Reltio IDs.

## Benefits of using Reltio ID

- **Durable**: Reltio ID is durable and unique for an entity within a tenant. It remains stable across data reloads and can be used for consistent identification.

  > **Note:** The Entity ID can’t be used as a durable identifier since it changes every time data is loaded into a new environment.
- **High latency search**: The search by Reltio ID API supports hyper performance. Get your search results quick as a wink.
- **Reuse**: You can reuse the earlier generated ID or generate a new ID when you reload data into a tenant.

## Custom UID

In addition to using a system-generated Reltio ID, you can configure any attribute in your entity as a **Custom UID**. This attribute is treated as a durable, unique identifier within your tenant.

**Custom UIDs** provide similar benefits to Reltio IDs. For example, you can use a medical license number or Social Security Number (SSN) as a **Custom UID**.

## Crosswalk behavior for Reltio ID and Custom UID

When a Reltio ID is generated—or a Custom UID is defined—Reltio automatically creates a crosswalk with:

- **Source system:**`ReltioID`
- **Value:** Either the generated Reltio ID or the provided Custom UID value

> **Attention:** You're responsible for maintaining the uniqueness of your Custom UID values. If two entities are created with the same Custom UID, they will behave like the same record for the ReltioID source. In this case, the second crosswalk replaces the first, and the entities merge based on crosswalk match.

## Reltio ID vs. Custom UID — Deep Dive Comparison

This table compares how Reltio ID and Custom UID work, including how they're configured, how they behave at runtime, and which use cases they best support.

| Feature | Reltio ID | Custom UID |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Type of ID** | System-generated UUID (v6) | User-defined, based on a specific attribute |
| **Value source** | Automatically created by Reltio at entity creation | Provided manually by user or loaded from source system |
| **How to enable** | Enable Reltio ID generation at the entity type level; add an attribute with type `ReltioId` | Mark an existing attribute with `customReltioId: true` in tenant configuration |
| **Entity creation behavior** | ID is generated during entity creation via UI, API, or Data Loader | Value must be present in the input; Reltio does not auto-generate |
| **Works for relationships/interactions?** | ❌ No | ❌ No |
| **Uniqueness enforcement** | ✅ Guaranteed by the system | ❌ Must be enforced by the user |
| **Crosswalk created** | ✅ Yes — a crosswalk with source system `ReltioID` and value = Reltio ID | ✅ Yes — same as Reltio ID; value = the custom UID |
| **Survivorship support** | ✅ Treated like a standard attribute, supports survivorship rules | ✅ Same survivorship behavior applies |
| **Merge behavior** | Multiple Reltio IDs from merged profiles are retained unless regenerated | Multiple Custom UID values can exist; OV determined by survivorship |
| **Can be regenerated?** | ✅ Yes — use `GenerateReltioIdTask` with `regenerate=true` | ❌ No — value must be replaced manually in data or through update |
| **Used in search API** | ✅ Yes — via `/entities/_byReltioId/{value}` endpoint | ✅ Yes — same endpoint, using the custom UID as crosswalk value |
| **Data type requirement** | Must be declared as `type: ReltioId` | Can be any supported type (e.g., `String`, `Number`, `URL`) |
| **Operational Value (OV) eligible?** | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes |
| **Multiple values allowed?** | ✅ Multiple crosswalks with Reltio IDs can be stored and versioned | ✅ Multiple values can be stored; must use survivorship to manage active one |
| **Persistence across loads** | ✅ Persistent and durable across data loads, clones, and environments | ✅ Persistent if maintained in source data and uniqueness is preserved |
| **Default system fallback** | ✅ Yes — recommended when no external durable ID is available | ❌ No — only use when you already have a consistent, authoritative ID in your business systems |

## How Reltio ID behaves in merges and survivorship

The `Reltio Id` and `Custom UID` attributes are treated like any other attribute:

- If several profiles are merged — each with its own Reltio ID — the resulting profile will contain multiple ReltioID crosswalks, increasing the total number of crosswalks.
- Each original (merged) profile contributes its own value.
- Reltio Id values are preserved unless regenerated by task.

You can define **survivorship rules** on the `ReltioId` and Custom UID attribute to control which value becomes the **Operational Value (OV)** shown in the UI and APIs.

## Next steps

Read on to find out more about how to use Reltio ID:

- [Enable Reltio ID and Custom UID](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/hub/profiles-at-a-glance/profiles-set-up/reltio-id-overview/enable-reltio-id-and-custom-uid?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs),
- [Generate a Reltio ID for an entity](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/hub/profiles-at-a-glance/profiles-set-up/reltio-id-overview/generate-a-reltio-id-for-an-entity?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs), and
- [Search for entity by ReltioID or Custom UID](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/hub/profiles-at-a-glance/profiles-set-up/reltio-id-overview/search-for-entity-by-reltioid-or-custom-uid?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).

# Generate a Reltio ID for an entity

> **Section:** Applications > Hub > Profiles at a glance > Profiles set up > Reltio ID overview


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/hub/profiles-at-a-glance/profiles-set-up/reltio-id-overview/generate-a-reltio-id-for-an-entity?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs

**Keywords:** generateReltioID, regenerate, Regenerate


Learn about running a task that generates a ReltioID parameter value for entities that have Reltio ID generation configured in a tenant.

Take a sneak peek at Reltio ID - your unique, durable identifier.

You can generate a Reltio ID for the following reasons:

- If the Reltio ID is missing for an entity in an existing tenant.
- If the Reltio ID is required for an entity for which data already exists.
- For a cloned tenant, the Reltio IDs are the same for the original and cloned tenant. Customers can regenerate the Reltio ID for the cloned tenant so that it has a unique Reltio ID for the Profile.

By default, a Reltio ID isn’t regenerated for an entity that already has Reltio Id, that is, the **regenerate** parameter is set to **false**. If the **regenerate** parameter is set to **true**, then a new Reltio ID is generated for an entity.

**Request**

Admin role is required: 

```
POST {ApplicationURL}/generateReltioId
```



Tenant admin role is required:

```
POST {ApplicationURL}/api/{tenantId}/generateReltioId
```

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tenantId` | Yes | The ID of the tenant for which Reltio ID generation enablement must be done. |
| `distributed` | No |  |
| `taskPartsCount` | No |  |
| `regenerate` | No | The current Reltio ID is removed and a new Reltio ID is regenerated for the entity when the parameter is set to `true`. |

**Response**

```
[
  {
    "id": "805478c5-1a6e-4ac7-ade2-e6df8b76e0b9",
    "groupId": "a39cd7fc-ba5a-4d1d-ae03-706a0db3abd1",
    "createdTime": 1663729380240,
    "createdBy": "yourname@yourcompany.com",
    "updatedTime": 1663729380240,
    "updatedBy": "yourname@yourcompany.com",
    "type": "com.reltio.businesslogic.tasks.ReltioID.GenerateReltioIDTask",
    "status": "SCHEDULED",
    "name": "Generate Reltio Id",
    "createdOnHost": "dataload-{pod-name}",
    "parallelExecution": false,
    "nodesGroup": "default",
    "parameters": {
      "tenantId": "your tenantname",
      "entityType": "all types",
      "uriList": "",
      "regenerate": "false"
    },
    "currentState": {},
    "duration": "0s"
  }
]
```

The request body, if provided, must contain a JSON array of the entity URIs that must be checked.

**Request**

```
POST {ApplicationURL}/api/{tenantId}/generateReltioId
["entities/9LIMXfO"]
```

**Response**

```
[
  {
    "id": "464ad37b-cedb-44a2-9746-ea6e743806cb",
    "groupId": "b7c0f9ab-cd21-4841-b973-09ba1f0aedd8",
    "createdTime": 1663730488676,
    "createdBy": "yourname@yourcompany.com",
    "updatedTime": 1663730488676,
    "updatedBy": "yourname@yourcompany.com",
    "type": "com.reltio.businesslogic.tasks.ReltioID.GenerateReltioIDTask",
    "status": "SCHEDULED",
    "name": "Generate Reltio Id",
    "createdOnHost": "dataload-{pod-name}",
    "parallelExecution": false,
    "nodesGroup": "default",
    "parameters": {
      "tenantId": "mytenantid",
      "entityType": "all types",
      "uriList": "[\"entities/9LIMXfO\"]",
      "regenerate": "false"
    },
    "currentState": {},
    "duration": "0s"
  }
]
```

If you send a request using the regenerate parameter, a new ID is generated in the response.

**Request**

```
POST {ApplicationURL}/api/{tenantId}/generateReltioId?regenerate=true
```

**Response**

```
[
  {
    "id": "1caf2410-742a-4e04-8cc2-83d79a8a336b",
    "groupId": "bea0f45c-859d-45f2-8f96-9315c8bc3360",
    "createdTime": 1663729455540,
    "createdBy": "yourname@yourcompany.com",
    "updatedTime": 1663729455540,
    "updatedBy": "yourname@yourcompany.com",

    "status": "SCHEDULED",
    "name": "Generate Reltio Id",
    "createdOnHost": "dataload-{pod-name}",
    "parallelExecution": false,
    "nodesGroup": "default",

      "tenantId": "mytenantid",
      "entityType": "all types",
      "uriList": "",

]

# Search for entity by ReltioID or Custom UID

> **Section:** Applications > Hub > Profiles at a glance > Profiles set up > Reltio ID overview


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/hub/profiles-at-a-glance/profiles-set-up/reltio-id-overview/search-for-entity-by-reltioid-or-custom-uid?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs

**Keywords:** getByReltioID


Learn about searching for an entity using the Reltio ID or Custom UID.

Take a sneak peek at Reltio ID - your unique, durable identifier.

**getByReltioID****Request**

```
GET {TenantURL}/entities/_byReltioId/1ed44bbe-ce65-8066-a07b-000027125fa0
Headers: Authorization: Bearer {your-access-token}
```

Where `1ed44bbe-ce65-8066-a07b-000027125fa0` is the **reltioId** parameter value

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Parameter | Required | Details |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Headers | `Authorization` | Yes | Stores the information about the authentication access token in the format "Bearer `<accessToken>` ". For more information, see topic [Authentication API](https://docs.reltio.com/en/developer-resources/system-administration-apis/system-administration-apis-at-a-glance/authentication-api?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs)). |
| Path | `reltioId` | Yes | Identifier of the object defined in the **reltioid** source property. For example, the Reltio Platform generates an assigned **ReltioID** for all entities. |
| Query | `options` | No | Comma-separated values that generate a response based on the option provided. Following are the options:  - **sendHidden** - disabled by default. The entity's JSON contains hidden attributes if this option is enabled. - **ovOnly** - returns only attribute values that have the **ov** flag set to **true**. - **nonOvOnly** - returns only attribute values that have the **ov** flag set to **false**.    If any nested or reference attribute values have the **ov** flag set to **true** and subattributes with the **ov** flag set to **false**, then these subattributes don’t appear in the response. |
| Query | `select` | No | Generates a comma-separated list of properties from the entity structure that must be returned in a response. The response generates a partial entity object.  For the `select` parameter, you can use the following fields in the request query:  - uri - type - tags - createdBy - createdTime - updatedBy - updatedTime - isFavorite - analyticsAttributes - label - secondaryLabel - crosswalks - attributes  For example:   - `select=attributes.FirstName,attributes.LastName` - `select=attributes`  The first query retrieves only the entity's first name and last name in the response. The second query retrieves all the entity's attributes.  Additional system properties are:   - `attributes._lookupCodes`: returns lookup codes for lookup attributes. - `attributes._lookupValues`: returns values for lookup attributes.  For example, `select=uri,label,attributes._lookupCodes,attributes._lookupValues.` |

**Response**

A JSON array with the object that contains the **reltioId** parameter.

```
GET /entities/_byReltioId/1ed44bbe-ce65-8066-a07b-000027125fa0
Headers: Authorization: Bearer {your-access-token}
[
    {

# Enable Reltio ID and Custom UID

> **Section:** Applications > Hub > Profiles at a glance > Profiles set up > Reltio ID overview


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/hub/profiles-at-a-glance/profiles-set-up/reltio-id-overview/enable-reltio-id-and-custom-uid?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs


Learn how to enable Reltio ID and Custom UID for specific entity types in your tenant configuration.

You need [ROLE_ADMIN_TENANT Access permissions](https://docs.reltio.com/en/objectives/administer-system/system-administration-at-a-glance/access-management-at-a-glance/access-management-reference/authorization/system-roles/critical-high-privilege-roles/role_admin_tenant-access-permissions?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs) or another role with similar configuration access to update the source and attribute configuration in your tenant. or another role with similar configuration access to update the source and attribute configuration in your tenant. For more information, see [System roles](https://docs.reltio.com/en/objectives/administer-system/system-administration-at-a-glance/access-management-at-a-glance/access-management-reference/authorization/system-roles?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).

Follow these steps to enable durable identifiers in your tenant. **Reltio ID** and and **Custom UID** must be configured manually using the API, as the required data types and flags aren't exposed in the UI.must be configured manually using the API, as the required data types and flags aren't exposed in the UI.


To enable Reltio ID for a specific entity type:

1. Add a source named `ReltioID`
   - In the **Sources** tab in **Data Modeler,**, add a new source **+ CREATE NEW**.
   - The **Display name** can be any value.*Image: i-create-reltioid-source.png*
2. Create a new attribute using the `ReltioId` data type via the API.
   This data type is not available in the UI.
   Addition of the `ReltioId` simple attribute to L3.
   Example payload:
   ```
{ "label": "Reltio Id", "name": "ReltioId", "type": "ReltioId", "hidden": false, "searchable": false, "attributeOrdering": { "orderType": "ASC", "orderingStrategy": "LUD" }, "uri": "configuration/entityTypes/Test1Profile/attributes/ReltioId", "skipInDataAccess": false }
   ```
   Example of how the Simple attribute looks like in the UI once added:*Image: i-reltioid-simple-attribute.png*
3. Save your tenant configuration changes.
4. To generate **Reltio IDs** for existing entities, run the `GenerateReltioIdTask`.
   For more information, see [Generate a Reltio ID for an entity](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/hub/profiles-at-a-glance/profiles-set-up/reltio-id-overview/generate-a-reltio-id-for-an-entity?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).

To enable Custom UID for a specific attribute:A Custom UID lets you define your own identifier, such as a license number or customer ID, and use it across tenants. Unlike the system-generated Reltio ID, a Custom UID value must be supplied by your source data. Reltio does not generate it automatically.

5. Ensure the source `ReltioID` has already been added
   Same setup as for **Reltio ID** above.
6. Edit the attribute configuration using the API
   This flag can't be configured through the UI.
   Example payload:
   ```
{ "label": "Website URL", "name": "WebsiteURL", "type": "URL", "customReltioId": true, "attributeOrdering": { "orderType": "ASC", "orderingStrategy": "LUD" }, "uri": "configuration/entityTypes/HCO/attributes/WebsiteURL", "skipInDataAccess": false }
   ```
   > **Note:** When `customReltioId: true` is set, Reltio expects the value to be provided during data load or via the API. It will not generate this value on its own. The platform creates a crosswalk using the ReltioID source system and the supplied value.
   - Add the `customReltioId: true` flag to mark it as a **Custom UID**.
7. Save your tenant configuration changes.

The selected entity types now support durable identifiers. New records will automatically be assigned a **Reltio ID** or or **Custom UID**. . Existing records will receive identifiers after running the generate task.

# Profiles at a glance

> **Section:** Applications > Hub


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/hub/profiles-at-a-glance?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs

**Keywords:** Working with Profiles, Profile Page, Common Mode, Profile View, Operational Value, View Mode, Edit Mode, profiles, profile page, profile view, operational value, ov, work with profile, view or edit a profile, common mode, Viewing, view a profile, viewing a profile, Editing, edit a profile, editing a profile


Learn about Profiles in the Hub.

Reltio Multidomain MDMReltio Intelligent 360

Reltio platform provides the ability to manage a variety of data entities using Hub. A profile is a collection of all the data associated with an entity.

Profiles contain the attributes for an entity, relationships for an entity, and sources for all of the attributes. It is possible that an entity attribute can have multiple sources and multiple values. The Operational Value (OV) is the current value for a given attribute, as defined by the survivorship rule for the attribute. The **Profile** pages enable you to view and manage the details for each entity in your tenant.

**Is an entity and a profile the same?**

A Reltio profile and a Reltio entity are subtly different, even though we tend to use the words interchangeably. An entity is a record; it has attributes (simple, nested and reference) and is treated as a node in the Reltio graph. A profile is a broader concept and refers to not only the entity of interest but all of the entities (nodes) connected directly to the entity via relationships, and all of the entity’s interaction data. So then a profile is really the 360 degree expression of an entity.

For more information about profiles, see topic [Profile management at a glance](https://docs.reltio.com/en/objectives/manage-profiles/profile-management-at-a-glance?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).

## Display attributes in all modes

When you use the viewing, editing, or suggesting modes, attributes without values are not displayed by default in the Profile view. However, if you want to view such attributes in all modes, include the `alwaysVisible` option in your UI configuration file. Add a list of attributes under a specific entity type, that you want to be visible in all these modes, as shown below:

```
"configuration/entityTypes/HCP": {
  ...,
  "views": [
    {
      "component": "Attributes",
      ...,
       "includeUris": [
         "configuration/entityTypes/HCP/attributes/FirstName",
         "configuration/entityTypes/HCP/attributes/LastName",
         "configuration/entityTypes/HCP/attributes/Address"
      ]
      "alwaysVisible": [
        "configuration/entityTypes/HCP/attributes/CallingName"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

In the above example, under `Views`, we've included the `CallingName` attribute as part of the `alwaysVisible` option. This ensures that the attribute is visible in all modes, even if a value is not defined for it.

> **Note:** Add the `alwaysVisible` option under the **Views** section, at the same level as the `includeUris`.

To update the UI configuration, see topic [Export and Import of UI Configuration Files](https://docs.reltio.com/en/objectives/configure-the-reltio-ui/ui-configuration-at-a-glance/export-and-import-of-ui-configuration-files?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).

# Profile Attribute Facets

> **Section:** Objectives > Manage profiles > Profile management at a glance > Profile navigation > Profile Attributes


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/objectives/manage-profiles/profile-management-at-a-glance/profile-navigation/profile-attributes/profile-attribute-facets?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs

**Keywords:** Working with Profiles, Attribute facets, Profile Page, Profile View, Hierarchy facet, Simple attributes, Nested attributes, Reference attributes, Boolean attributes, profiles, attribute facets, profile page, profile view, hierarchy facet, simple attributes, nested attributes, reference attributes, boolean attributes


The attribute facets in the profile view display details about the entity.

This area displays the main attributes of the profile, which are displayed in various facets. Right at the top is the profile banner, which displays the entity name, entity ID, and entity type. This profile banner is dynamic, which basically means that the size of the banner automatically adjusts in size based on the information in the banner. This ensures the critical facets in your profile get more space.

You can also view entity details in various facets (which are configured in the UI Modeler). For example, the Attributes facet display the basic attributes of the entity such as the name and address details, as shown below.

*Image: attributefacet.png*

The Hierarchy facet displays your organization structure and its child entities and how they are related to each other.

*Image: hierarchyfacet.png*

The organizational structure, in which there are successive branching and subdivisions, helps to understand the affiliations between organizations.

The Relationship facet displays the relationship of an entity with other entities.

*Image: ui_relationshipfacet.jpg*

You can rate each relation listed here to be correct or not. Taking the example in the above image, if you know that the Health Care Practitioner does not work at the HCO anymore, you can disagree and give the reason why you think so. A history is maintained, and you can view details of who agreed or disagreed, when the action was taken, and the number of agreements or disagreements. For more information, see topic [Rate details in the Relationship facet](https://docs.reltio.com/en/objectives/manage-profiles/profile-management-at-a-glance/profile-management-operation/rate-details-in-the-relationship-facet_1?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).

> **Note:** To enable voting in the relationship facet, you must configure the relationship chart in the UI Modeler. For more information, see topic [Charts for profile pages in the UI Modeler](https://docs.reltio.com/en/objectives/configure-the-reltio-ui/ui-configuration-at-a-glance/configure-your-profile-pages/charts-for-profile-pages-in-the-ui-modeler?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).

You also have the option of selecting the columns that you want to include in the Relationship table view, as shown below:

*Image: ui_showcolumrelationshipfacet.png* Select or deselect the columns you want shown in the facet. 

> **Note:** These preferences are saved at the user-level. When you log into the Hub the next time, these preferences remain and the Relationship facet displays columns you selected earlier.



For more detailed information about the various facets that can be configured for a profile, see[UI Modeler at a glance](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/console/configuration-applications/ui-modeler-at-a-glance?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).

## More about attribute and their values

You can use the Profile perspective to edit attribute values here. A blue icon next to an attribute value indicates that the value has additional values associated with it. You can hover over the blue icon to view these additional values. These multiple values are consolidated into the profile over a period of time, through the process of merging. The main value displayed here is the Operational Value(OV), which is determined by the survivorship rules.

**Nested** attributes have an arrow next to it, which when expanded will display the related sub-attributes.

**Reference** attribute is displayed as a link. When you click this link, the referenced location entity is displayed.

**Boolean** attributes are used to create true or false statements and contain **Yes** /**No** or **True** /**False** values. The value of a boolean attribute can be **Yes** or **No** at the attribute level, but at the nested attribute level, the value of a boolean attribute can be True or False.

You can also configure to display a **?** icon next to the attribute that helps you understand the significance or meaning of the attribute.

*Image: ui_supportdesc.png*

When you hover over the **?** icon, you will see a pop up that describes the attribute. You will find this icon in the **Viewing**, **Suggesting**, and **Editing** modes. The description that you see in the pop up is defined in the **Data Modeler** in the **Console**. You can also find the same icon in the **Single attribute** facet, next to the title. For more information, see topic [Configure your profile pages](https://docs.reltio.com/en/objectives/configure-the-reltio-ui/ui-configuration-at-a-glance/configure-your-profile-pages?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs) and [Create entity type attributes](https://docs.reltio.com/en/objectives/model-data/data-modeling-at-a-glance/data-modeling-operation/define-entity-types-and-attributes/create-entity-type-attributes?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).

## Errors and warnings

In the new **Profile** view, any errors in the profile data or warnings are displayed right at the top of the profile page. You will see the name of the attribute and sub-attribute, if it contains a validation error or warning.

*Image: ui_profileerrors.png*

You can now directly navigate to the attribute value that is related to the error. Select the **Editing** mode in the dropdown. You can now see the link next to the error and warning messages. You can click on this link to go directly to the attribute value that is incomplete or invalid.

*Image: ui_profileserrorlink.png*

For example, if the **Zip code** is blank in the **Address** attribute, the error or warning message will display the zip code attribute name to let you know where the error is. Make the required changes in the attribute and then save the profile.

*Image: ui_subattributewarning.png*

It's the same for reference attributes too, for example a location. You can view RDM transcode errors for reference attributes at the top of the profile, the difference being that these are only visible in the **Viewing** mode, In other words, these errors are not visible in the other modes such as Editing or Suggesting. See an example below:

*Image: ui_rdmerrorreference.png*

Notice the icon next to the attribute name. Hover over the icon to view a tooltip, which indicates that this is only available in view mode.

*Image: ui_rdmerrorreferencemsg.png*

You can navigate to the error by clicking on the error.

> **Note:** To enable display of the RDM transcode errors here, you must configure the `validateReferenceEntityInReadMode` parameter in the UI configuration file. An example of the configuration is given below:
> ```
> {
>          "point": "com.reltio.plugins.ui.configuration",
>          "id": "com.reltio.plugins.entity.Validation",
>          "validateRelations": true,
>          "validateReferenceEntityInReadMode": true
>       },
> ```

# Attribute Facets

> **Section:** Objectives > Manage profiles > Profile management at a glance > Profile navigation > Profile Attributes


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/objectives/manage-profiles/profile-management-at-a-glance/profile-navigation/profile-attributes/attribute-facets?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs

**Keywords:** Search Attribute Values, Starts With, search attribute values, starts with, attribute facet


Attribute facets display the details of a single attribute in a facet.

You can view and analyze an attribute in a facet of its own, also known as **Single Attribute View**. You can set the properties of the Single Attribute View by using the UI Modeler application in Console.

## Working with Inactive Attribute Values

In the Single Attribute View or attribute facet, you can view and analyze the details of a single attribute. By default, only the active attribute values are displayed.

Optionally, you can view the inactive attribute values in the Single Attribute View. To display the **Show Inactive values** option in the **Settings** menu in the attribute facet, turn on the **Show inactive values menu** option for the Single Attribute View in the UI Modeler application in Console. For more information, see [UI Modeler at a glance](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/console/configuration-applications/ui-modeler-at-a-glance?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).

With this option turned on for your tenant, the **Settings** menu of your attribute facet appears with the **Show Inactive values** option as shown in the following image:

*Image: ui_pro_showinactivevalues.png*

> **Note:** The inactive icon (*Image: ui_pro_inactiveicon.png*) indicates the number of inactive values that exist for the attribute.

When you select the **Show Inactive values** option, the active as well as the inactive attribute values are displayed. The inactive values have a striped background to indicate their inactive status. You can modify these values by changing the Profile view to the ‘Edit’ mode, if required.

*Image: ui_pro_inactivevalue.png*

## Search Attribute Values

*Image: ui_pro_attfacetsrch.png*

**starts with**- Ignores the order of words in the search string. For example, if we have an attribute value "ABC XYZ", we can find it by using search string "XYZ A".
- Searches across all attribute values of complex attributes. For example, if we have a complex attribute with sub-attribute1 having value "ABC" and sub-attribute2 having value "XYZ", then we can find this complex attribute by using search string "XYZ AB".

## Charts

Reltio Platform can display nested attributes in chart format, such as Profile transactional data (interactions). You can display line, graph, and bar charts.

# Profile perspectives navigation

> **Section:** Applications > Hub > Profiles at a glance > Profile perspectives tabs


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/hub/profiles-at-a-glance/profile-perspectives-tabs/profile-perspectives-navigation?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs

**Keywords:** Working with Profiles, Profile Page, Profile View, View Mode, profiles, profile page, profile view, work with profile, common mode


Learn to navigate the perspectives in the Hub Profile.

## Profile overview

What is an entity? An entity can be a person, organization, place, object, or thing that is an element of your organization. In the Reltio platform, entities are managed using Profiles. A profile can be defined as a collection of data associated with an entity. You can view all the relationships, interactions, hierarchies, and other such details associated with an entity.

**Is an entity and a profile the same?**

A Reltio profile and a Reltio entity are subtly different, even though we tend to use the words interchangeably. An entity is a record; it has attributes (simple, nested and reference) and is treated as a node in the Reltio graph. A profile is a broader concept and refers to not only the entity of interest but all of the entities (nodes) connected directly to the entity via relationships, and all of the entity’s interaction data. So then a profile is really the 360 degree expression of an entity.

**Attribute types**

An attribute can be any value that characterizes or defines the entity. For example, the name or date of birth of an employee in your organization. Attributes can be simple, nested (has sub-attributes), or referenced (references other attributes). To give an example, in a profile, the entity name is a simple attribute, the phone number is a nested attribute, and address (that references locations to be used as address) is a reference attribute.

The **Profile** perspective enables you to view related details about an entity. When you open the Profile view, you will see the entity details in facets, based on your configuration in UI Modeler. From within Hub too, you can personalize your profile view by moving around the facets or increasing the size of your facets. For example, let us say that you want the Potential Matches to be at the top of your profile and move the Hierarchy details below. You can do this by moving the facets around.

You don’t need to do this every time you open a Profile perspective. Once you have personalized your profile view, preferences are saved and the same layout is displayed the next time you log into your profile.

You can use UI Modeler to configure the layout of this view. You have the option to configure a different layout for each entity type defined. For more information about how to configure your profile page, see

Learn how to find your way around the Profile Stats dashboard

Let's take you around the Profile Stats dashboard neighborhood.

This dashboard in the Hub has charts providing statistics for different kinds of data management activities and business insights, such as the status of your profiles, notifications for you and your team, and so much more.

Use these key areas in the Profile stats dashboard UI to determine the data to display.

**Header/banner**

Displays the Reltio logo, the tenant you are currently logged into, Search bar and filter For more information, see the topic for your Reltio Context Intelligence Platform product in section [Hub navigation](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/hub/hub-at-a-glance/hub-navigation?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).

Displays the menus for the features available in the Hub. Select the **Profile stats** menu to view the UI described in this section.

**Profile stats toolbar**

Provides tools for customizing which charts to display on the chart, refreshing all chart data at once, and restoring the default layout. For more information, see topics [Add/remove Profile Stats dashboard charts](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/hub/profile-stats-dashboard-at-a-glance/profile-stats-dashboard-operation/addremove-profile-stats-dashboard-charts?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs), [Refresh all Profile Stats dashboard charts](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/hub/profile-stats-dashboard-at-a-glance/profile-stats-dashboard-navigation/refresh-all-profile-stats-dashboard-charts?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs), and [Reset the default Profile Stats dashboard layout](https://docs.reltio.com/en/objectives/explore-data-insights/data-insights-at-a-glance/data-insights-operation/reset-the-default-profile-stats-dashboard-layout?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs)

**Charts (facets)**

In addition to default charts that come preconfigured with the Profile Stats dashboard, your organization's Reltio Administrator also configure custom charts to suit your business needs. For details on configuring charts, see topic [Profile Stats dashboard navigation](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/hub/profile-stats-dashboard-at-a-glance/profile-stats-dashboard-navigation?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs). 

As a user, you can personalize the content and layout of your Profile Stats dashboard. For details, see topics [Display data in Profile Stats dashboard charts](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/hub/profile-stats-dashboard-at-a-glance/profile-stats-dashboard-navigation/display-data-in-profile-stats-dashboard-charts?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs), , and [Reset the default Profile Stats dashboard layout](https://docs.reltio.com/en/objectives/explore-data-insights/data-insights-at-a-glance/data-insights-operation/reset-the-default-profile-stats-dashboard-layout?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).

# Display data in Profile Stats dashboard charts

> **Section:** Applications > Hub > Profile Stats dashboard at a glance > Profile Stats dashboard navigation


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/hub/profile-stats-dashboard-at-a-glance/profile-stats-dashboard-navigation/display-data-in-profile-stats-dashboard-charts?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs


Learn how to manage the way data is displayed in Profile Stats dashboard charts

Reltio configured the Profile Stats dashboards initial content and layout in accordance with your organization's Reltio Context Intelligence Platform implementation. Reltio system administrators may subsequently have updated the configuration for other users in your organization. As a user, you can customize the layout to suit your personal preferences as shown in this topic. You also can change the position of charts on your dashboard as described in topic [Rearrange your Profile Stats dashboard layout](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/hub/profile-stats-dashboard-at-a-glance/profile-stats-dashboard-navigation/rearrange-your-profile-stats-dashboard-layout?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs)..

As a user, decide which of your organization's charts you want to display your own Profile Stats dashboard and and manage the way data is displayed in them. The changes you make affect only your dashboard display.


To manage the display of charts in your Profile Stats dashboard:

1. From **Hub > Platform stats**, locate an existing chart you want to manage.
2. On the top right of the chart, select the **More actions** menu and select the desire option:
   **Refresh chart data**

Select this option to refresh the data displayed in the selected chart 

*Image: ui_personalizerefresh.png*

**Fullscreen/Exit fullscreen**

Select the **Fullscreen** option to view the selected chart in full screen mode.The option changes to **Exit fullscreen** in the menu. Select that option to display the full dashboard again.

**Remove a chart**

Select this option to remove a chart from your Profile Stats dashboard..If you subsequently want to add this chart back to your dashboard, see topic [Add/remove Profile Stats dashboard charts](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/hub/profile-stats-dashboard-at-a-glance/profile-stats-dashboard-operation/addremove-profile-stats-dashboard-charts?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).

If needed, you can refresh one or more charts in your Profile Stats dashboard to display the latest information. Refresh the data in every chart in your dashboard at one time as shown in this topic. # Rearrange your Profile Stats dashboard layout

> **Section:** Applications > Hub > Profile Stats dashboard at a glance > Profile Stats dashboard navigation


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/hub/profile-stats-dashboard-at-a-glance/profile-stats-dashboard-navigation/rearrange-your-profile-stats-dashboard-layout?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs


Learn how to rearrange to position of charts in your Profile Stats dashboard

Your Reltio System Administrator configures which charts are available in your organization's Profile Stats dashboard, as well as their initial layout, in the UI Modeler. For details, see topic [Profile Stats dashboard navigation](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/hub/profile-stats-dashboard-at-a-glance/profile-stats-dashboard-navigation?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs)..

As a user, arrange charts in your Profile Stats dashboard to suit your preferences. The changes you make affect only your dashboard display. If you subsequently want to return to the original layout, see topic [Reset the default Profile Stats dashboard layout](https://docs.reltio.com/en/objectives/explore-data-insights/data-insights-at-a-glance/data-insights-operation/reset-the-default-profile-stats-dashboard-layout?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs)..


To rearrange the position and size of charts in your Profile Stats dashboard:

1. From **Hub > Platform stats**, locate an existing chart whose position or size you want to change.
2. Hover your mouse pointer over the top-center of the chart until the pointer shape changes, then click and drag the chart from its current position and drop it at the desired new position.
   *Image: ui_personalizedragdrop.png*
3. Position the mouse pointer on the lower-right corner of a chart until the pointer shape changes and then and drag the corner up and to the left to reduce its size or down and to the right to to enlarge its size.
   *Image: ui_personalizeresize.png*

Rearranged and resized charts remain in this layout the next time you open the Profile Stats dashboard.

> **Section:** Objectives > Explore data insights > Data insights at a glance > Data insights operation


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/objectives/explore-data-insights/data-insights-at-a-glance/data-insights-operation/reset-the-default-profile-stats-dashboard-layout?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs

Your Reltio System Administrator configures which charts are available in your organization's Profile Stats dashboard, as well as their initial layout, in the UI Modeler. For details, see topic [Profile Stats dashboard navigation](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/hub/profile-stats-dashboard-at-a-glance/profile-stats-dashboard-navigation?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs)..

# Profile Stats dashboard at a glance

> **Section:** Applications > Hub


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/hub/profile-stats-dashboard-at-a-glance?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs


Get a high-level view of Hub Profile Stats dashboard

Reltio Multidomain MDMReltio Intelligent 360

Take it from the top with Profile Stats dashboard. Get the overview here, then see the sub topics in this section to drill down to the details.

## What is Profile Stats dashboard?

The Profile Stats dashboard in the Hub gives you a bird's eye view of your tenant data.

This is similar to your car dashboard, where you can tell at a glance how much fuel is in your tank, how long you can drive with that fuel, or what speed you're traveling at.

## Who is Profile Stats dashboard for?

This content is curated for these Reltio user roles defined in topic [About roles](https://docs.reltio.com/en/roles/about-roles?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs):

Business UserData StewardSystem Administrator

## Why would I use the Profile Stats dashboard?

Use this dashboard to:

- 

  Work with operational statistics and workflow tasks
- 

  Gather data insights to make quick business decisions.
- 

  Customize the layout of the dashboard, create new charts, modify existing charts, and publish dashboard configuration for all users.

## When would I use Profile Stats dashboard?

Consult this dashboard after your data is available in your tenant and whenever you want to look for opportunities to fine tune it.

## Where do I find Profile Stats dashboard?

Reltio Multidomain MDMReltio Intelligent 360

Access this dashboard from **Hub > Profile stats**.

# Customize Profile Stats dashboard

> **Section:** Applications > Hub > Profile Stats dashboard at a glance > Profile Stats dashboard set up


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/hub/profile-stats-dashboard-at-a-glance/profile-stats-dashboard-set-up/customize-profile-stats-dashboard?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs


Learn how to make the Profile Stats dashboard your own

Let's get you going with Profile Stats dashboard.

## Pick your point of view

Configure the content and layout of your **Profile stats** dashboard to suit your preferences in the **UI Modeler**. If you're a System Administrator you can configure which charts are available to all users in your organization. If you're a user, you can customize the layout of your charts on the dashboard, without affecting other users.

Select from preconfigured or general charts, sometimes referred to as facets:

**Preconfigured charts**

These preconfigured charts come configured for you as part of the dashboard:

- 

  **Profile stats view**: The profile activity in your tenant for a specified period of time.
- 

  **Saved Searches**: The number of profiles returned for recent or saved searches.
- 

  **Notification Inbox** The Workflow Inbox details for the logged in user.
- 

  **Activity Log**: User activity across a tenant.

**General charts**

Use general charts to configure the data you want to view on the dashboard in these formats:

- Bar Chart
- Bubble Chart
- Cloud tags
- Custom
- Donut Chart
- Entities by type view
- Filtered entitites view
- Line Chart
- Map
- Pie Chart
- Table
- Treemap





Configure charts to present data for your business needs, such as: 

- 

  Tenant operational statistics: View events that have occurred in your profiles for a specified time period. For example, the Profile Stats view facet is a line graph that displays the profile activity in your tenant.
- 

  Business data visualization maps: View business data in your organization on a map. For example, you can configure a map of the world that displays the number of organizations in each country.
- 

  Data quality charts: Analyze the quality of your data. For example, you can configure a chart that displays the profiles where addresses were not verified or only partially verified

For more information on configuring the charts available for your organization, see topics [Configuring Dashboards](https://docs.reltio.com/en/objectives/explore-data-insights/data-insights-at-a-glance/data-insights-reference/configuring-dashboards?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs) and [UI Modeler at a glance](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/console/configuration-applications/ui-modeler-at-a-glance?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs). After you configure and publish your dashboard in the UI Modeler, the modified chart displays **Updated** next to its title in the Profile Stats dashboard.

For more information on managing the display of data in configured charts in your own Profile Stats dashboard, see topic [Profile Stats dashboard navigation](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/hub/profile-stats-dashboard-at-a-glance/profile-stats-dashboard-navigation?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).

## Location, location, location

The data you see on the dashboard depends on your access rights to the tenant. For example, if you have access to profiles in the US, then the dashboard only displays data for US profiles in that tenant. However, if you also have access to profiles in other regions, such as Canada and the UK, the dashboard also displays details of the Canada and UK profiles.

Apply global filters to your data to specify whether search results display active, inactive, or both entities for your Reltio Platform data. For more information, see topic [Understanding the Global Filters](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/search/search-at-a-glance/search-operation/understanding-the-global-filters?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).

# Create a folder

> **Section:** Objectives > Manage profiles > Profile management at a glance > Profile management operation > Work with segments > Group segments by folders


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/objectives/manage-profiles/profile-management-at-a-glance/profile-management-operation/work-with-segments/group-segments-by-folders/create-a-folder?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs

To group segments, you can create folders and add or move segments under them. You can also create subfolders under a folder. Folders can be created with duplicate names.


To create a folder:

1. In the **Hub**, select **Segmentation** from the left navigation pane.
2. In the **Segments** page, select **+New** > **Create new folder**.
3. In the **Name** field, enter the name of the folder.
4. Select **Save** to save the folder. The folder is created and displayed in the Segments list.
   > **Note:** Folders are visible in the **All Segments** section but not in the **Favorite** or **My Segments** sections. In this section, sorting by name organizes folders and segments separately.

# Segmentation at a glance

> **Section:** Applications > Hub


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/hub/segmentation-at-a-glance?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs


Learn about the Segmentation feature for Reltio Intelligent 360 in the Reltio Hub

Reltio Intelligent 360

In simple terms, Segmentation means dividing a dataset into categories or groups based on shared characteristics, attributes, or behaviors. For example, if you have a large dataset of your consumers and you want to target only those consumers who spend a certain amount on electronics or cosmetics every month, you can create a specific segment consisting of such consumers based on interactions that capture their behavioral patterns.

The Dynamic Segmentation feature in Reltio Intelligent 360 empowers you to easily look into your data through search, and then, bring it all together to create and utilize segments based on real-time entity and transactional data. You can analyze your data more effectively, tailor marketing strategies to target particular segments and ultimately enhance your end-user’s experience.

The Reltio Intelligent 360 Hub provides you with the **Segmentation** option on the left navigation drawer to easily and quickly visualize and create segments of the data on your tenant. You can then seamlessly send those segments to downstream systems for activation.

*Image: dp_seg_selectsegmentation.png*

On selecting **Segmentation** from the left slide-out menu, the **Segments** page lists the existing segments. If there are no segments, you can create segments by using the **Create Segment** option from either the top bar or the button that appears as part of the welcome message. For more information, see topic [Create a segment](https://docs.reltio.com/en/objectives/manage-profiles/profile-management-at-a-glance/profile-management-operation/work-with-segments/create-a-segment?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).

The Activation service related to Segmentation is a process that enables Reltio to synchronize segment members to downstream systems through scheduled jobs. For more information, see topic [Activation service for segmentation](https://docs.reltio.com/en/objectives/manage-profiles/profile-management-at-a-glance/profile-management-operation/work-with-segments/activation-service-for-segmentation?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).

> **Note:** Dynamic segmentation is enabled by making changes to the way in which entities and interaction attributes are stored, indexed, and retrieved. Currently, Reltio provides this feature in the Google Cloud Platform (GCP) and the Amazon Web Services (AWS) environments with plans to extend it for other cloud providers in the future releases.

## Prerequisite for segmentation

The Dynamic Segmentation feature in Reltio Intelligent 360 enables you to group similar profiles by using the profile attributes , derived attributes and other interaction details including the interaction type, interaction attributes, interaction members .

Interaction attributes are available for segmentation by default. However, before you use entity attributes in filters to create a segment, you must mark these attributes for segmentation in your L3 configuration. For more information regarding entity attributes, see topic [Enable attributes for segmentation](https://docs.reltio.com/en/objectives/manage-profiles/profile-management-at-a-glance/profile-management-operation/work-with-segments/enable-attributes-for-segmentation?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).

**Related links**

- [Segmenter](https://docs.reltio.com/en/products/reltio-agentflow/reltio-agentflow-overview/agentflow-agents-catalog/segmenter?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs)
