# Segmentation navigation

> **Section:** Applications > Hub > Segmentation at a glance


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/hub/segmentation-at-a-glance/segmentation-navigation?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs


Learn how to get around the Segmentation page in the Hub.

Reltio Intelligent 360

To view the main Segmentation page, access the **Segmentation** option from the Hub left navigation drawer.

*Image: ui_segmentationmain.png*

In the All segments page, view a list of segments created for the tenant. For each segment, you can view the following:

- 

  **Name** of the segment
- 

  **Status** - which can be one of the following:
  - Live - denotes a segment with real-time sync rules.
  - Computing - denotes a segment with a batch process that is in progress
  - Queued- denotes a segment with a batch process, where the evaluation job is yet to start
  - Disabled - denotes a segment that is disabled
- 

  **Description** - the description of the segment
- 

  **Shared with** - Denotes whether everyone can view the segment, or is it available only for the user who created it.
- 

  **Refresh type** - Can be one of the following:
  - Real-time - Based on the rules configured, the segment is refreshed with profile data in real-time. In other words, any change in profile data is instantly reflected in the segment.
  - Batch - Applicable only when you select Interaction data when configuring rules for the segment. You can specify a periodic batch process to refresh profile data for the segment.
- 

  **Last refreshed on** - the date when the segment was last refreshed.
- 

  **Audience count** - The number of profiles that match the rules set in the segment
- 

  **Destinations** - the destinations configured for the segment.
- 

  **Show/hide columns** - Enables you to select attributes you want displayed in the table here.

**Segment facet in the Profile view**

You can also view segments for a specific entity in the **Profile** view. In the **Search** page, select the entity for which you want to view Segments and look at the Segments facet.

*Image: ui_segmentfacet.png*

For more information, see [Configure the Segments facet for the Profile view](https://docs.reltio.com/en/objectives/configure-the-reltio-ui/ui-configuration-at-a-glance/configure-the-segments-facet-for-the-profile-view?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).

## What is Hub?

The Hub is the user interface for managing data in the Reltio Context Intelligence Platform.

**RIA - Reltio Intelligent Assistant**

Reltio Intelligent 360

Get answers to questions about Reltio features and functions as well as the data on your tenant.

**Dashboards**

Get a comprehensive overview of the data in your tenant and provide an insight about the quality of this data:

- 

  Profile statistics
- 

  Data quality

**Segmentation**

Reltio Intelligent 360

Segmentation means dividing a dataset into categories or groups based on shared characteristics, attributes, or behaviors.

**Profiles**

View and manage the attributes and relationships for each entity in your tenant, based on Search results.

**Bulk match**

Merge or mark records as not a match, in bulk, for a selected entity type.

## Who is Hub for?

This content is curated for these Reltio user roles defined in [About roles](https://docs.reltio.com/en/roles/about-roles?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs):

Business UserData Product OwnerData Steward

## Why would I use Hub?

Hub is where you view and manage your unified data.

- 

  View data quality metrics to monitor and improve the integrity of your data.
- 

  Search, create, update, and delete profiles to keep your records accurate and up to date.
- 

  Resolve potential matches to maintain a unified and consistent view of your data.
- 

  Explore relationships between profiles for deeper insights into data connections.

## When would I use Hub?

Use the Hub to view, access, and analyze your tenant data:

- 

  look at charts and maps in your dashboard
- 

  determine the quality of your data
- 

  search for profiles that you imported or created
- 

  view their relationship details
- 

  match and merge profiles that you think are the same

# Inbox navigation

> **Section:** Applications > Inbox > Inbox at a glance


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/inbox/inbox-at-a-glance/inbox-navigation?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs


Learn how to find your way around the Inbox UI.

Let's take you around the Inbox neighborhood.

## Inbox access

Access Inbox from here in the Reltio UI: **Reltio App Selector > Inbox***Image: g-apps-inbox-nav.gif*

## Inbox anatomy

Use the following key areas of the **Inbox** page to view your Inbox tasks.*Image: i-apps-inbox-anatomy.png*

**Select workflow task tab**

By default, your open assigned tasks are in view. In the navigation menu on the left, you may select:

- **Inbox (My assigned tasks)** - this is the default view with **Filters > Status** = `Open`
- **Team (All team tasks)** - tasks assigned to your team. Team members can action or view any of these tasks.
- **Sent (My requested tasks)** - tasks that you sent for approval.
- **All (All tasks)** - no filters, both open and closed tasks. The users who have the necessary permissions are able to access the closed or resolved tasks. By default, closed tasks are available in the Inbox for a period of one year from the resolved or closed date.

**Filters**

Use the filters in the navigation menu to narrow down tasks by these criteria: **Task type**, **Step**, **DCR type**, **Entity type**, **Relationship type**, **Priority**, **Status**, **Step action taken**, **Created by**, **Created date**, **Assigned to**, **Entity ID**, **DCR ID**, **Decision**, and **Has Changes**. For more information, see topic [Filter tasks](https://docs.reltio.com/en/objectives/manage-workflow-tasks/workflow-management-at-a-glance/workflow-management-operation/working-with-tasks/filter-tasks?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).

**Tasks selector**

Select all or clear selected tasks.

**Task type tabs**

Select the type of task to view:

- **ALL** - default
- **AUTHORING** - tasks for authoring entities.
- **DATA CHANGE REQUEST REVIEW** - tasks to change entities.
- **POTENTIAL MATCH REVIEW** - tasks that involve a potential match.
- **RDM DATA CHANGE REQUEST REVIEW** - tasks to change reference data.
- **RECOMMEND FOR DELETE** - tasks with data deletion recommendations.

**Column selector & View switcher**

Using **show/hide columns**, select the columns to view for the tasks: **Task type**, **Entities**, **Status**, **Priority**, **Created by**, **Created on**, **Taken on**, and **Action taken**.The**View switcher** switches the display of task details between list and tabular format. For more information, see topic [Switch between Table and List views](https://docs.reltio.com/en/objectives/manage-workflow-tasks/workflow-management-at-a-glance/workflow-management-operation/working-with-tasks/switch-between-table-and-list-views?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).

**Workflow task details area**

The area to the right of the navigation pane displays the tasks according to the selections and filters. The task icon indicates the process the task belongs to. More than one process can be represented in the list, and the processes can be varied with regard to things like approving an expense report, matching tasks, and so on. 

For more information, see topic [Working With Tasks](https://docs.reltio.com/en/objectives/manage-workflow-tasks/workflow-management-at-a-glance/workflow-management-operation/working-with-tasks?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).

For custom workflows, the entity types are sorted based on L3 configuration. If there are more than one entity for entity type, then they are in turn sorted on their label. If you select the entity, details of all the entities for that custom workflow is displayed on the right pane. For more information, see [Configure custom workflows](https://docs.reltio.com/en/objectives/manage-workflow-tasks/workflow-management-at-a-glance/workflow-management-set-up/overview-of-workflow-customizations/overview-of-workflow-configuration/configure-custom-workflows?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).

# Recipes for Search before create

> **Section:** Applications > Data Integrations > Application Integration at a glance > Reltio Integration for Salesforce (with RIH) at a glance > Reltio Integration for Salesforce (with RIH) Overview > Search before create (SBC)


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/data-integrations/application-integration-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-overview/search-before-create-sbc/recipes-for-search-before-create?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs


Learn about the recipes used in the Search before create functionality.

The Search before create (SBC) feature searches for records in Salesforce, to determine if already present, thus avoiding duplication. We use a set of recipes to implement this feature, which searches for account and contact records before importing them into the system.

Access the prebuilt SBC recipes in the RIH interface from the left navigation panel under **Projects** → **SFDC** → **SBC** folder.

Use these recipes for the Search before create feature:

- Trigger recipes - The API trigger recipes expose the logic for the search and import features, managing the return of the HTTP codes.
  - SFDC | API | SBC - Search Account
  - SFDC | API | SBC - Import Account
  - SFDC | API | SBC - Search Contact
  - SFDC | API | SBC - Import Contact

- 

  Process recipes - The Process recipes handle the orchestration and business logic required to deal with the search and import features. When importing, the To SFDC Sync/RT Event-Driven PROC recipes are called.
  - SFDC | PROC | SBC - Search Process for Account - Reltio and Salesforce
  - SFDC | PROC | SBC - Import Process for Account - Reltio
  - SFDC | PROC | SBC - Search Process for Contact - Reltio and Salesforce
  - SFDC | PROC | SBC - Import Process for Contact - Reltio
- 

  SFDC-SBC - The API collection create the API endpoints.
  - SBC-Account-Import
  - SBC-Account-Import
  - SBC-Contact-Search
  - SBC-Contact-Import

## Connections

Ensure you have these connections for the recipes to work successfully:

- 

  Connection to your Salesforce account
- 

  Connecting to your Reltio tenant

# Search before create (SBC)

> **Section:** Applications > Data Integrations > Application Integration at a glance > Reltio Integration for Salesforce (with RIH) at a glance > Reltio Integration for Salesforce (with RIH) Overview


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/data-integrations/application-integration-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-overview/search-before-create-sbc?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs


Learn about the search before create functionality in the Reltio Integration for Salesforce (with RIH).

The Reltio Integration for Salesforce (with RIH) enables you to sync contact and account data between Reltio and Salesforce using prebuilt recipes.

Before you decide to create a record in Salesforce, wouldn't it be beneficial if we could check if the record already exists in Reltio or Salesforce? The Search before create (SBC) feature does exactly that. It first checks for records in both Reltio and Salesforce, and imports the ones that are not available, thus avoiding duplication.

The Search before create is implemented using a set of recipes, which search for account and contact records before importing them from Reltio to Salesforce. For more information, see topic [Recipes for Search before create](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/data-integrations/application-integration-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-overview/search-before-create-sbc/recipes-for-search-before-create?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).

In order to use the recipes for SBC, you must install the Salesforce managed package for SBC. For more information, see topic [Install the Reltio Integration for Salesforce managed package to enable SBC](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/data-integrations/application-integration-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-overview/search-before-create-sbc/install-the-reltio-integration-for-salesforce-managed-package-to-enable-sbc?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs)

# Search account or contact before creating records

> **Section:** Applications > Data Integrations > Application Integration at a glance > Reltio Integration for Salesforce (with RIH) at a glance > Reltio Integration for Salesforce (with RIH) Overview > Search before create (SBC) > Recipes for Search before create


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/data-integrations/application-integration-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-overview/search-before-create-sbc/recipes-for-search-before-create/search-account-or-contact-before-creating-records?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs


Learn more about the recipe to search for accounts and contacts in Salesforce.

## SFDC | API | SBC - Search Account/Contact

This recipe uses a API endpoint, which searches for accounts and contacts in Salesforce and Organization details in the Reltio source system. If the recipe is successful, it returns the search results as an array. If it's not successful, it returns an error code and message.

This is the base API recipe for SBC Search functionality, which is triggered by requests from the API Platform. The input parameters of this recipe are:

- 

  `filter` - the SBC search filter that contains `field:data map`.
- 

  `recordTypeId` - The Salesforce Account or Contact record type identifier.
- 

  `test` - The recipe has to test itself with some fake search data, by calling the underlying systems.
- 

  `options` - Search options such as `searchByOv`, `useContains`, `useFuzzy`, `useOr`
- 

  `max` - The maximum limit of the number of records in the search results, per source system. This value cannot be higher than 100.

For the specified input parameters, this recipe calls the Process sub-recipe to execute the search from Salesforce and Reltio. If the recipe is executed successfully, it returns a list of records. If it is not successful, it returns an error code with a message.



---

# Import account and contact information

> **Section:** Applications > Data Integrations > Application Integration at a glance > Reltio Integration for Salesforce (with RIH) at a glance > Reltio Integration for Salesforce (with RIH) Overview > Search before create (SBC) > Recipes for Search before create


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/data-integrations/application-integration-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-overview/search-before-create-sbc/recipes-for-search-before-create/import-account-and-contact-information?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs


Learn about the recipe to import account and contact information.

## SFDC | API | SBC - Import Account/Contact

This recipe uses a API endpoint to trigger the import of account and contact objects, and their parent objects from Reltio to Salesforce.

This is the base API recipe for the SBC Import functionality, and is triggered by requests from the API Platform. The input parameters of this recipe are:

- 

  `sourceSystem` - The Source of the entity. For example, Reltio.
- 

  `recordTypeId` - The Salesforce Account/Contact record type identifier.
- 

  `test` - Recipe has to test itself with some fake search data, by calling the underlying systems.
- 

  `sourceSystemEntityID` - The Entity ID for the source system. In the case of Reltio, the URI. For examle, `entities/04rIXee`.

This process recipe invokes a subprocess to import data from the Reltio source system into Salesforce, using the given input parameters. If the recipe is successful, it returns information about the imported record and its related records, such as the parent account object. If the recipe fails, it returns an error code along with an error message.



---

# Import process for account and contact information

> **Section:** Applications > Data Integrations > Application Integration at a glance > Reltio Integration for Salesforce (with RIH) at a glance > Reltio Integration for Salesforce (with RIH) Overview > Search before create (SBC) > Recipes for Search before create


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/data-integrations/application-integration-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-overview/search-before-create-sbc/recipes-for-search-before-create/import-process-for-account-and-contact-information?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs


Learn more about the recipe to import process fo account and contact information.

## SFDC | PROC | SBC - Import Process for Account/Contact - Reltio

This recipe uses a API endpoint to trigger the import of account and contact objects, and their parent objects from Reltio to Salesforce.

This process imports data from the Reltio source system into Salesforce, and returns the results. It converts the Reltio entity organization objects into Salesforce account object models, and imports it into the appropriate system. Additionally, this process provides information on dummy import records and conducts a search in Reltio to verify connectivity and the successful execution of each step when you set the input parameter `test` to true.

# Search process for accounts and contacts

> **Section:** Applications > Data Integrations > Application Integration at a glance > Reltio Integration for Salesforce (with RIH) at a glance > Reltio Integration for Salesforce (with RIH) Overview > Search before create (SBC) > Recipes for Search before create


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/data-integrations/application-integration-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-overview/search-before-create-sbc/recipes-for-search-before-create/search-process-for-accounts-and-contacts?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs


Learn more about the recipe to search for account and contact details.

## SFDC | PROC | SBC - Search Process for Account/Contact

This recipe uses API endpoints, which search for accounts and contacts in Salesforce and Organization details in the Reltio source system.

This is a process recipe that performs search in Salesforce and Reltio, and returns the results. It converts the SBC search parameters into a Salesforce SOQL query format as well as a Reltio search parameter format, and searches both systems.

# Search for existing records prior to import

> **Section:** Applications > Data Integrations > Application Integration at a glance > Reltio Integration for Salesforce (with RIH) at a glance > Reltio Integration for Salesforce (with RIH) Overview > Search before create (SBC) > Install the Reltio Integration for Salesforce managed package to enable SBC


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/data-integrations/application-integration-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-overview/search-before-create-sbc/install-the-reltio-integration-for-salesforce-managed-package-to-enable-sbc/search-for-existing-records-prior-to-import?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs


Learn how to search for records before importing records into Salesforce.

Configure the Search before create feature. For more information, see topic [Configure Search before Create](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/data-integrations/application-integration-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-overview/search-before-create-sbc/install-the-reltio-integration-for-salesforce-managed-package-to-enable-sbc/configure-search-before-create?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs)..

The Search Before Create feature does a real-time search against Reltio and Salesforce data before creating a new record. This is to identify duplicate records so that you can determine to update the current record or create a new one.


To search for existing records prior to import:

1. Open the App launcher.
2. Select **Reltio Integration for Salesforce**.
3. Select the **Control Panel** tab.
   *Image: sfdcrih_sfobjects.png*
4. From the **Search objects** tab, select the Salesforce object.
5. Open the list view of the Salesforce object.
6. Select **New**.
   *Image: sfdcrih_searchaccount.PNG*
   In the **Search Account** page, you will see a list of fields that you can use to search for records.
   - To add or remove fields, select the **Configure Search** option on the top right-hand corner of the page.
     *Image: sfdcrih_configuresearch.png*
   - In the **Configure Search Fields** dialog, from the **Selected fields** column, add or remove fields that you want displayed in the **Search account** page. For example, let's remove the **Type** field from the **Selected fields** column.
   - Select **Save**. Navigate back to the Search account page, which now doesn't include the Type field.
7. Enter details in the fields and select **Search** to search for an existing record.
   If the account already exists, you'll see the record details.
8. Select **Preview** to preview the record.
   *Image: sfdcrih_previewrecord.png*
9. Select **Import** to import the record into Salesforce.

# Install the Reltio Integration for Salesforce managed package to enable SBC

> **Section:** Applications > Data Integrations > Application Integration at a glance > Reltio Integration for Salesforce (with RIH) at a glance > Reltio Integration for Salesforce (with RIH) Overview > Search before create (SBC)


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/data-integrations/application-integration-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-overview/search-before-create-sbc/install-the-reltio-integration-for-salesforce-managed-package-to-enable-sbc?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs


Learn how to install the Salesforce managed package of the Salesforce connector.

To be able to use the Search Before Create functionality, you must install the Salesforce managed package.

Before you install the Salesforce managed package, ensure you have the following:- 

  Create a Trailblazer account. You need this to download managed packages from the Saleforce AppExchange.
- 

  Login credentials for Salesforce.

As an administrator, ensure you have access to the [Salesforce AppExchange](https://appexchange.salesforce.com/). You may access Salesforce AppExchange:. You may access Salesforce AppExchange:- 

  From the Setup in your organization, search for **AppExhange** and open the **AppExchange Marketplace**.
- 

  From the **App Launcher**, select the **Visit AppExchange** link from the top right corner of the page.


To install Salesforce Connector:

1. In the **AppExchange Marketplace** page, select **Go to AppExchange** link.
   *Image: sfdcrih_appexchange.png*
2. Select **Go to AppExchange.**
   *Image: sfdcrih_trailblaizeracclogin.png*
3. In the **AppExchange** page, select **Log In** to log into your Trailblazer account.
   *Image: sfdcrih_trailblaizeraccloginmain.png*
4. In the dialog box displayed, select **Continue with Salesforce**.
   *Image: sfdcrih_continuewithsf.png*
   You are logged in using the Trailblazer account credentials.
5. In the **AppExchange** page, in the **Search** box, type **Reltio Integration for Salesforce**.
6. From the list displayed, select **Reltio Integration for Salesforce**.
   *Image: sfdcrih_getsf.png*
7. Select **Get It Now**.
   *Image: sfdcrih_allowaccess.png*
8. Select **Allow** to allow AppExchange to access the Salesforce URL.
   *Image: sfdcrih_installorg.png*
9. In the **Where do you want to install this package** dialog box, in the **Connected Salesforce Accounts** field, select the environment where the package is to be installed.
   > **Note:** We recommend you test the package in a sandbox environment before you install it in your production environment. Select **Install in Sandbox** to test the package.
   *Image: sfdcrih_confirminstall.png*
10. In the **Confirm Installation Details** page, select **Confirm and Install** to install the package.
11. Enter your Salesforce login credentials. You are prompted to select the installation type.
   *Image: sfdcrih_installadmin.png*
12. Select the **Install for Admins Only** option.
13. In the prompts displayed, complete the installation of Reltio Integration for Salesforce.
   > **Note:** This option deploys the package into the Salesforce organization and enables you to proceed with the configuration of the connector.
   Once you are done with the installation, configure remote settings for your environment. For more information, see topic [Configure remote site settings for Salesforce managed package](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/data-integrations/application-integration-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-overview/search-before-create-sbc/install-the-reltio-integration-for-salesforce-managed-package-to-enable-sbc/configure-remote-site-settings-for-salesforce-managed-package?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs). After configuring the remote site settings, launch the Reltio Integration for Salesforce. For more information, see topic [Configure Search before Create](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/data-integrations/application-integration-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-overview/search-before-create-sbc/install-the-reltio-integration-for-salesforce-managed-package-to-enable-sbc/configure-search-before-create?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).

# Activate API collection and generate endpoints

> **Section:** Applications > Data Integrations > Application Integration at a glance > Reltio Integration for Salesforce (with RIH) at a glance > Reltio Integration for Salesforce (with RIH) Overview > Search before create (SBC) > Enable Search Before Create


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/data-integrations/application-integration-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-overview/search-before-create-sbc/enable-search-before-create/activate-api-collection-and-generate-endpoints?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs


Learn how to activate API collection and generate endpoints.

Before activating the API collection, ensure that you've started the recipes required for Search before create (SBC). For more information, see topic [Enable Search Before Create](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/data-integrations/application-integration-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-overview/search-before-create-sbc/enable-search-before-create?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs)..


To activate the API collection and generate endpoints:

1. In the [Reltio Integration Hub](https://console.reltio.com/integration), in your tenant, select **API Platform**.
2. From the list, select **API Collection**.
3. In the **API Collection** page, select **SFDC-SBC**.
   *Image: sfdcrih_activateendpoints.png*
4. For allendpoints, from the more options menu, select **Activate endpoint**.
   The endpoints are now activated.
5. Select an endpoint to view its details.
   *Image: sfdcrih_endpointcopyurl.png*
6. In the right pane, select **Copy URL** to copy the Endpoint URl, which is used during the SFDC MP configuration.

After activating the API collection and generating endpoints, create an API client and generate a security code. For more information, see [Create API client and generate security code](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/data-integrations/application-integration-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-overview/search-before-create-sbc/enable-search-before-create/create-api-client-and-generate-security-code?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs)..

# Create API client and generate security code

> **Section:** Applications > Data Integrations > Application Integration at a glance > Reltio Integration for Salesforce (with RIH) at a glance > Reltio Integration for Salesforce (with RIH) Overview > Search before create (SBC) > Enable Search Before Create


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/data-integrations/application-integration-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-overview/search-before-create-sbc/enable-search-before-create/create-api-client-and-generate-security-code?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs


Learn how to create an API client and generate the security code.

Ensure all prerequisites are taken care of and that you've started the recipes required for Search before create (SBC). For more information, see topic [Enable Search Before Create](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/data-integrations/application-integration-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-overview/search-before-create-sbc/enable-search-before-create?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs)..

During synchronization, an authorization token is required to call the RIH API endpoints from the Salesforce-Reltio managed package in order to guarantee a secure connection.


To create an API client and generate the security code:

1. In the **Reltio Integration Hub** (RIH), select **API Platform**.
2. Select **Clients** > **Add new client**.
3. In the Name field, enter **SBC MP Client**.
4. Select **Create New Access Profile**.
5. In the **Name** field, enter **SBC MP Client Profile**.
6. In the **API Collections to Include** field, select **SFDC-SBC**.
7. In the **Authentication Mode** field, select **Auth Token**.
8. Ensure the **Policy** field is empty.
   > **Caution:** Policy configuration is not required for this setup. If a policy is configured, it can restrict API request access based on the defined policy rules.
9. Select **Next**.
   The API client is created.
10. Select the **API keys** tab.
11. Click **Create API key**.
12. Enter a name in the **API Key Name** field.
13. Ensure the **Allowed IPs** and **Blocked IPs** fields are empty.
   > **Caution:** IP restrictions are not required for this setup. If values are configured, API access is limited according to the specified IP rules.
14. Copy the Auth Token (i.e. Security Code) for the SFDC MP configuration.

# Example - Add new field for Salesforce in Search

> **Section:** Applications > Data Integrations > Application Integration at a glance > Reltio Integration for Salesforce (with RIH) at a glance > Reltio Integration for Salesforce (with RIH) Overview > Search before create (SBC) > Recipes for Search before create


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/data-integrations/application-integration-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-overview/search-before-create-sbc/recipes-for-search-before-create/example---add-new-field-for-salesforce-in-search?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs


Learn how to add a new field in SBC recipe.


To add a new Salesforce field in Search:

1. Log into your Salesforce account.
2. Navigate to **SFDC** > **Search Before Create** > **2-Process**.
3. Select the **SFDC | PROC | SBC - Search Process for Account - Reltio and Salesforce** recipe
4. Select Step 2.
   *Image: sfdcrih_sbcrecipeexample.png*
5. In the right pane, under the **List item schema** section, select **Add field**.
6. Add details of the new Salesforce field, and make it optional.
7. Select Step 11.
   *Image: sfdcrih_sbcrecipeexampleone.png*
8. In the right pane, under the **Fields to retrieve** section, add the new Salesforce account.
9. Select Step 15.
   *Image: sfdcrih_sbcrecipeexampletwo.png*
10. In the right pane, in the New account field, select the optional field you created.
11. Select Step 17.
   *Image: sfdcrih_sbcrecipeexamplethree.png*
12. Add mapping from Salesforce to Reltio as shown above.
13. Select Step 23.
   *Image: sfdcrih_sbcrecipeexamplefour.png*
14. In the right pane, under the **Output fields** section, select **Add field** and add the new Salesforce account field.
15. In the right pane, under the Code section, add this code:
   ```
let accountNewField = obj.attributes.NewOrganizationField && obj.attributes.NewOrganizationField.length > 0 ? obj.attributes.NewOrganizationField[0].value : "";
   ```
16. Additionally, add this code:
   ```
if(accountNewField!== undefined && accountNewField !== null) { salesforceObject.NewOrganizationField = accountNewField; }
   ```
17. Select Step 24.
   *Image: sfdcrih_sbcrecipeexamplefive.png*
18. In the **New account** field, add the newly created Salesforce field.

# Configure Search before Create

> **Section:** Applications > Data Integrations > Application Integration at a glance > Reltio Integration for Salesforce (with RIH) at a glance > Reltio Integration for Salesforce (with RIH) Overview > Search before create (SBC) > Install the Reltio Integration for Salesforce managed package to enable SBC


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/data-integrations/application-integration-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-overview/search-before-create-sbc/install-the-reltio-integration-for-salesforce-managed-package-to-enable-sbc/configure-search-before-create?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs


Learn how to configure search before create in Salesforce.

To configure search before create, you must first install the managed package and configure remote site settings. For more information, see topics [Install the Reltio Integration for Salesforce managed package to enable SBC](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/data-integrations/application-integration-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-overview/search-before-create-sbc/install-the-reltio-integration-for-salesforce-managed-package-to-enable-sbc?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs) and and [Configure remote site settings for Salesforce managed package](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/data-integrations/application-integration-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-overview/search-before-create-sbc/install-the-reltio-integration-for-salesforce-managed-package-to-enable-sbc/configure-remote-site-settings-for-salesforce-managed-package?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs)..

The Search Before Create feature in the Reltio Integration for Salesforce (with RIH) helps you prevent duplicate records and keep your data clean. It performs a real-time search across both Reltio and Salesforce before creating a new record, ensuring you don't add duplicates. If a match is found, you can choose to update an existing record or create a new one. This feature is built into the Reltio-managed package for Salesforce and integrates seamlessly with Lightning Components. Once configured, it overrides the standard New button, letting you search and validate data without leaving Salesforce.


Follow the below steps to configure search before create in Salesforce:

1. Open the App launcher.
2. Select **Reltio Integration for Salesforce**.
3. Select the **Control Panel** tab.
   *Image: sfdcrih_sfcontrolpanel.png*
4. Select the **+NEW** option.
   *Image: sfdcrih_configsbc.png*
5. From the **Object** dropdown list, select the object.
6. In the **Endpoints** field, specify the **Import** and **Search** endpoints. This denotes the endpoints where Salesforce must send API calls when querying existing records or import new data. For more information, see topic [Activate API collection and generate endpoints](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/data-integrations/application-integration-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-overview/search-before-create-sbc/enable-search-before-create/activate-api-collection-and-generate-endpoints?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).
7. In the **Security code** field, enter the code required to call the endpoints from Salesforce-Reltio managed package. For more information, see topic [Create API client and generate security code](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/data-integrations/application-integration-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-overview/search-before-create-sbc/enable-search-before-create/create-api-client-and-generate-security-code?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).
8. In the **Input fields** section, select the fields from the list of available fields.
9. Select **Test**. You will see the configured object in the **Search Objects** tab.
   *Image: sfdcrih_sfobjects.png*
10. Go to **Setup** > **Object Manager**.
11. Select the newly added object.
   *Image: sfdcrih_setupobjectmanager.png*
12. From the left pane, select **Buttons, Links, and Actions**.
   *Image: sfdcrih_overrideprop.png*
13. Override the New button. For example, for the **Lightning Component Override** and the **Mobile Override** in the **Lightning component** dropdown, select `rihsbc:SbcObjectFormComponent`.
14. Select Save to save the object details.
   You can now use this object to search for records before importing them into Salesforce. For more information, see topic [Search for existing records prior to import](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/data-integrations/application-integration-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-overview/search-before-create-sbc/install-the-reltio-integration-for-salesforce-managed-package-to-enable-sbc/search-for-existing-records-prior-to-import?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).

Learn how to configure remote settings for Salesforce.

Make sure you have installed the Reltio Integration for Salesforce connector in your environment. For more information, see topic [Install the Reltio Integration for Salesforce managed package to enable SBC](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/data-integrations/application-integration-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-overview/search-before-create-sbc/install-the-reltio-integration-for-salesforce-managed-package-to-enable-sbc?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs)..


To configure remote site settings:

1. In the Salesforce Org, select **Setup** > **Security** > **Remote Site settings**.
2. In the **Uniform Resource Identifier** field, add the URI for the configuration. For example, add the URI for Workato, which would be https://apim.workato.com.
3. Give access to the URIs.
4. Select Save.
   > **Note:** If you are an administrator and you want to set permissions for non-admin users, go to **User** > **Permissions** > **Set Assignment** > **Edit Assignments**. Select the **RIH SBC Other Users** option and save the changes.

# Reltio Integration for Salesforce (with RIH) at a glance

> **Section:** Applications > Data Integrations > Application Integration at a glance


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/data-integrations/application-integration-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-at-a-glance?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs


Get a high-level view of Reltio Integration for Salesforce (with RIH).

## What is Reltio Integration for Salesforce (with RIH)?

Reltio Integration for Salesforce (with RIH) provides prebuilt Reltio Integration Hub recipes with out-of-the-box mapping setups related to Reltio's B2B and Healthcare velocity packs.

## Who is Reltio Integration for Salesforce (with RIH) for?

This content is curated for these Reltio user roles defined in topic [About roles](https://docs.reltio.com/en/roles/about-roles?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs):

Data Product OwnerDeveloperReltio ConfiguratorSolution Architect

## Why would I use Reltio Integration for Salesforce (with RIH)?

By integrating with the Reltio Context Intelligence Platform, you acquire data that is cleansed and consolidated from various sources into a golden record.

## When would I use Reltio Integration for Salesforce (with RIH)?

Use this integration when you need to sync and maintain the latest data related to your contacts and accounts in Salesforce with your data in your Reltio tenant.

## Where do I find Reltio Integration for Salesforce (with RIH)?

Reltio Integration for Salesforce (with RIH) are available from Reltio Integration Hub. Access RIH from **Applications > Integration Hub**.

# Operational Guidelines

> **Section:** Applications > Data Integrations > Application Integration at a glance > Reltio Integration for Salesforce (with RIH) at a glance > Reltio Integration for Salesforce (with RIH) Overview


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/data-integrations/application-integration-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-overview/operational-guidelines?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs


Learn more about the design considerations for handling errors and large entity payloads.

In this topic, know more about how errors are handled, how to retrieve the latest data from the Reltio platform, and the locking mechanism for events.

## Error handling

When a recipe job fails due to an application or data error, it's marked as failed. The error details are passed to the `SFDC | FUNC | Error Handler` recipe, which logs a message to the centralized RIH logging tool by default and sends an email notification. To ensure this works effectively, we recommend you change or extend this logic to align with your error handling or alerting requirements.

The related recipe jobs table contains the required metadata for search. Here's a sample table:

*Image: sfdcrih_errorhandlertable.png*

## Retrieving the latest entity payload from Reltio platform

Events processed and delivered to the SNS topic or SQS queue aren't always delivered in order. Sometimes, older messages arrive after newer ones. To make sure you're working with the latest data from the Reltio platform, set `SFDC_GetNewPayloadFromReltio` to `true`.

## Dealing with large entities or objects

If an entity payload is bigger than the maximum size supported by streaming queues, the Reltio platform sends the attribute `exceededQueueSizeLimit: true` without including the entity payload. In such cases, the RIH SFDC recipes must retrieve a fresh copy of the entity payload from the Reltio platform.

To support large entities and objects, we recommend you update your tenant's physical configuration with:

```
"streamingConfig": {
"streamingEnabled": true,
"streamingAPIEnabled": true,
"analyzeOvChanges": false,
"emptyStartEndRelationCrosswalks": false,
"largeObjectsSupport": true,
```

## Locking mechanisms for events with Salesforce crosswalks

When processing events from Reltio to Salesforce in parallel, a locking mechanism prevents duplicate entries when entities lack a Salesforce crosswalk. This occurs when you have an LCA that causes more than one event to be generated at the same time or are faced with a significant load in the system that delays the process.

How the locking mechanism works:

1. 

   Recipe checks for the Salesforce crosswalk.
   1. If present, processes the job as an update to the Salesforce object.
   2. If not present, verifies the RIH Lookup Table `SFDC_LockedEntities`. If the entity URI isn't present in the lookup table, inserts the following data to the lookup table

1. 

   Entity URI
2. 

   Start time, which is the current time
3. 

   End time, which is Start time +8 seconds
   3. After data is inserted into the lookup table, the job is processed as a new Salesforce object created.
   4. After the callback to Reltio, the entry is deleted from the lookup table.
2. 

   If the Salesforce crosswalk isn't present for the entity, find the entity in the lookup table.
   1. If the entity is present in the lookup table and the end time is still valid, pause the recipe for 8 or less seconds and set the `isWait` to `true`.
3. 

   When the `isWait=true`, then do the following:
   1. Retrieve the entity payload from Reltio.
   2. Obtain the Salesforce Crosswalk.

1. 

   If Salesforce Crosswalk is present, process the job as an update to the Salesforce object.
2. 

   If Salesforce Crosswalk is't present, throw an exception error.

# Reltio Integration for Salesforce (with RIH) Overview

> **Section:** Applications > Data Integrations > Application Integration at a glance > Reltio Integration for Salesforce (with RIH) at a glance


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/data-integrations/application-integration-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-overview?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs


Learn about the Reltio Integration for Salesforce (with RIH)

Reltio Integration for Salesforce with Reltio Integration Hub (RIH) enables you to sync and maintain the latest data related to your contacts and accounts in Salesforce. By integrating with the Reltio Context Intelligence Platform, you acquire data that is cleansed and consolidated from various sources into a golden record.

Reltio Integration for Salesforce (with RIH) differs from the legacy [Reltio Integration for Salesforce](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/data-integrations/application-integration-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-set-up?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs) by providing enhanced alerting, monitoring, troubleshooting, and self-service capabilities through the Reltio Integration Hub (RIH).

## Data Synchronization Architecture

Reltio Integration Hub (RIH) supports bidirectional data synchronization between Reltio and Salesforce.

**Data synchronization from Reltio to Salesforce**

The following diagrams illustrate the flow of data from Reltio to Salesforce through Reltio Integration Hub (RIH).

*Image: i-salesforce-to-reltio.png*

Key characteristics of data synchronization from Reltio to Salesforce include: 

- Trigger through Amazon SNS (real time) and SQS (near real time) for Reltio change events
- Push-based delivery from Reltio to RIH recipes without polling
- Best-effort event ordering and single-event processing per recipe job
- Recipe concurrency of up to 5 jobs per entity type
- Recipe-based delivery of the final payload to Salesforce objects

**Data synchronization from Salesforce to Reltio**

The following diagram illustrates the flow of data from Salesforce to Reltio through Reltio Integration Hub (RIH).

*Image: i-rih-salesforce-outbound.png*

Key characteristics of data synchronization from Salesforce to Reltio include:

- Salesforce changes are notified through outbound messages, with backup polling every 6 hours to recover missed events and ensure that RIH creates any required jobs if a notification is not received.
- RIH recipes handle the outbound message and keep the Reltio system in sync with Salesforce.
- Optionally, the integration performs a write-back to update the Reltio URI in the external ID field of the originating Salesforce record, so that both systems maintain a consistent cross-reference.

## Key Features

The Reltio Integration Hub uses Salesforce Data Connector (SFDC) recipes and includes the following features:

- Prebuilt recipes for the Reltio B2B Velocity Pack and Reltio Healthcare Velocity Pack that integrate with Salesforce objects.
- Bi-directional sync of account and contact data.
- Configuration to map objects and fields between Salesforce and Reltio.
- Extensive monitoring and troubleshooting through transparent RIH dashboards and configurable alerts in recipes.
- Ability to create new integration from the prebuilt recipes for expanded use cases.
- Search for records before creating them, and import the records not available into Salesforce.

## Next Steps

To complete the integration setup, perform the following tasks:

- **Configure bidirectional synchronization**: Use the RIH recipes to synchronize data between Reltio and Salesforce. For more information, see:
  - [Prebuilt integration for Salesforce with RIH](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/data-integrations/application-integration-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-overview/prebuilt-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs)
  - [Synchronization modes](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/data-integrations/application-integration-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-overview/synchronization-modes?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs)
  - [Get started with Reltio Integration for Salesforce (with RIH)](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/data-integrations/application-integration-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-overview/get-started-with-reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs)
  - [RIH recipes for Salesforce Integration](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/data-integrations/application-integration-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-overview/rih-recipes-for-salesforce-integration?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs)
- **Enable Search Before Create**: Use the Salesforce managed package to enable the [Search before create (SBC)](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/data-integrations/application-integration-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-overview/search-before-create-sbc?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs) feature.

To deploy the recipes in your RIH account in your Dev tenant, contact your Reltio CSM. For more information, see [Get help in Support Portal](https://docs.reltio.com/en/reltio/whats-in-the-box/whats-in-the-box-at-a-glance/technical-assistance-at-a-glance/technical-assistance-operations/get-help-in-support-portal?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).

When new updates are available, we'll send notifications. Note that the prebuilt integration is not automatically upgraded, so please request access to the latest version of the prebuilt integration package. Once you receive the latest version, do one of the following:

# Batch synchronization from Reltio to Salesforce

> **Section:** Applications > Data Integrations > Application Integration at a glance > Reltio Integration for Salesforce (with RIH) at a glance > Reltio Integration for Salesforce (with RIH) Overview > RIH recipes for Salesforce Integration


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/data-integrations/application-integration-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-overview/rih-recipes-for-salesforce-integration/batch-synchronization-from-reltio-to-salesforce?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs


Learn about the batch sync from Reltio to Salesforce.

Use batch synchronization to extract, transform, and load data from one application to another using recipes with batch triggers. It follows a multiple transaction approach, handling a batch of entities for one job. We recommend this mode for initial migrations or high-volume data updates in a short period.

The basic recipe calls the `export entity from reltio` sub recipe to export entities as below.

- 

  Entities with Salesforce crosswalk to update the SFDC account object
- 

  Entities without salesforce crosswalk to create new SFDC account object

The basic recipe also calls `export relationship from reltio` sub recipe to export relationships with Salesforce crosswalk. The process also synchronizes with Salesforce in batch.

If the recipe is unsuccessful, the `Error Handler` recipe is executed.

## Error handler

The error handling is reduced to sending failed records in a JSON format to a specified mail. You can also implement your own error handling method. For example, a queue of sending failed records and subsequent processing or configure downloading failed records to an FTP server for processing.

## Connections

You must ensure the following connections are available for the recipes to work:

- 

  Connection to your Salesforce account, from where the base recipe receives events.
- 

  Connecting to your Reltio tenant, which the synchronization recipe uses to synchronize data.

# Batch synchronization from Salesforce to Reltio

> **Section:** Applications > Data Integrations > Application Integration at a glance > Reltio Integration for Salesforce (with RIH) at a glance > Reltio Integration for Salesforce (with RIH) Overview > RIH recipes for Salesforce Integration


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/data-integrations/application-integration-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-overview/rih-recipes-for-salesforce-integration/batch-synchronization-from-salesforce-to-reltio?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs


Learn about the batch sync from Salesforce to Reltio

Use batch synchronization to extract, transform, and load data from one application to another using recipes with batch triggers. It follows a multiple transaction approach, handling a batch of entities in one job. We recommend this mode for initial migrations or high-volume data updates in a short period.

Synchronization of account details occurs in the basic recipe through the Reltio connector. Only Salesforce Accounts are used for synchronization. If at least one record (Account) is not synchronized, the recipe will be considered as failed.

Synchronization of Relationships between Organizations or between HCO is done through a separate basic recipe. This recipe receives all accounts with Relationships from Salesforce and creates new Relationships between organizations.

> **Note:** If the organization already has the Relationship between the two Organizations or between two HCOs, the Relationship will not be created, an error occurs, and the recipe will not be successful.

## Failed events and event handler

If the Reltio connector cannot synchronize data, i.e. if at least one record is executed unsuccessfully, the recipe selects the failed records and sends them to the `SFDC to Reltio - Error Handler` sub recipe for further processing of these records.

The `SFDC to Reltio - Error Handler` sub recipe accepts two arguments: an email address and an array of failed records. When calling this recipe, it translates the received records into JSON format and sends them to the specified email. The message body contains the number of failed records, as well as the error of the first record and the last one. The attachment contains the JSON itself with an array of failed records and an error message for each record.

## Connections

You must ensure the following connections are available for the recipes to work:

- 

  Connection to your Salesforce account, from where the base recipe receives events.
- 

  Connecting to your Reltio tenant, which the synchronization recipe uses to synchronize data.

# Real-time synchronization from Reltio to Salesforce

> **Section:** Applications > Data Integrations > Application Integration at a glance > Reltio Integration for Salesforce (with RIH) at a glance > Reltio Integration for Salesforce (with RIH) Overview > RIH recipes for Salesforce Integration


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/data-integrations/application-integration-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-overview/rih-recipes-for-salesforce-integration/real-time-synchronization-from-reltio-to-salesforce?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs


Learn about the recipes that synchronize data in real-time from Reltio to Salesforce.

During integration, real-time synchronization follows a single transition approach, meaning one event, one recipe job. These recipes use Amazon SQS real-time triggers to start the process. This trigger is based on webhooks, which enable real-time response for the integration to take place after the data is changed in the Reltio platform. To achieve this, ensure recipes are always enabled, so RIH does not miss any events.

The main trigger of the basic recipes is Amazon SQS. SQS triggers the recipe as soon as a message is published to the selected external SQS queue in the Reltio tenant. These recipes receive different types of Reltio entity event messages, processing them to create, update, delete, and merge Salesforce Account objects.

## Recipes for B2B

Use the following recipes to sync data from Reltio to Salesforce in real-time for B2B:

- 

  Trigger recipes: These simple recipes for each event/object use the AWS SQS connector trigger that initiates the PROC recipes.
  - SFDC | TRG | Real Time Sync from Reltio to Salesforce - Organization
  - SFDC | TRG | Real Time Sync from Reltio to Salesforce - Individual
  - SFDC | TRG | Real Time Sync from Reltio to Salesforce - OrganizationIndividual Relation
  - SFDC | TRG | Real Time Sync from Reltio to Salesforce - OrganizationAffiliation Relation
  - SFDC | TRG | SQS Queue Sync from Reltio to Salesforce
- 

  Process recipes: These recipes handle the orchestration and business logic required to deal with each event or object, in turn calling other PROC or SYS recipes
  - SFDC | PROC | Upsert Process for Salesforce Object and Callback to Reltio - Account
  - SFDC | PROC | Upsert Process for Salesforce Object and Callback to Reltio - Contact
  - SFDC | PROC | Upsert Process for Salesforce Objects - OrganizationIndividual Relation
  - SFDC | PROC | Merge Process for Salesforce Objects - Contact
  - SFDC | PROC | Delete Process for Salesforce Object - Contact
  - SFDC | PROC | Remove Process for Salesforce Object - Contact Account Relation
  - SFDC | PROC | Delete Process for Salesforce Object - Account
  - SFDC | PROC | Upsert Process for Salesforce Objects - Parent Account Relation
  - SFDC | PROC | Merge Process for Salesforce Objects - Account
  - SFDC | PROC | Remove Process for Salesforce Object - Parent Account Relation
- 

  System recipes: These recipes handle the mapping and API calls to the SFDC system
  - SFDC | SYS | Get Master and Child Salesforce Object IDs for Reltio Entity
  - SFDC | SYS | Upsert Salesforce Objects - Contact
  - SFDC | SYS | Upsert Salesforce Objects - Account
  - SFDC | SYS | Merge Salesforce Objects - Account
  - SFDC | SYS | Merge Salesforce Objects - Contact
  - SFDC | SYS | Upsert Salesforce Object - Contact Account Relation
  - SFDC | SYS | Upsert Salesforce Object - Parent Account Relation
  - SFDC | SYS | Delete Salesforce Objects - Account
  - SFDC | SYS | Delete Salesforce Objects - Contact
- 

  Function recipes: These recipes are used in the synchronization process.
  - SFDC | FUNC | De-normalize Fields From Reltio Entity

## Recipes for Healthcare

Use the following recipes to sync data from Reltio to Salesforce in real-time for Healthcare:

- 

  Trigger recipes: These simple recipes for each event/object use the AWS SQS connector trigger that initiates the PROC recipes.
  - SFDC | TRG | Real Time Sync from Reltio to Salesforce - HCO
  - SFDC | TRG | Real Time Sync from Reltio to Salesforce - HCP
  - SFDC | TRG | Real Time Sync from Reltio to Salesforce - HCPisAffiliatedWithHCO Relation
  - SFDC | TRG | Real Time Sync from Reltio to Salesforce - OrganizationAffiliation Relation
  - SFDC | TRG | SQS Queue Sync from Reltio to Salesforce
- 

  Process recipes: These recipes handle the orchestration and business logic required to deal with each event or object, in turn calling other PROC or SYS recipes
  - SFDC | PROC | Upsert Process for Salesforce Object and Callback to Reltio - Account
  - SFDC | PROC | Upsert Process for Salesforce Object and Callback to Reltio - Contact
  - SFDC | PROC | Upsert Process for Salesforce Objects - HCPisAffiliatedWithHCO Relation
  - SFDC | PROC | Merge Process for Salesforce Objects - Contact
  - SFDC | PROC | Delete Process for Salesforce Object - Contact
  - SFDC | PROC | Remove Process for Salesforce Object - Contact Account Relation
  - SFDC | PROC | Delete Process for Salesforce Object - Account
  - SFDC | PROC | Upsert Process for Salesforce Objects - Parent Account Relation
  - SFDC | PROC | Merge Process for Salesforce Objects - Account
  - SFDC | PROC | Remove Process for Salesforce Object - Parent Account Relation
- 

  System recipes: These recipes handle the mapping and API calls to the SFDC system
  - SFDC | SYS | Get Master and Child Salesforce Object IDs for Reltio Entity
  - SFDC | SYS | Upsert Salesforce Objects - Contact
  - SFDC | SYS | Upsert Salesforce Objects - Account
  - SFDC | SYS | Merge Salesforce Objects - Account
  - SFDC | SYS | Merge Salesforce Objects - Contact
  - SFDC | SYS | Upsert Salesforce Object - Contact Account Relation
  - SFDC | SYS | Upsert Salesforce Object - Parent Account Relation
  - SFDC | SYS | Delete Salesforce Objects - Account
  - SFDC | SYS | Delete Salesforce Objects - Contact
- 

  Function recipes: These recipes are used in the synchronization process.
  - SFDC | FUNC | De-normalize Fields From Reltio Entity

## Dependencies

Here's a list of components that the recipes are dependent on:

**Connections**

- 

  Connection to Amazon SQS. When you configure Reltio tenant for Amazon SQSand add an external queue, select Payload type as Snapshot - selected fields. Select all **attributes**, **crosswalks**, **endObject**, **startObject**, **updateBy**, **createdBy**, **type**, and **uri**. Add the SQS queue in AWS and use the same queue name in the Reltio tenant configuration.
- 

  Connection to Reltio tenant.
- 

  Connection to Salesforce from RIH.
- 

  Connection to Salesforce using credentials - Ensure you have a standard user ID and password to use in Salesforce calls. Update the following environment properties with actual credentials:
  - `SFDC_SalesForcesUserId` - The user id for Salesforce SOAP calls. For example, "myusername".
  - `SFDC_SalesforceSecurityId` - The password for Salesforce SOAP calls. This password is usually made up of your password and the Salesforce security token. For example, "mypassSecurityToken".

**Function Recipes for B2B and Healthcare**

- SYS | Merge Salesforce Objects - Account
- SYS | Upsert Salesforce Objects - Account
- SYS | Remove Parent ID Field From Salesforce Object - Account
- SYS | Remove Parent ID Field From Salesforce Object - Account
- SYS | Delete Salesforce Objects - Account
- FUNC | De-normalize Fields From Reltio Entity
- SYS | Get Master and Child Salesforce Object IDs for Reltio Entity
- FUNC | Get Salesforce IDs From Reltio Entity Crosswalks
- SFDC | SYS | Upsert Salesforce Objects - Contact
- SFDC | SYS | Remove Account Id Field From Salesforce Object - Contact
- SFDC | SYS | Merge Salesforce Objects - Contact
- SFDC | SYS | Delete Salesforce Objects - Contact
- FUNC | De-normalize Fields From Reltio Entity
- SYS | Get Master and Child Salesforce Object IDs for Reltio Entity
- FUNC | Get Salesforce IDs From Reltio Entity Crosswalks

**Custom Field**

You must add a "ext_id" custom string field to the Salesforce **Contact** and **Account** objects on both B2B and Healthcare to successfully execute the batch recipes.

> **Section:** Applications > Data Integrations > Application Integration at a glance > Reltio Integration for Salesforce (with RIH) at a glance > Reltio Integration for Salesforce (with RIH) Overview > RIH recipes for Salesforce Integration

Learn about the recipes used to synchronize data from Salesforce to Reltio.

These recipes use Salesforce real-time triggers to start the synchronization process from SFDC to Reltio. This process follows a single transaction approach, i.e. one event, one recipe job. This trigger is based on webhooks, which enable real-time response for the integration to take place after the data is changed in the Salesforce organization.

The main trigger of the basic recipe is new or updated event messages in Salesforce. An event where a new account is created or updated immediately activates this trigger, and it automatically retrieves jobs that have been missed if the recipe is stopped when restarted.

## Recipes for B2B

  - SFDC | TRG | Sync from Salesforce to Reltio - Account Delete
- 

  Process recipes: These recipes handle the orchestration and business logic required to deal with each object or event, in turn calling other PROC or SYS recipes.
  - SFDC | PROC | Upsert Process for Reltio Entity - Individual and OrganizationIndividual
  - SFDC | PROC | Delete Process for Reltio Entity - Individual and OrganizationIndividual

  - SFDC | PROC | Handle Process for Reltio Relations - OrganizationAffilliation and OrganizationIndividual
- 

  System recipes: These recipes handle the mapping and API calls to the Reltio system

  - SFDC | SYS | Upsert Reltio Relation - OrganizationAffiliation
  - SFDC | SYS | Terminate Reltio Entity or Reltio Relation
- 

  Function recipes: These recipes are used in the synchronization process.
  - SFDC | FUNC | Get Address And Phone From Salesforce Object

## Recipes for Healthcare

Use the following recipes to sync data from Salesforce to Reltio in real-time for Healthcare:

- 

  Trigger recipes: These recipes for each event or object use Salesforce Connector triggers to initiate PROC recipes.
  - SFDC | TRG | Real Time Sync from Salesforce to Reltio - Contact Upsert
  - SFDC | TRG | Real Time Sync from Salesforce to Reltio - Account Upsert

# RIH recipes for Salesforce Integration

> **Section:** Applications > Data Integrations > Application Integration at a glance > Reltio Integration for Salesforce (with RIH) at a glance > Reltio Integration for Salesforce (with RIH) Overview


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/data-integrations/application-integration-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-overview/rih-recipes-for-salesforce-integration?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs


Learn about the RIH recipes used for integration between Reltio and Salesforce.

Reltio Integration for Salesforce (with RIH) is available in the Reltio Integration Hub. This integration has prebuilt recipes that help sync account and contact data between Reltio and Salesforce. Sync the data using one of the 2 modes - Real-time and ELT/Batch. For more information, see topic [Synchronization modes](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/data-integrations/application-integration-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-overview/synchronization-modes?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).

Take a look at the recipes used to sync data from and to Salesforce and Reltio, in Real-time and Batch.

# Batch Dispatch with near real-time synchronization

> **Section:** Applications > Data Integrations > Application Integration at a glance > Reltio Integration for Salesforce (with RIH) at a glance > Reltio Integration for Salesforce (with RIH) Overview > RIH recipes for Salesforce Integration


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/data-integrations/application-integration-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-overview/rih-recipes-for-salesforce-integration/batch-dispatch-with-near-real-time-synchronization?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs


Learn about the near real-time synchronization data from Reltio to Salesforce.

Use batch dispatch with near real-time synchronization to start the synchronization process from Salesforce to Reltio following a batch transaction approach, handling multiple events per job.

## Failed events and event handler

If Reltio cannot synchronize data, i.e. if at least one record is executed unsuccessfully, the recipe selects the failed records and sends them to the `SFDC to Reltio - Error Handler` sub recipe for further processing of these records.

The `SFDC to Reltio - Error Handler` sub recipe accepts two arguments: an email address and an array of failed records. When calling this recipe, it translates the received records into JSON format and sends them to the specified email. The message body contains the number of failed records, as well as the error of the first record and the last one. The attachment contains the JSON itself with an array of failed records and an error message for each record.

## Connections

You must ensure the following connections are available for the recipes to work:

- 

  Connection to your Salesforce account, from where the base recipe receives events.
- 

  Connecting to your Reltio tenant, which the synchronization recipe uses to synchronize data.

# Prerequisites for installing Reltio Integration for Salesforce (with RIH)

> **Section:** Applications > Data Integrations > Application Integration at a glance > Reltio Integration for Salesforce (with RIH) at a glance > Reltio Integration for Salesforce (with RIH) Overview > Get started with Reltio Integration for Salesforce (with RIH)


**Source:** https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/data-integrations/application-integration-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-overview/get-started-with-reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih/prerequisites-for-installing-reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs


Learn about what you need to do before you install Reltio Integration for Salesforce (with RIH).

Reltio Integration for Salesforce (with RIH) uses prebuilt recipes to help sync data between Reltio and Salesforce. For more information, see topic [Prebuilt integration for Salesforce with RIH](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/data-integrations/application-integration-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-overview/prebuilt-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).

The sub topics in this section explain how to prepare the underlying systems before you install RIH recipe:

**Prerequisites - Amazon Web Services**

This prebuilt integration uses the SNS or SQS service of the Amazon Web Services (AWS) to determine the changes or updates done by Reltio platform and then trigger the synchronization to Salesforce. You need these AWS prerequisites: 

- 

  AWS Security configuration. For more information, see topic [Prerequisites - AWS security configuration](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/data-integrations/application-integration-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-overview/get-started-with-reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih/prerequisites-for-installing-reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih/prerequisites---aws-security-configuration?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).
- 

  AWS Event streaming - SNS topic/SQS Queue configuration. For more information, see topic [Prerequisites - AWS event streaming](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/data-integrations/application-integration-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-overview/get-started-with-reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih/prerequisites-for-installing-reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih/prerequisites---aws-event-streaming?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).

**Prerequisites - Reltio Platform**

You need these Reltio Context Intelligence Platform prerequisites: 

- 

  The B2B velocity pack or the Healthcare velocity pack deployed in the Reltio tenant.
- 

  A Reltio service account user. The RIH recipes need a dedicated Service Account User or API ID/secret to call the Reltio Platform API. The service account user must be assigned the ROLE_API for the corresponding tenant. For more information, see topic [ROLE_API Access permissions](https://docs.reltio.com/en/objectives/administer-system/system-administration-at-a-glance/access-management-at-a-glance/access-management-reference/authorization/system-roles/critical-high-privilege-roles/role_api-access-permissions?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).
- 

  Reltio Tenant Management configured to stream specific events to the previously created AWS SNS topic or SQS queue. For more information, see topic [Configure Reltio Tenant Management](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/data-integrations/application-integration-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-overview/get-started-with-reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih/prerequisites-for-installing-reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih/configure-reltio-tenant-management?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).

**Prerequisites - Salesforce**

In Reltio Integration for Salesforce, ensure the following are available: 

- 

  A Salesforce Organization with the default data model. The default account and contact object is used by the RIH recipes.
- 

  A Salesforce Service Account Profile. This service account must have a specific set of permissions to be able to run related Salesforce services.
- 

  Salesforce Object Field permission. All objects used here must have read/write permission for all the used fields.
- 

  Salesforce Service Account User. RIH recipes need a dedicated service account user to use the Salesforce services. This user must be associated with the RIH Service Account profile previously created.

For more information, see topic [Configure Salesforce model and user accounts](https://docs.reltio.com/en/applications/data-integrations/application-integration-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-at-a-glance/reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih-overview/get-started-with-reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih/prerequisites-for-installing-reltio-integration-for-salesforce-with-rih/configure-salesforce-model-and-user-accounts?utm_source=ai-corpus&utm_medium=markdown&utm_campaign=reltio-ai-ready-docs).
